reviewers.overall_notes:
I reviewed all 21 cards in batch_01 in the All pitchers, vs RHP and vs LHP views. I checked the claims against the UNDERLYING DATA and against step 17's code (scripts/17_build_player_cards.py: fallback_line, framing_line, keep_line, contact_line, spread_line, productive_line) and the template (scripts/templates/player_cards.html: zones() draws markers from leaks.all only; aside() renumbers hand leaks and appends coach_note on every view). Scratch checks are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-samsullivan-Desktop-Personal-Projects-Baseball-Chase-Leaderboard/d455bc39-e405-4b67-b2e8-fa1ecc7f61ad/scratchpad/audit/b01/checks.py.

Most findings come from one root cause: the hand tabs are only partly rebuilt.
- framing_line, contact_line/contact_clause and keep_line's fastball clause read all-pitchers summary numbers.
- spread_line and fallback_line read the hand table.
- The coach's note, picture markers and selected picture never change with the tab.
- The leak list and plan tags are renumbered per hand.
This produces sign contradictions (Abreu vs RHP '+1.1' over a −1.1 table; Edman vs LHP '+0.5' over −1.9), contact lines that the tab's own table refutes (Edman vs RHP, Conine vs LHP), coach notes describing another plan (Martínez, Moniak), and leak tags that point at a different pitch's marker.

Two generator bugs:
- Python and JavaScript round x.5% differently, so Conine's plan says 62% and the leak row says 63%, about 17 plan lines page-wide; plan_checks cannot see it because it compares Python to Python.
- fallback_line labels any negative choices total 'about average' (Diaz vs LHP, −2.7), with an ASCII hyphen.

The target-scale mismatch (known item) is wider than the no-target sentence. It also appears in target sentences and the roster's 'was N': Tawa '20 points' next to 69% vs 39%, Olson 7 vs about 14 pooled. On Rutschman it flips sign ('3 points below' for a leak at 49% vs 43%).

Sample size is the main advice risk. First lines for Tawa (16 pitches) and Moniak (18) come from the take-before-two-strikes ordering, and many hand-tab lines rest on 12-20 pitches.

Nothing broken (undefined/NaN/missing roster rows) was found. Roster rows matched their cards apart from the rounding case. I did not verify the phone or dark layout; the dossier has no screenshots for this batch.

I reviewed all 20 cards in batch_02, each in the All pitchers, vs RHP and vs LHP views. I checked plan-line rates against the leak lists with a script, and checked the target sentences against what the leak lists' rates add up to. I read the step 17 code to tell rules working as designed from bugs. Nothing that plan_checks.py claims to guard broke, with one exception. The pitch-line rate check deliberately accepts both neighbors of a half point, so Duran (51 vs 52) and Goodman (62 vs 63) pass while the page shows two different numbers for one leak.

Biggest generator patterns:
1. **Hand tabs reuse the all-pitchers summary.** plan_items() gets the all-pitchers summary on every view. So the framing and contact lines quote all-pitcher numbers. Rengifo's vs LHP tab calls him better than average above a −4.7 table. Cam Smith's vs LHP tab says his bigger issue is contact over a 40%/40% misses row and +3.0 contact.
2. **Hand-tab closing lines speak for the whole card.** On Adell's vs LHP and France's vs RHP tabs, "Nothing on this card is a take rule" cancels the main plan's two take rules.
3. **Picture markers keep the all-pitchers numbers.** The plan's tags renumber on hand tabs, so a tag points at a different pitch's marker. Hand-tab plans can also include leaks that have no marker at all, including Lukes's −3.3 vs RHP, the biggest leak on his card.
4. **Markers sit on blue or gray spots.** This includes the only plan line on Lane Thomas and Perdomo, on the picture the card opens on.
5. **The no-target sentence flips sign** (Perdomo, Alonso), and it says "about at it" when the forecast is 5-6 points below the league.
6. **Video items are dropped silently.** When a plan has two takes, a video leak in the costliest count disappears with no word (France, Adell, O'Hearn).
7. **"Mostly vs LHP" without the LHP tab.** France's all-pitchers first line names left-handers, and his vs LHP tab says no single pitch stands out.

Many plan lines rest on 13-25 pitches. The take-before-two-strikes order often makes the smallest leak the first instruction and the roster's Start with.

No undefined/NaN or missing roster rows. The only stray text is an ASCII "-1.4" on France's vs LHP tab, and "–" in empty Zone numbers cells.

I read all 20 cards in batch_03 in all three views and checked sentences against the leak list, the By count table, the underlying data and the step 17 and template code (read only). Every leak-row rate and count, the target, the inches and the plus-count quotes agree. The bare '3' or '2' leak numbers in the dossier (Hicks, Bell, Schwarber, Lee, Baldwin, DeLuca) are a format_dossiers.py regex artifact, not a page bug; the raw page text numbers them all the same way.

The main problems are structural and mostly on the hand tabs:
(1) Picture markers always use the all-pitchers numbering, while hand-tab plan tags use the tab's own numbering. Tags then point to the wrong pitch, confirmed in the template: zones() draws only from p.leaks.all.
(2) A leak named for a hand, sometimes the plan's own line, disappears from that hand's tab (Hicks, Chourio, DeLuca, Arenado).
(3) Framing, contact and fastball sentences on hand tabs come from the all-pitchers summary.
(4) Hand-tab closings speak for 'this card'. Bell's LHP tab says nothing on the card is a take rule.

On the all-pitchers view the biggest issues are:
- Markers on blue spots under the plan's first line, on the picture that opens (Reynolds −13, Schwarber −5). The pictures pool pitch types; for switch hitters they also pool sides while drawing on the Batting left row.
- Costly counts left silent while the closing says these are the only changes (Caglianone −15.9, Chourio, Mullins, Varsho, DeLuca, Crews).
- Plan lines on 12 to 25 pitches.
- 'Within a ball' used for medians of 3.5 to 3.8 inches.
- Contact losses up to −8.7 unmentioned for 'mixed' hitters.
- Mullins told he misses 'about as often' while he misses 10 points less.

There are no noted hitters in this batch, so no coach's notes to check. The phone and dark views are not in the dossier and were not reviewed.

I read all 20 cards in batch_04 in all three views. Every 'N of M' rate, the 5-point quote rule, inches, count sums, step numbering and the selected picture checked out. None of the plan_checks guards misfired. The problems are structural and mostly on the hand tabs. A hand tab rebuilds the plan from the hand's leaks but reuses the card-level summary (framing choices, whiff, fastball clause), the static coach's note, the 'on this card' closing, and the leak-number tooltip, while the picture markers stay on the all-pitchers numbering. So the tabs regularly flip take/video for one pitch (Turang, Butler, Walker), drop a leak that is labelled for that hand (Vivas, Simpson, Lowe, Crawford, Cowser, Pages), contradict the coach's note (García, Harris), and quote the wrong totals, once with the wrong sign (Rumfield LHP). Second, the runs-based leak rule plus no pitch floor lets 12- to 23-pitch cells become plan lines, including García's first line and note lead (14 pitches). Third, decision-only hitters with big losses (Harris, Lile, Crawford, Walker, Lowe) get two-strike-only plans with no line or framing about 3 to 9 runs lost before two strikes. Walker gets a video-only plan beside a 6.0-run far-off cost. Fourth, markers often sit on blue or gray spots, because the pictures pool every pitch type, and the tooltip's bold gap is a shrunk number that does not match the two rates printed under it. I did not check phone or dark layout. I confirmed the generator behaviour in scripts/17_build_player_cards.py (framing_line, fallback_line, keep_line, plan_items using the card-level summary for hand tabs, target_text) and scripts/templates/player_cards.html (lines 927-944: leaktag title, the 'target counts all pitchers' condition, markers always drawn from p.leaks.all). I wrote no scratch files.

I reviewed all 20 cards in batch_05 in all three views, then checked every printed number against the leak list, the By count tables, the markers, the roster rows and UNDERLYING DATA. I also read step 17's plan code and the template, read-only, to confirm causes. Scratch scripts are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-samsullivan-Desktop-Personal-Projects-Baseball-Chase-Leaderboard/d455bc39-e405-4b67-b2e8-fa1ecc7f61ad/scratchpad/audit/b05/.

The biggest problem is the hand tabs, which are rebuilt from the hand's data:
- **Leaks missing.** A plan line that says 'mostly against right-handers' can have no leak on the vs RHP tab (Swanson, Hamilton, Álvarez).
- **Take vs video flips.** A leak near 4 inches can be a take on one view and a video item on another. On Guerrero's vs RHP tab this writes the take rule his whole card denies (19 such flips page-wide).
- **All-pitchers numbers.** The framing line, the contact clause and the fastball-strength clause read the all-pitchers summary, so a tab can call choices 'better than average' next to its own negative table. Hamilton's vs RHP tab calls his fastball decisions a strength while his top leak is fastballs mostly from right-handers.
- **Leak numbers.** The 'leak N' tags are the hand list's numbers, not the numbers drawn on the pictures.
- **Coach's note.** The note is repeated word for word on every tab, where it names a first line that tab doesn't have.

Two more issues reach every card:
- **Rounding.** Python's half-even formatting in plan lines doesn't match JS Math.round in the leak list: 16 plan lines and 5 roster lines page-wide differ by a point. plan_checks misses this because its rate check apparently formats both sides in Python.
- **Take-first order.** It can drop the biggest leak and the costliest count, while the closing line says the others are 'the only changes' and the target still counts the dropped leak (Álvarez, Ramírez).

Several first lines and roster Start-with lines come from 15-20 pitches, and hand-tab lines from as few as 12.

Not a page bug: in the dossiers, a leak whose label starts with '0-1 or 1-1' shows its number on its own line without parentheses ('1' then '0-1 or 1-1, ...'). That comes from the formatter's regex (it expects a capital letter after the number), not from the page.

I did not check phone or dark mode, because the dossier has no data for them.

I read all 20 cards in batch_06 in every view. I checked suspicious sentences against UNDERLYING DATA, the By count tables, the step 17 source (read only) and dump_2026.json, using one scratch script (audit/b06/rates.py). The batch covers 2 no-leak cards (Stephenson, Contreras), 3 execution-led hitters (Greene, Lowe, Taveras; Taveras is the switch hitter), 2 traded hitters (Lowe, Ballesteros), 1 noted hitter (Peraza), and decision-only/decision-led hitters (Julio, McCarthy, Ballesteros, Peraza).

The two most serious patterns:
1. **Markers on blue spots.** Leak markers often sit where the pooled-pitch picture is blue or gray. On García's and Chapman's cards this happens to the plan's own first line, on the picture the card opens on. Season-wide, 62 of 547 markers sit on a negative gap.
2. **Hand-named lines vanish from the hand tab.** The hand tabs drop all-pitchers plan lines that name that very hand: Julio's first line ('against right-handers') and Crawford's second ('mostly against right-handers').

Beyond those, the hand tabs drift from the all-pitchers view in four ways:
- different first lines and leaks;
- the pictures keep the all-pitchers numbers;
- the framing and contact sentences quote all-pitchers numbers;
- the fastball-strength clause sits beside a fastball leak.

Other recurring problems:
- Plan lines from 12 to 24 pitches, including first lines (Julio 17, Álvarez 24).
- Video leaks dropped from the plan without a mark in the leak list (Wells' biggest leak).
- Costly counts left with no line (McCarthy's costliest, ahead −3.5; Peraza's ahead −5.9).
- Plan lines on leaks at the league's rate (Chapman's whole plan).
- Stephenson's −8.4 contact loss never mentioned, because his net is positive and he falls to 'mixed'.

Two problems slip past plan_checks.py: rate rounding at exact .5 (Witt and Álvarez plan lines print 52% and 62% where their leak rows print 53% and 63%; 16 lines season-wide), and the no-target sentence ('1 points'; 'points below' for above-league leaks; 'about at it' for forecasts well below the league).

Several findings are the rules working as designed but still confusing to a reader; the 'why' field says so where it applies. I did not check the phone or dark views; the dossier has no rendering of them.

I read all 20 cards in batch_08, in all three views. None of the plan_checks.py-guarded failures showed up in this batch. Plan rates, inches, plus-count clauses, numbering, video-only closings and the roster Start-with lines all matched their leaks. Header, tiles, roster team, PA and runs agree on every card.

What the batch turns up is mostly cross-view trouble. The hand tabs are rebuilt independently, but they borrow season-level text without saying so:
- the contact sentence, from contact_why(summary);
- the framing total, from framing_line(summary);
- the fastball-strength clause, from keep_line and fastball_choices;
- the coach's note.

So a tab can quote numbers that are not on it, contradict the all-pitchers plan (Moreno: nothing-to-change vs a take; Mack: take/video swap at the 4.0-inch cut), or praise fastball decisions the other view asks him to fix.

Markers are drawn only for the all-pitchers leaks and never change with the hand control. So the leak tags on hand tabs point at the wrong pictures, or at nothing.

Inside the all-pitchers view, plan_pitch_items() does two things. It sorts small ahead-count leaks (16-21 pitches) first and drops video leaks whenever there are two takes. The result is first lines on tiny samples, the biggest leak left out without a reason (Langeliers, Lewis, Riley), and costly counts with no line or explanation (Pérez's Ahead −7.0 misses the spread line at 25.3% coverage).

By-design items I checked against code:
- 'Mostly vs LHP' needs only 55% LHP (HAND_LHP_SHARE 0.45), which is how Dubón's 56% leak gets the label; the brief's 80% applies to RHP only.
- execution-led requires a net loss (step 13), which is why Mitchell and Ewing get no contact word.

Not a card issue: the dossier prints a leak whose name starts with '0-1 or 1-1' as a bare number on its own line (e.g., Dubón's '3', Henderson's '2', Seager's '2', Pérez's '3'). This comes from the regex in format_dossiers.py (the lookahead wants an uppercase letter), not from the page.

I did not check phone or dark layouts.

I read all 20 cards in batch_09 across every view, checking the numbers against the UNDERLYING DATA, step 17's plan code (plan_items, framing_line, keep_line, productive_line, fallback_line), leak_rules.leak_cells and the template's marker code. Within cards the numbers tie out: the header rates equal the All counts row, the tiles and roster match, and the 'x of y' counts match the rates. The real problems are structural and mostly sit on the hand tabs.

1. The hand tabs mix data sources. plan_items() gets the hand's leaks and table, but takes the all-pitchers summary for the framing level, the far-off 0.0, the contact archetype and miss rate, and the fastball clause. The plus-count clause and the spread line use the tab's table. So one tab can quote two different totals, and plan_checks validates against the all-pitchers number, so it cannot catch this.

2. Leaks are re-derived per hand under the full leak rule: 12 pitches, 0.75 runs, and no net damage. A leak tagged 'mostly vs RHP/LHP' on the main view can vanish from that hand's tab. For Realmuto, Steer and Goldschmidt that is the plan's first line, and for Sánchez it is the biggest leak.

3. Picture markers always use the all-pitchers numbering, while hand-tab lists and tags are renumbered.

4. The LHP 'mostly' threshold is 55%, not the 80% the brief states.

Other findings: markers on blue spots (Burger's first line), costly counts left unexplained, the order rule leading with 12-15 pitch leaks, a few fallbacks whose sentence the table contradicts (Sánchez vs LHP, Vargas vs LHP), and an unclear number in Neto's coach's note.

Not issues on the page:
- In the dossier, leaks starting with '0-1 or 1-1' print as '1' instead of '(1)'. That comes from format_dossiers.py, whose regex needs an uppercase letter after the digit.
- Meckler's vs LHP '– / –' misses cell is correct: he has no chases there, and the league figure is computed on his chased pitches.

I did not check phone or dark views (not in the dossier).

I read all 20 cards in batch_10 (1,807 lines) in all three views. I checked every plan line against the leak list, the By count tables, the tiles, the target, the markers, the roster and the underlying data. Checked with no problems found: header rates vs All counts, tiles vs table totals, the inches quoted in plan lines, the plus-count "why" numbers, the 5-point rate rule, plan numbering and tags, roster Start with/Beat/Leak runs, and season-trend 2026 values. None of the plan_checks.py guards fired.

The biggest problems are in how the hand tabs relate to the all-pitchers view:
- **Leaks missing from their hand's tab:** a "mostly vs RHP" leak can vanish from the vs RHP tab. For Lee and Church it is the plan's first line, and the card even opens on that vs RHP picture.
- **Opposite instructions:** a hand tab can contradict the main plan. Bohm gets a take rule vs RHP where the main view says no take rule; Lee is told "Nothing to change" with two strikes where the main view says take.
- **Markers:** they always show the all-pitchers leaks, so on a hand tab the circled numbers point to different pitches than the tab's own numbers.
- **Borrowed numbers:** hand-tab sentences quote all-pitchers miss rates, run totals and the fastball clause.

Bugs I traced in step 17:
- **productive_line():** quotes total contact, not the named count's. This makes Church's vs LHP "Nothing to change" false: his ahead-count swings lost runs.
- **fallback_line():** calls any negative choices total "about average" and prints an ASCII hyphen instead of the minus sign.
- **target_text():** prints "about at it" for forecasts 6 to 9 points below the league. Its no-target sentence also flips sign: McMahon's leak is +3 in the list and "3 points below" in the target.
- **Contact line skipped:** step 13 labels any hitter with a slightly positive net as "mixed", so Jensen (+8.7 / −8.1) gets no contact line while Okamoto (+5.3 / −5.6) does.

The take-before-two-strikes order often puts a 16-22 pitch leak first, ahead of leaks up to four times bigger (Church: 16 pitches ahead of a 6.0-run leak on 74).

Two things in the dossier are not page bugs:
- Bare leak numbers ("3" instead of "(3)") on leaks whose name starts with "0-1 or 1-1" come from the dossier formatter (format_dossiers.py only adds parentheses before a capital letter).
- The By count "count status" column is not drawn on the card, so "productive" there versus "hitting well" on the roster is not something a reader sees.

I did not view the phone or dark layouts.

I read all 20 cards in batch 11 in all three views. Bogaerts and Durbin, the two no-leak cards, are clean. The biggest problems are on the pitcher-hand tabs, which are only partly rebuilt for the hand:

1. A leak the all-pitchers view names for a hand, often the plan's first line, can be missing from that hand's tab. 46 such leaks season-wide, 32 of them in the all-view plan.
2. Duran's coach's note names a lead pitch that the vs RHP plan drops.
3. The same pitch flips between take and video across tabs because the 4-inch cutoff is applied to each subset's median. 19 flips season-wide.
4. The framing line, the contact clause and the fastball-strength clause quote all-pitcher numbers that contradict the tab's own table.
5. The pictures keep the all-view leak numbers while the tab renumbers its leaks.

On the all-pitchers view:
1. The take-before-two-strikes order lets 12 to 14 pitch leaks lead the plan over costlier, better-sampled leaks (Young, McNeil, Duran).
2. Video leaks with large excess are dropped silently (Sheets).
3. Costly non-two-strike counts get no line and no explanation. 76 cards season-wide.

One finding means a plan_checks guard is wrong: plan percentages differ from the leak list by a point because Python and JavaScript round 0.5 differently (16 cases season-wide), and the "rates not its leak's" check compares Python with Python.

The extraction script's dossier formatter leaves leak numbers such as "2" or "3" on their own line when the leak name starts with "0-1". That is an extraction artifact, not a page bug, and is not reported. The card's By count table does not print count status; that column comes from the dossier formatter.

My scratch scripts are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-samsullivan-Desktop-Personal-Projects-Baseball-Chase-Leaderboard/d455bc39-e405-4b67-b2e8-fa1ecc7f61ad/scratchpad/audit/b11/: check.py and check_all.py (rounding), hand_missing.py, flip.py.

I read all 20 cards in batch_12 in all three views. Four cards are clean (Bauers, Betts, Keaschall, Cole Young): nothing stands out on any tab, and the table supports it. The biggest problems come from step 17 and the template, so they will recur on other cards.
(1) Leak markers are drawn where the smoothed picture shows blue or gray, including on the picture that opens selected for the plan's first line (Mayo, Kurtz, Bazzana).
(2) The hand tabs are rebuilt from that hand's leaks, but the pictures keep the all-pitchers marker numbers. Coaches see a 'leak N' tag that points to a different marker, and tab-only leaks with no marker (Caminero's 2.7-run fastball up against right-handers is on no other view).
(3) Lines driven by the summary (framing, contact reason, fastball-strength clause, coach's note) quote all-pitchers numbers on the hand tabs. On some tabs the tab's own table contradicts them (Manzardo vs LHP contact +0.6 under 'Your bigger issue is contact... 5 runs'; Giménez and Caballero notes naming 'the plan's two lines' in the wrong order).
(4) The hand label uses a 55% threshold for left-handers, so Grissom's first line says 'mostly against left-handers' while the cost sits with right-handers and the lefty tab says nothing stands out.
(5) The pre-two-strike-first rule promotes very small leaks into the lead line (Mayo 12 pitches, Larnach and Carrigg 15).
Already guarded by plan_checks and not seen here: plus-count why, framing runs, rates and inches in pitch lines, the roster start line, and 'hand overstated'.
Formatter artifact, not a page bug: leak numbers before names starting with a digit ('3\n0-1 or 1-1...') appear without parentheses in the dossier only, from the regex in format_dossiers.py.
Not covered: the phone and dark views, which the dossier does not include.

I reviewed all 20 cards in batch 13 (ranks 13 to 260), each in all three views, and cross-checked every card with a script (scratchpad/audit/check13.py) against dump_2026.json. The one "2" in Hoerner's leak list that is not printed "(2)" comes from the dossier formatter: its regex needs a capital letter after the number, and "0-1 or 1-1" starts with a digit. The page itself is fine.

What looks right: roster rows agree with the cards (team, PA, runs at stake, choices, contact, top leak, leak runs, inches off, beat, start-with). Every card opens on the picture of its plan's first line. Plan step numbers and leak tags are consistent.

The biggest problems:
1. Hoerner's first plan line says "mostly against right-handers", but his vs RHP tab says "Nothing to change". This is high.
2. On Hoerner, Soler and Murakami, the marker for the plan's first line sits on a blue spot in the picture the card opens on. The pictures pool all pitch types; the leak is one type.
3. The hand tabs are not really rebuilt from the hand's own data. The framing line, the contact reason, the fastball-strength clause, the coach's note, "the only change on this card", and the picture markers all still come from the all-pitchers data. As a result the tabs argue with their own tables: Antonacci vs LHP is called "better than average (+10.1)" over a table total of −0.2, and Caissie vs LHP gets "miss on 61%" over a table showing 78%.
4. Hand-tab plans rest on very small samples, down to 11 chases in 12 pitches.
5. Counts costing 2 to 4 runs go unexplained on Castro, Tovar and Raleigh. On Raleigh it is his costliest count, the first pitch at −3.1, which only his vs RHP tab takes up.
6. The 62.5% rounding mismatch between Python and the page's JS slips past plan_checks.

The known target-scale gap appears in target sentences too, not only the no-target ones: Winn's target says 9 points where his only leak shows 19. I did not review phone or dark layouts; this batch has no screenshots.

issues.statement:
On 136 of 261 cards, a vs RHP or vs LHP tab ends with a sentence about "this card" ("The only change(s) on this card..." or "Nothing on this card is a take rule for you yet"), but the tab's pitch lines are not the all-pitchers plan's. Counting a pitch that is a take on one view and a video item on the other, it is 143 cards (181 of 289 hand-tab closing lines). Most of these are a wrong scope word that the tab's heading and note soften (medium). A subset of about 50 cards directly contradicts the card's main instruction (high):
- 10 video-only tabs say nothing is a take rule while the main plan has takes.
- 4 tabs are the reverse.
- 30 cards drop a main-plan line that says "mostly against" that very hand and still claim "the only change".
- 3 tabs belong to cards whose main view has no plan.
- 2 vs RHP tabs (Schanuel, Hamilton) call fastball decisions a strength when the main plan's first line is a two-strike fastball take "mostly against right-handers".
evidence: Measure (dump_2026.json, rendered asides cross-checked against plan_items): 289 hand tabs on 216 cards have a closing line, and every one contains 'on this card'. 173 tabs on 136 cards name a different set of pitch cells from the all-pitchers plan. 181 tabs on 143 cards differ once take vs video status is counted. 116 tabs match.

Trea Turner, vs RHP: "Keep swinging at strikes. Nothing on this card is a take rule for you yet: the staff takes the pitch above to video with you first." All pitchers: "(1) On the first pitch, let breaking balls below the zone go." UNDERLYING DATA: that leak's share_rhp is 0.67, so the take mostly comes from the very hand whose tab denies it.

Nick Gonzales, vs RHP: the tab opens "So a pitch that is clearly off is a take even when you could reach it." and closes "Nothing on this card is a take rule for you yet". All pitchers (1): "When you're ahead in the count, let fastballs above the zone go." (share_rhp 0.69)
Video-only tab vs a take plan, all 10: Turner R, Gonzales R, Josh Jung R, Heliot Ramos R, Ty France R, Paul Goldschmidt R, Josh Bell L, Kyle Karros L, Jo Adell L, Francisco Lindor L.

Nolan Schanuel, All pitchers (1): "With two strikes, mostly against right-handers, let fastballs above the zone go." vs RHP: "Keep swinging at strikes; your fastball decisions are a strength. The only change on this card is the pitch above." The tab's one line is two-strike breaking balls. David Hamilton has the same pattern.

Sam Antonacci, All pitchers: "Nothing stands out. Your chase choices are about league average or better in every count." vs LHP: "The only change on this card is the pitch above." then "The plan for this pitcher hand only; pick All pitchers for the full plan." The same happens to Kevin McGonigle (vs LHP: 'Nothing on this card is a take rule') and Gabriel Moreno (All: "Nothing to change...").

Vladimir Guerrero, All pitchers: "fastballs above the zone are one to go over on video with your coaches, not a take rule" and "Nothing on this card is a take rule for you yet". vs RHP: "(1) When you're ahead in the count, let fastballs above the zone go." and "The only changes on this card are the pitches above." The reverse case also hits Alec Bohm R, Lawrence Butler L and Jordan Walker R.

Ben Rice, All pitchers (1): "With two strikes, let fastballs above the zone go." vs LHP: "Keep swinging at strikes; your fastball decisions are a strength. The only change on this card is the pitch above." 15 hand tabs say the fastball clause while the main plan has a fastball line. In 6 more (e.g. Austin Wells vs RHP, whose leak 1 is "Two strikes vs RHP, fastballs above the zone ... −2.0"), the tab's own leak list has a fastball leak.

31 main-plan lines on 30 cards say 'mostly against <hand>' but are missing from that hand's tab, which still ends 'The only change(s) on this card...'. Examples: Schanuel, Hamilton, Lile, Lukes, Hicks, Yandy Díaz, Crawford, Elly De La Cruz, Lowe, Pages.
63 cards have a vs RHP tab and a vs LHP tab that each name a different 'only change(s) on this card'.

What softens it, on every hand tab: the heading "What to work on vs right-handers" and, right after the closing line, "The plan for this pitcher hand only; pick All pitchers for the full plan." That note itself says the card holds more than "the only change on this card".
issues.method: I read keep_line and plan_items in scripts/17_build_player_cards.py, the aside() render in scripts/templates/player_cards.html, and the cross-view coverage of scripts/plan_checks.py (it checks each view on its own and never compares a tab with the all view). I wrote scripts in scratchpad/audit/handkeep/ (measure.py, final.py, detail.py, detail2.py). They run over all 261 players in dump_2026.json. For every R/L tab with a keep item, they compare the sorted pitch cells, and the cells with their video flags, against p['plan_items']. They split the mismatches into buckets: video-only vs take, the reverse, no main plan, a hand-named line dropped, and the fastball clause. Each keep text was confirmed in the rendered aside text, and the high cases were checked against UNDERLYING DATA (share_rhp, hand, leak lists per hand). I took no screenshot because this is a text issue, not layout.
issues.why_it_matters: Coaches open a hand tab to prepare a hitter for a starter of that hand. For Turner, Gonzales, Jung or Ramos facing a right-hander, the tab says nothing on the card is a take rule, though most of the main take rule's pitches came from right-handers. For Schanuel and Hamilton, the vs RHP tab calls fastball decisions a strength when the card's first instruction is a two-strike fastball take mostly vs right-handers. A coach could drop the card's main instruction for that game. Elsewhere, the player hears two or three different 'only changes' for one card, which undercuts trust in the plan. The rebuild per hand is by design; the closing sentence was written for the all view and never scoped.
issues.root_cause: scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:785-800, keep_line(summary, chosen). 'on this card' is hard-coded, and the function has no view argument, although plan_items(view=h) is called for each hand at :1067 and passes view only to pitch_line; it calls keep_line(summary, chosen) at :845. The fastball clause at :798 tests summary['fastball_choices'], a whole-card number (:1054), against only the tab's own chosen pitches. scripts/templates/player_cards.html:930 adds 'pick All pitchers for the full plan' on every hand tab, even when p.plan_items has no pitch line. scripts/plan_checks.py:252 checks each hand plan alone, so nothing compares a tab with the all view. The 30-card 'mostly vs this hand but dropped' subset also comes from the per-hand leak rebuild (leaks(hand_view(p, h)), :1061): the all-pitchers leak falls under 0.75 runs on one hand's pitches.
issues.suggested_fix:
1. Pass view into keep_line. On a hand tab, say "Against right-handers, start with the pitch(es) above." (or "...nothing here is a take rule yet: the staff takes the pitch above to video with you first."). When the all-pitchers plan has a take line the tab lacks, add "The All pitchers plan still stands." Never say "on this card" on a tab.
2. On a hand tab, leave out the fastball clause when the all-pitchers plan has a fastball line or the tab's leak list has a fastball leak.
3. In the template (:930), when p.plan_items has no pitch item, replace "pick All pitchers for the full plan" with "This line shows up only against left-handers; over all pitchers nothing stands out."
4. Add plan_checks guards: no 'on this card' in a hand keep line; no 'nothing ... take rule' on a tab when the all plan has a take; a main-plan line tagged 'mostly against <h>' must appear on tab h.
5. Bigger option: show the all-pitchers plan on every tab, marking the lines that apply to that hand and adding a hand-only line beneath. A tab's own rebuilt plan would then not compete with the main one.
refuted_items: Chase DeLauter is not in the high subset. His all-pitchers plan is also video-only ("Nothing on this card is a take rule for you yet: the staff takes the pitches above to video with you first"), so the vs RHP tab agrees with it in kind. Only the count (one pitch vs two) differs, which puts him in the medium bucket.

Corbin Carroll, José Altuve, Konnor Griffin, Patrick Bailey and Moisés Ballesteros do not hold. On their hand tab with a closing line, the pitches are the same as the all-pitchers plan's, so 'The only changes on this card are the pitches above' is true there. Carroll and Altuve list them in a different order, which is a separate issue. Their other tab is a fallback, contact or frame line with no closing.
Ballesteros's reported point, a video item counted among 'the only changes', is on the all-pitchers view of a mixed take+video plan. That is a separate keep_line wording issue, not a hand-tab one.

Severity high for all 143 cards is too strong. About 90 cards are a scope-word problem, and the tab heading ('What to work on vs right-handers') and the note under it limit it to confusion (medium). High holds for about 50 cards: the 10 video-only tabs against take plans, the 4 reverse, 30 cards with a dropped 'mostly against this hand' line, the 3 no-plan cards, and Schanuel and Hamilton's fastball clause.

Goldschmidt vs RHP and Ty France vs RHP (line 1) are weaker than reported. The main take they 'cancel' is tagged 'mostly against left-handers', so leaving it off the RHP tab is right in substance; only the 'on this card' wording is wrong. France's line 2 (52% from RHP) still holds.
Josh Bell, Karros, Adell and Lindor vs LHP hold as written. The main takes came 64-76% from right-handers, so the LHP tab is closer to right about lefties, but it still denies the card's rules.
Antonacci's misleading 'full plan' pointer holds and also hits Kevin McGonigle and Gabriel Moreno (3 cards).
Not reported but found: Francisco Lindor vs LHP and Josh Jung vs RHP are in the high subset. The same fastball-clause scope bug hits 15 more tabs (e.g. Ben Rice vs LHP, Maikel García vs LHP).

issues.statement: The hand label only checks who threw the leak's pitches (80% from right-handers, or 55% from left-handers). It never asks where the extra chasing came from, and its rates count both hands. Part (1), the mixed rates, holds: 141 cards carry a "mostly vs" leak, and on 151 of the 158 such leaks that also show on the named hand's tab, the two views print different rates. Part (2) is half right. The uneven thresholds are real and the page never states them. But checked against what each hitter actually faces, the left-hander label is the stricter one, and the glossary's "most of its pitches" rule is wrong in the other direction. Part (3) holds on a few cards. Grissom's plan line 1 names left-handers, but right-handers carry 75% of the cost, and his vs LHP tab says "Nothing stands out". On 8 cards the first plan line names a hand whose own tab says nothing stands out or nothing to change.
evidence: GRISSOM (wrong hand, plan line 1 and the roster's Start with): all-pitchers "(1) With two strikes, mostly against left-handers, let breaking balls below the zone go. You swung at 63% of them; hitters on average swing at 45%." Leak "(1) Two strikes, mostly vs LHP, breaking balls below the zone 63% vs 45% avg · 27 of 43 −2.3" (share_rhp 0.442). The vs RHP tab has the same pitch: "(2) Two strikes vs RHP, breaking balls below the zone 84% vs 53% avg · 16 of 19 −1.7", and its plan line 2 is "With two strikes, let breaking balls below the zone go. You swung at 84%...". The vs LHP tab: "Nothing stands out. Your chase choices are about league average or better in every count." / "None worth 0.75 runs per 600 PA." By subtraction the left-hander pitches are 11 of 24 (46% vs about 39%): 22% of the extra chases and 0.57 of the 2.32 runs. The card opens on "vs LHP, Two strikes", and marker 1 sits there at "you 65% vs avg 64% (gap +1 pts)".

HORWITZ (the extra chasing comes from the other hand): "(2) With two strikes, mostly against right-handers, let breaking balls below the zone go. You swung at 60% of them; hitters on average swing at 52%." (24 of 40). The vs RHP tab: "53% vs 51% avg · 18 of 34". So the 6 left-hander pitches were all chased (6 of 6, against about 58% for the league): 2.50 of the 3.02 extra chases. Marker 1 on the vs RHP row: "gap -11".

JOE MACK (plan line 1): "With two strikes, mostly against right-handers, let breaking balls below the zone go. You swung at 56% of them; hitters on average swing at 48%." (22 of 39). The vs RHP tab cell is 53% vs 49% (18 of 34), which would print "about as often". Five left-hander pitches (4 chased) carry 1.81 of the 3.24 extra chases.

8 plan first lines name a hand whose own tab has no leak and only a fallback: Wood, Vaughn, Lee, Hoerner, Goldschmidt, Vivas, Grissom, France (Gilbert's is line 2). Goldschmidt: "(1) With two strikes, mostly against left-handers, let breaking balls below the zone go. You swung at these about as often as other hitters do...", and his vs LHP tab says "Nothing stands out." Hoerner: "At 0-1 or 1-1, mostly against right-handers, let breaking balls below the zone go", and his vs RHP tab says "Nothing to change. You chase more than most hitters with two strikes (52% against 44%), but those swings have paid".

Mixed rates (known item), quotes checked: Rengifo all "mostly against left-handers... You swung at 45% of them; hitters on average swing at 20%" (10 of 22) vs the vs LHP tab "You swung at 71% of them; hitters on average swing at 27%" (10 of 14), so all 10 chases came from left-handers and the 8 right-hander pitches had none. Guerrero "69% vs 52% avg · 27 of 39" vs "78% vs 53% · 25 of 32". Peña "84% vs 41% · 21 of 25" vs "90% vs 42% · 19 of 21". Across all cards: 202 mostly-labelled leaks; 158 also on the named hand's tab, 151 of those print different rates, 26 by 5+ points; 44 are not on the named hand's tab at all.

Threshold: step 17:417 `HAND_RHP_SHARE, HAND_LHP_SHARE = 0.8, 0.45`. The docstring at :498 says "80% or more of its pitches came from it (55% for left-handers), and its rates count every pitch". There are 22 LHP-labelled leaks: 18 under 80% LHP, 10 under 65%, 8 under 60%. 77 unlabelled leaks on 65 cards are 75-80% RHP.

The left-hander threshold measured against each hitter's own mix: the league is 71.7% RHP. 20 of the 21 'mostly vs LHP' leaks are 10+ points above the hitter's own LHP share. Goldschmidt is the exception: 58% LHP in the leak, 51% overall (391 LHP pitches vs 375 RHP). 80 of the 181 'mostly vs RHP' leaks are within 10 points of the hitter's own RHP share, 46 within 5, and 10 below it. Nathaniel Lowe's plan line 1 is 'mostly against right-handers' at 80% RHP, while he faces 90% RHP (796 of 889).

Glossary (player_cards.html:1048): "with the pitcher hand when most of its pitches came from one (“mostly vs RHP”)". By that wording, 307 of the 317 unlabelled leaks would carry a hand (298 majority RHP, 9 majority LHP). The card's own leak note says only "Numbered on the pictures, on the row of the hand a leak names." No text on the web page says these rates include the other hand; only the staff report (step 17:2307) says so.

Reach: 144 all-pitchers plan lines say "mostly against", 77 of them the first line, 13 for left-handers. 77 roster "Start with" lines and 72 roster top leaks carry a "mostly" hand. Scripts: skeptic_mostlyhand/sweep.py, wronghand.py; output in skeptic_mostlyhand/out.json and wronghand.json.
issues.method: Read step 17 (lines 417-521: thresholds, leaks(), hand_phrase, leak_phrase; leak_markers at 1528), leak_rules.leak_cells (the leak rule: 12 pitches and 0.75 runs), plan_checks.py (lines 170-176 and 236-240, which only check that "mostly" is present), and the template's glossary and leak note. Wrote skeptic_mostlyhand/sweep.py and wronghand.py over dump_2026.json for all 261 cards and 547 leaks. They tally every hand-labelled leak by its share. They match each leak to the same cell on the named hand's tab and on the other hand's tab, compare the printed rates, and split chases, extra chases and cost between the hands by subtraction (the views share the e_match expectation, so these add up). They compare each leak's share with the hitter's own RHP/LHP mix from the tab totals. They also flag the named hand's tab having no leak and a fallback plan, and read each marker's picture gap on the named row. Then I checked every quoted example in the findings against the dump and the dossiers (Grissom, Goldschmidt, France, DeLuca blocks).
issues.why_it_matters: By design, but misleading: the 55%/80% thresholds and the mixed rates are deliberate, per the docstring at step 17:498. The wrong-hand outcomes are not deliberate. "Mostly against right-handers" reads to a player as "this is a right-hander problem". Yet the label measures only who threw the pitches, so for most hitters it mostly reflects facing about 72% right-handers. When the other hand carries the excess, the line aims the player at the wrong matchup. Grissom's first line, his roster Start-with and the picture the card opens on all point at left-handers. His own vs LHP tab says nothing stands out, while the vs RHP tab has the same pitch at 84% vs 53%. A hitter taking that line literally keeps chasing the right-hander's breaking ball. On 8 cards the first line names a hand that the card's own hand tab clears, a contradiction coaches will hit as soon as they switch tabs. The mixed rates (45% vs 71% for Rengifo) can't be reconciled from anything on the page. That piece is medium; the wrong hand on a first line (Grissom) is high.
issues.root_cause: scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:417 (`HAND_RHP_SHARE, HAND_LHP_SHARE = 0.8, 0.45`) and :460-463 (the hand is set from the raw pitch share alone: `rhp = (s["p_throws"] == "R").mean()`, with no check of which hand's pitches carry the extra chases or the cost, or of the hitter's own mix). :465-481 (rate, league, chases, pitches and choices come from the mixed cell s). :497-521 (hand_phrase and leak_phrase put ", mostly against <hand>" into the plan line, the leak name and the roster). scripts/templates/player_cards.html:1048 (the glossary's "when most of its pitches came from one" matches neither threshold), :943 (the leak note doesn't explain the label). scripts/plan_checks.py:170-176 and 236-240 check only that "mostly" is present, not that the named hand's tab agrees.
issues.suggested_fix: In leaks(), name a hand only when that hand's slice carries the leak. Compute xs = is_chase - e_match per hand. Set hand=H only if H's slice holds at least about 75% of the cell's extra chases and cost, its share is at least 10 points above the hitter's own share of H (this handles platoon bats like Goldschmidt, Straw and Lowe), and the slice passes lr.leak_cells on hand_view(p, H) without the LEAK_TOP cut. Otherwise leave the hand off. When a hand is named, print that hand's rate, league and "x of y" (the hand-tab cell), or say the share ("58% from LHP"). Add a plan_checks guard that fails when an all-pitchers line names a hand whose tab doesn't list the cell, or whose other hand's tab does. Rewrite the glossary to state the actual rule. A rough check with card data, "listed on the named hand's tab only, and that hand holds at least half the extra chases", keeps 151 of the 202 labels and drops 51. Of those, 35 are plan lines and 20 are first lines, among them Grissom, Goldschmidt, France, DeLuca and Joe Mack.
refuted_items: The left-hander label is the loose one: refuted against what each hitter faces. The league is 71.7% RHP, and 20 of the 21 'mostly vs LHP' leaks are 10+ points above the hitter's own LHP share (only Goldschmidt is not: 58% vs his 51%). The right-hander label is the one that mostly echoes who he faces: 80 of the 181 'mostly vs RHP' leaks are within 10 points of the hitter's own RHP share, and 10 are below it (e.g. Nathaniel Lowe, 80% vs 90%). 'Mostly' at 56% is still literally a majority.

"Even in a plan's first line (DeLuca, France, Goldschmidt, Grissom, Dubón, Taveras)": Dubón's and Taveras's leaks are not plan lines (no step). The first lines under 80% LHP are DeLuca, France, Goldschmidt, Grissom, Vaughn, Straw, Muncy and Riley.
"64 leaks that are 75 to 80% RHP carry no hand": it is 77 leaks (share_rhp 0.75 to 0.80) on 65 cards; 64/65 is the card count.

Dubón as a wrong-hand case: refuted. The left-hander pitches are 11 of 15 (73% vs about 45%) and carry the larger share of the extra chases (about 4.3 of 7.7). The vs LHP marker shows "gap +23". The label fits; it just isn't a leak on the vs LHP tab (about 0.65 runs).

Goldschmidt rated high: partly holds. His line already says "about as often as other hitters". Neither hand's tab lists the cell, so the card data can't show which hand carries the 0.9 runs, and he faces 51% left-handers, so the label adds little. What holds is that the vs LHP tab says "Nothing stands out" against line 1's "mostly against left-handers", and that his −5.8 vs RHP gets only a video item. He is medium, not the high case; Grissom is.

Taveras, Carrigg, Caglianone: the label doesn't name the wrong hand. The cell is a leak on BOTH tabs (Carrigg vs RHP "71% vs 49%" is that tab's first line), so the label narrows the line rather than misdirecting it.

Sheets leak 3 and Stowers leak 2: the named hand holds under half the extra chases (2 of 2 and 5 of 5 other-hand pitches chased), but Sheets' line already says "about as often" and Stowers' leak isn't in the plan, so the harm is small.

Every quoted rate pair in the findings was checked and holds exactly: Rengifo, Guerrero, Peña, Meidroth, Lile, Bregman, Stott, Contreras, Kirk, Gorman, De La Cruz, Collins, Yastrzemski. So do Karros (8 of 14 from LHP) and Heim (61% LHP).

Marker-gap signal: 49 of 202 labelled leaks show a gap under 5 points on the named row, but that also happens on leaks whose cell clearly beats the league on the tab. The smoothed picture is not the cell, so I did not use it alone as proof of a wrong hand.

issues.statement: On 52 of 261 cards, an all-pitchers leak or plan line named "mostly vs RHP/LHP" is missing from that hand's tab. On 45 cards it is not in the tab's leak list, and on 40 it is not in the tab's plan. On 21 cards it is the plan's first line, and on 12 the named hand's tab lists no leaks and prints a fallback or contact line instead. There are five causes, not one. A further 4 first lines say "mostly against left-handers" when most of the leak's cost comes from right-handers.
evidence: Sweep (handtab/final.py over dump_2026.json). 230 all-view leaks are named for a hand (208 R, 22 L). 46 of them, on 45 cards, are not in that hand's leak list, and 32 of those 46 are all-view plan lines. 41 hand-named plan lines on 40 cards are not in that tab's plan. The union is 52 cards. The first line is missing on 21 cards (20 also off the tab's list; Duran's is listed but not planned).

Why the 46 drop (read-only replication of the per-hand cell pitches, choices and contact with leak_rules; it matched all 285 all-view leaks exactly). 18: under 0.75 runs from that hand alone (e.g. Hoerner: 23 RHP pitches, −0.66). 10: the cell passes on that hand but falls past the top-3 cut or fails the extra-chase test (e.g. Julio: 17 of 17 from RHP, −1.12, fourth on the vs RHP list). 7: under 12 pitches from that hand (Realmuto 10, Elly 10, J. P. issues.root_cause:
scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:1057 re-runs leaks() per hand. That calls lr.leak_cells(...).head(LEAK_TOP), whose rules are in leak_rules.py:137 (12 pitches, 0.75 runs, extra chases > 0, choices+contact < 0) and leak_rules.py:54 (top 3). So a hand-named all-view cell can fail on its own hand's pitches.

17_build_player_cards.py:417/463 names a hand from its pitch share alone (R ≥ 0.8, L when RHP ≤ 0.45, i.e. 55% LHP), never checking whether the cell survives on that hand or carries most of the cost there.

17_build_player_cards.py:1067 builds the hand plans without start, so neither note_start nor the all-view lead is passed.

keep_line (17_build_player_cards.py:798) uses the all-pitchers fastball_choices on hand tabs.

After building summary["leaks"] for all three views, keep an all-view leak's hand only when its cell is also in summary["leaks"][hand] and that hand carries at least half the cell's choices cost. Otherwise set lk["hand"] = None and rebuild the phrase, so the plan line drops "mostly against ..." and the marker goes to the All pitchers row. This fixes 46 leaks and replaces the 55%-of-pitches LHP rule.

If the hand label should stay, carry the leak instead. Append the hand-only numbers to that tab's list, flagged ("from the all-pitchers plan; vs right-handers alone: 23 pitches, −0.7 runs, under the 0.75 bar"), and print that sentence in place of "Nothing stands out" / "Nothing to change".

- Use the hand's own fastball choices in keep_line.

issues.why_it_matters: Coaches use the card with the player in the room, and they will open the vs RHP tab before facing a right-hander. On these cards that tab tells the player the opposite of the main plan. Examples: "not a take rule" for the card's only take (Turang); "the only change on this card" for a take the main view says does not exist (Guerrero, Butler, Bohm, Walker, Moreno, Antonacci); "Nothing to change" or "Nothing stands out" for the hand the main line names (Grissom, Vaughn, Hoerner, Lee, Goldschmidt, France). In Grissom's case the hand label points the player at lefties, while most of the cost is against righties. Several flips come from medians 0.03 to 0.5 in either side of the 4-inch line, or from 7 to 8 chased pitches, so the reversal is noise, not a real difference between hands. This is how the code is meant to work (each tab is rebuilt from its own subset), and the tab note says to use All pitchers for the full plan. But the keep lines claim card-wide scope ("on this card"), which defeats that note.
issues.root_cause: scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:1057 builds each view's leaks from its own pitch subset, and :1067 rebuilds each hand plan with plan_items(..., view=h). Every threshold is applied again to the subset with no reference to the All view: is_video (:612-613, CLEARLY_OFF_IN=4 at :527, on the median depth of that subset's chased pitches set at :484), the leak rule (leak_rules.py:137: 12 pitches, 0.75 runs, choices+contact<0), and the fallback/'Nothing to change' text from that hand's count table (:644-701). The hand label is set by pitch share, not cost share (:417, :463). keep_line (:785-800) says 'on this card' on every view, and 'Nothing on this card is a take rule' looks only at the All plan. plan_checks.py checks each view on its own (:246-252), with no check across views.
issues.suggested_fix: 1. Make the take/video call once per pitch. In plan_items for a hand view, look up the same cell in summary['leaks']['all'] and use its is_video (and its depth wording) when the cell is there. Use the hand's own depth only for a hand-only cell, and add a dead band of about 0.5 in so a hand split cannot flip a call made on the All view. 2. On a hand tab whose plan has no pitch line, when the All plan has a line naming that hand, replace 'Nothing to change'/'Nothing stands out' with something like 'No leak of its own against right-handers; line 1 of the All pitchers plan (mostly against right-handers) still applies.' 3. In keep_line, say 'on this tab' (or 'against right-handers') for view != 'all'. In the All view, when a hand tab carries a take, write 'Nothing in this plan is a take rule yet' instead of 'Nothing on this card...'. 4. Do not print a hand-only take from fewer than about 20 pitches when the All view lists no leak there, or mark it as a small sample. 5. Name a leak's hand only when that hand carries most of the cell's choices cost, not just most of its pitches (fixes Grissom). 6. Add cross-view checks to plan_checks.py: same cell, same video flag in every view; no All-view 'no take' or fallback while a tab has a take; a hand-named All line must appear on that hand's tab or be explained there.
refuted_items: 'The sweep counts 19 such flips': partly. I count 12 distinct pitches on 11 cards whose printed plan text flips between take and 'not a take rule' (15 view pairs). Another 6 pitches on 6 cards (Harper, Carrigg, Mullins, Schmitt, Royce Lewis, Crow-Armstrong) are a take in one view and a listed video leak in another, left off that plan without comment: 18 in all, but only 12 are printed opposite instructions.

Harper (and Carrigg's vs LHP tab): no sentence on the other view calls the pitch 'not a take rule'. The video leak is left off because two takes already fill that plan (video never ahead of a take, at most 2 lines). This is an unexplained omission, not an opposite instruction. Carrigg's other point does hold: the 'mostly against left-handers' take quotes a blended 5-inch depth, while against LHP the depth was 2.94 and against RHP 6.59.

Kevin McGonigle: refuted as a take conflict. His vs LHP tab gives a video item ('Nothing on this card is a take rule for you yet') against an All view of 'Nothing stands out'. That is a low-severity inconsistency, not take vs no take.

Angel Martínez vs LHP 'Nothing to change': weak. Only 24% and 28% of the two plan pitches came from left-handers, and the tab's verdict is honest for that hand. It reads as a contradiction only because 'Nothing to change' is unqualified. The same applies to Arenado, Vargas, Church and Naylor (18-37% from that hand).
'Often on 13 to 18 pitches': true for 4 of the 6 hand-only takes (Antonacci 13, Butler 13, Guerrero 16, Moreno 17). Bohm's is 38 pitches and Walker's 30.

Jung Hoo Lee: holds, and is stronger than reported. Besides his two-strike take (78% RHP), his step-1 line 'When you're ahead, mostly against right-handers, let breaking balls below the zone go' (88% RHP) has no trace on the vs RHP tab, which says 'Nothing to change'.

Not reported but the same defect: Vaughn Grissom, Andrew Vaughn, Paul Goldschmidt, Nico Hoerner, Ty France and Spencer Steer (step-1 hand-named take; that hand's tab has no pitch line), and James Wood, Drew Gilbert and Jorbit Vivas (the same with a video item).

issues.statement: On 8 of the 261 cards (8 of the 73 "No target" sentences), the Target line says the leak or leaks were "N points below the league's chase rate in 2026". On each of those cards, every leak row shows him above the league. Pooled on the card's own rates, his leaks run +1.4 to +6.2 points. On 3 cards the plan's only take line also quotes his rate 5 to 7 points above the league's. The sentence prints step 19's frozen excess. That number is measured against a coarser league baseline, and on it these leaks (all two-strike breaking balls or changeups below the zone) come out below the league. The page never says the target uses a different measure. The same sentence then says "should be about at it in 2027" for forecasts of 4.4 to 8.6 points below the league.
evidence: Rutschman, plan line 1: "With two strikes, let breaking balls below the zone go. You swung at 49% of them; hitters on average swing at 43%."; leak row: "Two strikes, breaking balls below the zone 49% vs 43% avg · 22 of 45 −1.9"; Target: "No target: leak 1 was 3 points below the league's chase rate in 2026, and with no change should be about at it in 2027." (screenshot skeptic_flip/rutschman.png)

Alonso, plan line 1: "You swung at 56% of them; hitters on average swing at 51%."; leak row "56% vs 51% avg · 48 of 85"; Target: "No target: leak 1 was 2 points below the league's chase rate in 2026, and with no change should be about at it in 2027." (screenshot skeptic_flip/alonso.png)

Torkelson, plan line 1: "You swung at 51% of them; hitters on average swing at 44%."; leak rows "51% vs 44% avg · 28 of 55" and "51% vs 48% avg · 31 of 61"; Target: "No target: leaks 1 and 2 together were 1 points below the league's chase rate in 2026"
Perdomo: leak row "49% vs 46% avg · 40 of 81"; Target: "No target: leak 1 was 4 points below the league's chase rate in 2026"
García: leak rows "47% vs 44% avg · 15 of 32" and "57% vs 46% avg · 13 of 23"; Target: "leaks 1 and 2 together were 1 points below the league's chase rate in 2026"
Chapman: leak rows "48% vs 47% avg · 14 of 29" and "41% vs 39% avg · 11 of 27"; Target: "leaks 1 and 2 together were 6 points below the league's chase rate in 2026"

Okamoto: leak row "51% vs 49% avg · 39 of 76"; Target: "No chase target: leak 1 was 7 points below the league's chase rate in 2026, and with no change should be about at it in 2027. The number to move is contact on chases."
McMahon: leak row "Two strikes, mostly vs RHP, breaking balls below the zone 53% vs 50% avg · 26 of 49"; Target: "No chase target: leak 1 was 3 points below the league's chase rate in 2026"

The script finds 8 cards whose target_text contains 'points below the league'; on all 8, every leak's rate is above its league rate, both raw and as printed. The 2026 page holds the string exactly 8 times.

Frozen file results/xchase/coaching/leak_predictions_2026.csv, step 19's league rate vs the card's league rate on the same pitches: Rutschman 51.5% vs 43.5%, Alonso 58.6% vs 51.5%, Perdomo 53.0% vs 46.4%, Okamoto 58.0% vs 48.6%, McMahon 56.2% vs 50.1%. The hitter row's also_a_backtest_leak is 'no' for all 8. Of the 43 leak rows that sit below the league on that scale, 31 are two-strike breaking balls below the zone.

Card's pooled leak gap vs the frozen excess: Rutschman +5.4 vs −2.6, Alonso +5.0 vs −2.1, Torkelson +4.7 vs −0.8, García +6.2 vs −1.0, Perdomo +3.0 vs −3.6, McMahon +3.0 vs −3.1, Okamoto +2.7 vs −6.7, Chapman +1.4 vs −5.9
Glossary: "The target covers every leak on the card, together, in points above the league's chase rate." Nothing on the page says the target's league rate differs from the 'avg' in the leak rows.

Related: 22 'No target' cards print "should be about at it in 2027" for a forecast below −2 points, all 8 flip cards among them (Okamoto −8.6, Chapman −8.1, Perdomo −6.5, McMahon −6.1, Rutschman −5.7, Alonso −5.3, García −4.6, Torkelson −4.4)

The same sentence is also drawn on the printable card (17_build_player_cards.py:1662-1665) and written to player_cards_2026.csv and team_view_2026.csv. The page for every other season carries it too (counts of the string: 2022 16, 2023 10, 2024 8, 2025 8).
issues.method: I wrote scratchpad/audit/skeptic_target_flip.py and ran it over dump_2026.json (all 261 players). For each card with a target it compares target_text, target.excess and target.predicted with the card's own leak rates, raw, printed and pooled. I read the frozen leak_predictions_2026.csv with the project venv to get step 19's league rate for each leak. I read target_text and the TARGETS loader in step 17, step 19's excess computation, BACKTEST_LEAGUE_CELL in leak_rules.py and target_problems in plan_checks.py. I counted the string in each season's index.html. I re-took screenshots of the Rutschman and Alonso cards with shot.mjs (skeptic_flip/*.png). Each card named in findings 2, 33, 183, 218, 315 and 442 was checked on its own.
issues.why_it_matters: The word "leak", the leak row and, on Rutschman, Alonso and Torkelson, the plan's only take line all say he swings at that pitch more than other hitters. Three lines lower the Target says he swung at it less than the league. A player or coach cannot tell which is true and may decide the take rule is not needed. On the other 5 cards the plan line already says he swung "about as often as other hitters do", so there the clash is with the leak row. That is closer to medium, but high holds for the 3. The second half, "should be about at it in 2027", printed for a forecast 4 to 9 points under the league, reads as if he will rise to the league's rate. The mechanism is by design: step 17 has an explicit "points below" branch (line 994), plan_checks.py:216 accepts the "below" wording, and step 19's docstring expects some card leaks to sit at or below the league on its simpler baseline. The effect is not intended: the page tells the reader the target is in points above the same league rate the leak rows use.
issues.root_cause:
- scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:927-944 loads the target from leak_predictions_2026.csv excess_2026. That number is on step 19's scale: 19_freeze_leak_predictions.py:216-235 with leak_rules.py:62, BACKTEST_LEAGUE_CELL = [game_year, count_state, distance_bucket, pitch_group, region]. That baseline has no batter-side or pitcher-hand matchup and no spot smoothing. For two-strike breaking balls below the zone it puts the league about 7 points higher than the card's matched rate.
- target_text() at 17:988-997 prints round(excess*100) with its sign, so a negative excess becomes "points below the league's chase rate" (:994).
- The no-target test at :988 (pred <= TARGET_MIN_PTS) is one-sided, so a forecast of −8.6 gets "should be about at it" (:997).
- plan_checks.py:214-216 accepts "points below the league's chase rate" as a valid unit, so no check catches the flip.
issues.suggested_fix:
1. In target_text's no-target branch, take the "in 2026" points from the card's own leaks rather than the frozen excess: x = round(100 * (Σchases − Σleague·pitches) / Σpitches) over summary["leaks"]["all"]. That matches the rows above and is positive on all 8 cards (+1 to +6). The branch prints no number to beat, so it does not need the backtest number.
2. If the backtest number has to stay, drop the direction when it is ≤ 0, for example: "No target: on the measure the 2027 check uses, this leak was not above the league's rate, so there is no number to beat; the plan above still stands."
3. Say "at or under it" instead of "about at it" when the forecast is below −2.
4. In plan_checks.py, add a kind "target says below over leaks above": target_text contains "points below the league's chase rate" while every leak has rate > league. It would flag 8 cards today. Also remove "points below" from the accepted units at :216.
5. The target-scale cluster's broader fix (one measure for both, or a label saying the target is measured differently) would also cover this.
refuted_items: Finding 218 says 'Page-wide the sentence says below on 9 cards'. It is 8: both the 2026 page text and the dump show 8.

Finding 183's Crawford (+2.0), Suzuki (+0.8), Fermín (+11.4) and Teoscar Hernández (+17.6) have a positive frozen excess and no flip. That is a size gap only, so they belong to the target-scale cluster.
Finding 315's Collins (+3.9), Montgomery (+4.3) and Baty (+1.6) also have no flip and belong to the target-scale cluster.

Finding 442's 17 non-flip cards (Trout, Crawford, Paredes, Bleday, Wells, Lowe, Baty, Turang, Mullins, Yelich, Montgomery, Swanson, De La Cruz, Lindor, Henderson, Ewing, Bohm) say 'above', not 'below'. They are not in this cluster.

From finding 442: A. J. Ewing and Alec Bohm print "No number to beat: every leak on this card was mostly within a ball of the zone...". No points are printed, so they are in neither cluster. JJ Bleday's sentence says 6 points against a card pooled gap of +6.4, so there is no pooled scale gap.

Four more cards have a negative frozen excess but print no flip. James Wood (−0.9), Drew Gilbert (−1.9) and A. J. Ewing (−0.5) are video-only cards with no number. Curtis Mead (−0.1) prints "about at the league's chase rate" beside "52% vs 51%", which agrees with the row.

The 'medium' rating in findings 183, 218, 315 and 442 is too low for Rutschman, Alonso and Torkelson, where the target contradicts the take line's quoted rates. It is fair for Perdomo, García, Chapman, Okamoto and McMahon, whose plan line already says 'about as often as other hitters do'.
Finding 2's extra claim holds: 'should be about at it' is printed for Rutschman's −5.7 forecast. The same happens on 22 'No target' cards in all.

issues.statement: Confirmed in part. With the Mac/iOS font (Avenir Next), every card's By count table is wider than its scroll box at 320-430px phones, at 641-746px and at every two-column width from 1101 to about 1470px. The cut columns are Contact at 1366-1470, Choices and Contact at 1280, and xwOBA, Choices and Contact at 1101-1200 and on phones. The box draws no scrollbar and nothing else marks that the table scrolls. Several of the report's details are wrong: 1512px and wider (including 1600 and 1920) show the whole table on all 261 cards, 641-746px does not fit, and with Nunito Sans (the font Windows and Android get) 1440px fits.

issues.method: I confirmed that the served page matches results/xchase/player_cards/2026/index.html (same sha1). I wrote skeptic_bycount2/m.mjs, which drives headless Chrome over CDP. At 26 viewport widths (320-1920) it loops over every card on the vs-all, vs-RHP and vs-LHP views, with and without 'Show far-off and misses'. For each card it measures the #aside .tablewrap scrollWidth against clientWidth and the scrollbar height, then tests each header and cell one glyph at a time to see which characters fall past the box's right edge. I re-ran it with Nunito Sans forced, and again with scrollbars not hidden. I took screenshots with shot_layout.mjs and shot.mjs (viewport shots scrolled to the table; I printed the card's name each time because one clipped shot had loaded the wrong card). I read the template CSS and countTable(), and git history for commit e7bf2a1. I searched dump_2026.json for plan sentences that cite the count table or the Misses rate. Finally I injected trial CSS to test the fix (trialA.json, trialB.json).
issues.why_it_matters: This is partly by design. Commit e7bf2a1 deliberately made the table scroll inside its own box rather than push the page sideways, and that commit notes the table is 665px against a 561px aside at 1280. Nothing was added to tell readers the box scrolls, though, so on a Mac trackpad or a phone they see what looks like a finished table with broken numbers ('−0.', '.2', '.29') or simply no Choices or Contact column. The real cost is the Choices column. 81 plans send the reader to it ('+8.4 runs in the count table', 'the count table shows where'), and it is invisible on 1101-1280px laptops and tablets and on every phone, while the note under the table goes on describing columns the reader can't see. On phones the 'Show far-off and misses' button shows neither column in full, so contact hitters can't find the miss rate their plan quotes. The plan itself still reads correctly, so this stays medium. The report overstated two points: the Contact total is always in the header tile, and 1512px and wider is fine.
issues.root_cause: scripts/templates/player_cards.html, several pieces together. At :98 the two-column body splits 1.05fr/1fr, and the :220 breakpoint at 1100px turns that into a 474-662px aside. At :146 the cells are 'th, td { padding: 4px 8px; white-space: nowrap }' and at :150 'td .avg { margin-left: 6px }' puts each you/avg pair on one line, so the 8-column table from countTable() (:852-876) is 656-665px wide. At :141 '.tablewrap { overflow-x: auto; }' clips it with no shadow, fade or hint. At :115 (commit e7bf2a1) the minmax(0, 1fr) column makes it scroll rather than spill. On phones (:223, :873) only Far-off and Misses are toggled ('nar'), which leaves a table of about 460px in a 278px box.
issues.suggested_fix: These are all in player_cards.html. (1) Put the league number under the hitter's number: 'td .avg { display: block; margin-left: 0; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.25 }' plus 'thead th small { white-space: normal }'. Also use 5px side padding on #aside th/td at min-width 1101px. Tested on all 261 cards: the table then fits at 1200, 1280, 1366 and 1440 (it is 22-25px over at 1101). (2) On phones (max-width 640px), make Pitches and xwOBA the toggled columns instead of Far-off and Misses, so the default view shows Chases, Choices and Contact (the columns the plan cites), and rename the button to match. Tested: fits at 390 (1px into the cell padding), still 31px over at 360. (3) Wherever the table still overflows (1101-1199, 360px phones, the all-columns view on phones), add a visible cue: a sticky first column plus a right-edge fade drawn with a background-attachment: local gradient. (4) Add a layout check next to e7bf2a1's: every card's #aside .tablewrap scrollWidth - clientWidth must be 8px or less at 390, 1280 and 1440.
refuted_items: 'Only widths of 641 to 1100px show the whole table' is wrong at the low end. 641-746px also clips: at 641, Choices and Contact are hidden on 261/261, a 113-122px overflow, because the phone rules stop at 640 and all 8 columns return. The widths that fit are about 747-1100, plus exactly 640 in the phone layout's default view.

'143 cards at 1600/1920' is wrong. At 1512px and wider, including 1600 and 1920, 0 of 261 cards lose any glyph. The 143 are cards with a 3px overflow that falls inside the cell's 8px right padding. A real 143-card glyph cut happens only at 1472px.

'At 1440 the Contact column is cut' holds only for Avenir Next (macOS/iOS). With Nunito Sans, the web font Windows and Android readers get, 0/261 clip at 1440 and above. For those readers clipping starts at 1366 (Contact partial) and 1280 (Choices partial, Contact hidden).

'For contact hitters Contact is the main evidence' does not hold. The contact sentence quotes the Misses column ('You miss on 68% of your chases, against 45%', in 28 of 43 execution-led plans), and the Contact total is always visible in the header's 'Where the runs go' tile. The column the plans actually point to is Choices: 81 plans, hidden at 1280px and below and on phones.

'Choices and Contact off-screen even after Show far-off and misses' holds, and it is worse than reported: after the tap, Misses, xwOBA, Choices and Contact are all hidden at 390 and Far-off shows only its first digits.
'macOS hides scrollbars' holds for this Mac: no bar is drawn even with scrollbars enabled in headless Chrome. Windows classic scrollbars would probably show a bar as a cue, but I could not test that.

issues.statement: Most of this cluster holds on all 261 cards. Below 1100px the card is one column: the plan comes first and the pictures sit 975 to 2,128px below the plan's heading, after the closing "Does fixing a leak pay?" line. On phones the leak markers are 8.6px circles with 5.1px digits, the Misses-row key is hidden, the 3D panel clips its axis labels, header values break away from their units, the leak rate column wraps on every leak at widths over 640px, and a double rule sits over the Misses row. Several details are overstated: the first phone screen is controls plus the name and header lines, not controls only; Zone numbers scrolls sideways rather than being cut off; dark-mode hairlines are no fainter than light-mode ones; the 3D clipping is not dark-specific. One clipped panel the reviewers missed: the By count table is wider than the right column, which hides its Choices and Contact columns at 1101 to about 1575px and on phones.

HEADER BREAKS: at 1280px, 172 of 261 cards break inside a value (171 'xChase+' / 'NNN', e.g. Geraldo Perdomo 'xChase+' / '148, 2nd of 261' in shots/perdomo_1280_head.png; 1 'NNN PA': Curtis Mead '331' / 'PA · xChase+ 122, 40th of 261' in shots/mead_1280_head.png). issues.method: Started a static server on the built page, results/xchase/player_cards (read-only). Ran an in-page script, sk_layout3/allcards.js, through headless Chrome (sk_layout3/cdp.mjs) over all 261 hitter cards at 390x844, 768x1024, 1024x768, 1280x800 and 1440x900. It measured offsets of the controls, name, plan heading, 'Does fixing' line and pictures; picture width, from which marker size follows; line breaks inside values in the header and eyebrow, using Range client rects; leak-rate wraps and natural widths; Misses-row subtitle display, legend text and the rule positions; Zone numbers and By count scrollWidth vs clientWidth, with which column heads are visible. Probed the By count box at 360, 390, 640, 1101, 1280, 1440, 1600 and 1920 (probe_aside.js). Took about 25 screenshots (some at DPR 2-3) of Montgomery, Chapman, Pérez, Ward, Mead, Perdomo, Hernández and Rutschman, in light and dark, with the 3D and Zone numbers panels open and Show = Misses. Computed WCAG contrast for the hairline and plate-line tokens and the blended weak-red colors in both themes. Read the CSS and drawing code in scripts/templates/player_cards.html.
refuted_items: 'On a phone the first 844px are all controls' is overstated. Controls end at y=483 and the name, header line and chase sentence are on the first screen (name y=625). What is true is that no plan line and no picture are (plan heading at median y=1,068).
'Pictures 1,400 to 2,000px further down' is roughly right. Measured 975-2,128px depending on width and card (tablets 975-1,479; phones 1,094-2,128).

'Zone numbers shows only the First pitch column' is partly right. The box scrolls sideways (overflow-x:auto) so nothing is lost; the real problems are that nothing shows the table scrolls and that cells are cut mid-number.
'3D clips its axis labels (phone / dark)' holds on phones in both themes; it is not a dark-mode problem.

'Dark mode nearly hides the hairlines' does not hold. Hairline contrast is 1.24:1 in dark vs 1.29:1 in light, equally faint by design in both themes. The plate line is only modestly fainter (1.48 vs 1.75), and the weak-red-turns-brown part holds.

'Names wrap at 1280' is not a defect by itself: a balanced two-line name reads fine. The cause worth fixing is that the tiles squeeze the name column to its 340px basis, which also breaks 'xChase+' from its number on 172 cards, far more than the three named.
'Every leak wraps to rate · / n of m' is confirmed (547/547 rows at widths over 640px), not refuted, but it holds only above 640px; at 390 the rate moves under the leak name and does not wrap.
issues.why_it_matters: On a phone or tablet, the plan's 'leak ②' tags point to pictures two or three screens away, after the card's closing line. On a phone the numbered markers are too small to read, and nothing explains the purple and green row that is the evidence for a contact hitter's 'You miss on N% of your chases' line. The By count table's Choices column backs the plan's 'your choices are a plus overall' and costly-count lines, but it is out of view at 1101 to about 1300px and on phones (Contact up to about 1575px). The plan text itself is intact, so the main instruction survives; that is why this is medium, not high. Two parts are deliberate: the plan-first order (CSS comment 'so a phone opens on the plan', which the phone does not actually achieve) and marker shrinking (comment 'markers shrink with the panel so they never swamp a small picture'). Hiding the row subtitles at ≤640px is also on purpose to save width. Nothing else here is.

Line 229 hides '.zgrid .rowhead span' at ≤640px; the legend (lines 741-743) names only blue and red in chase mode. Line 614 builds line1 with ordinary spaces ('${p.pa} PA', 'xChase+ ${...}', '${ordinal} of ${p.of}'), line 630 the eyebrow 'per 600 PA'; .tile .note has no max-width, so at 1280 the tiles take the row and .head > :first-child sits at its 340px flex basis (line 85).
