issues.suggested_fix: (1) At ≤1100px, split the aside so the order is plan, then leaks, then .zones (pictures), then By count, trend and the evidence line, and move D.evidence out of the aside so it is always last. At ≤640px put the card before the controls, or fold Compare / Show / Pitches / Plan-hand into a collapsed 'View options' details element, so the first screen holds the name and the plan. (2) Give markers a floor: scale = Math.max(0.8, Math.min(1, w/150)), about a 17.6px circle with a 10px digit, or show two count columns per row on phones. (3) Keep '.zgrid .rowhead.whiff span' visible at ≤640px, or add 'Purple: more misses. Green: fewer.' to the chase-mode legend when the Misses row is present. (4) Use   in '${p.pa} PA', 'xChase+ ${n}', '${ordinal} of ${p.of}' and 'per 600 PA', and give .tile .note a max-width of about 34ch so the name column is not squeezed at 1280. (5) Leak rate: render 'X% vs Y% avg' and 'n of m' as two block spans with no ' · ', or use 'max-content' for the column. (6) By count: also hide the .nar columns, with the toggle button, in the two-column layout below about 1600px; on phones put Choices and Contact before xwOBA, or move xwOBA behind the button. (7) Zone numbers: add a right-edge fade or 'swipe for more counts' note on phones, or transpose the table there. (8) 3D: at widths under 500px set margin {l:30, r:10, b:30} and move the camera eye out about 1.3x. (9) Dark mode: fade low-evidence colors toward --mid rather than --surface, and lighten the plate line (e.g. #5a5953). (10) Drop the border-top on .rowhead.whiff and append .whiffrule only for the extra Misses row in chase mode, not for every row when Show = Misses.

issues.statement: Most of the cluster holds. xChase+ (on all 261 headers, a roster column and the dropdown), "no target" (73 roster rows), "noted" (17 rows), step numbers and "frozen line" are never explained. The only reading guide sits on the two reference cards, and nothing links to them. Far-off is called "off the plate" in some places and "off the zone" in others, and a few labels slip ("Changeups", "Where it missed", "Target: No target:"). The most-reported piece, card "productive" against roster "hitting well", is refuted: no card prints a count-status word.
evidence: xChase+ never defined: no definition in the footer, count note, guide, roster lede, glossary or state line, and none on any of the 261 cards (regex for 'xChase+ is/means/measures', '100 = average', 'higher is better' finds 0). It shows on 261 of 261 headers, e.g. Canzone: 'Bats left · 6'0" · SEA 2026 · 532 PA · xChase+ 107, 108th of 261' with line 2 'Swings at 35% of pitches outside the zone. Hitters on average swing at 30% of the same pitches.'

27 hitters have xChase+ above 100 while their header says they chase more than the league (Burleson 106 at 38% vs 27%, Bichette 102 at 41% vs 31%, Arráez 129 at 33% vs 30%). 21 are below 100 while chasing less (Nathaniel Lowe 97 at 27% vs 33%). This is by design: README says 'xchase_plus = 100 + 100 * runs_saved_shrunk / league_chase_cost_per_600_pa ... 100 is league average', and that counts what the chases produced.

The dropdown shows a bare number, 'Salvador Pérez (73)', under the group 'Every qualified hitter, by xChase+ (261)'. Footer: 'xChase+ 1.1 · Statcast 2026 · 261 qualified hitters. ... Built by step 17 of the Chase Leaderboard project.'

Guide: 0 of 261 player cards carry 'How to read a player card'; only the 2 reference cards do (template aside(), p.reference branch). An empty hash opens defaultSlug 'salvador_perez' (default_1440_vp.png). The template has no href to '#average-right-handed-hitter' or the left-handed one, so the Hitter dropdown's 'Reference' group is the only way in.
The guide's 7 items never mention the cost tile, video items (37 cards print 'not a take rule'), the Target (229 cards), the coach's note (17 cards), the vs RHP/vs LHP tabs or xChase+.

no target: the roster Beat column shows 140 'under N (was M)', 73 'no target', 16 'none: video only' and 32 blank. The glossary explains only the video case: 'a fix is anything under it, and a card whose leaks are all video items has none.' Of the 73, 49 cards say 'No target: ...should be about at it in 2027' and 24 say 'No chase target: ... The number to move is contact on chases.'

Griffin roster row: '| PIT | Konnor Griffin | R | 81 · 241st | 339 | 6.8 | −11.0 | −1.0 | choices | Two strikes, breaking balls below the zone | −2.7 | 6 | average | no target | At 0-1 or 1-1, let breaking balls below the zone go (71% vs 43%, 5 in off) |'

New in the same pattern: 89 cards print a doubled label (template:944 adds 'Target: ' to text that already starts with one). 49 read 'Target: No target: leaks 1 to 3 together were 7 points above...' (Griffin, konnor_griffin_1440_full.png), 24 read 'Target: No chase target: ...' and 16 read 'Target: No number to beat: ...' (James Wood).

noted: 17 roster rows carry the tag (e.g. 'Salvador Pérez noted', 'Oswald Peraza noted'), 9 easiest and 8 biggest. 'noted' appears nowhere in the roster title, lede, glossary or state line. Only the card dropdown names the groups: 'Noted: easiest to improve' / 'Noted: biggest losses'.

Jargon: glossary 'Problem: the share of the loss that is choices (step 13)' and '...with this season's number beside it (step 19)'. Lede: 'what the frozen line expects with no change at all'. 'qualified' (footer, lede) never gives the PA floor.

Off the plate vs off the zone: far-off is distance outside the zone measured both ways (02_build_chase_dataset.py:390 sqrt(horizontal_miss**2 + vertical_miss**2); step 17:250 distance_outside_zone > 0.35 ft). Yet the tile on 261 of 261 cards says 'runs per 600 PA from your choices on pitches at least 4 inches off the plate', the count note says 'Far-off: 4+ inches off the plate.' and the guide says 'far-off means at least 4 inches off the plate'. Plan lines say 'The ones you swung at were typically 5 inches off the zone.' (773 times), and so does the glossary. 452 of 547 all-pitcher leaks sit directly above or below the zone.

Two names for one number: roster 'Runs at stake' and the card tile 'COST OF FAR-OFF CHASES' are the same value on 261 of 261 cards. Team separator: 19 of 19 traded hitters show ' / ' on the card and ', ' on the roster, e.g. Ward 'BAL / SEA 2026' vs '| BAL, SEA | Taylor Ward |' and Mead '| WSH, CWS, BOS | Curtis Mead |'.

Bare hand in Top leak: 4 roster cells and 28 all-pitcher leak rows, e.g. '| ATH | Carlos Cortes | ... | Ahead in the count vs RHP, fastballs above the zone |'. The glossary defines only '(“mostly vs RHP”)'. A bare 'vs RHP' means every pitch in the cell came from right-handers (step 17 leak_phrase docstring).

Controls and labels: 'Pitches' control label 'Changeups' (template:295), while 95 cards' leak lists say 'changeups / splitters' and the state line says 'changeups and splitters'. Zone numbers head is 'Where it missed' on 261 of 261 cards (template:978), while the count note says 'Misses: swing-and-miss on a chase.'

The count note's last sentence, 'With a pitcher-hand tab, both sides face that hand.', prints under the All pitchers table on 261 of 261 cards, where no hand tab is open. Elsewhere on the page 'side' means batter side ('Same side and hand', 'hitters of your side').
Evidence line on 261 cards: 'Hitters who cut their leak chasing more than expected stopped giving counts away'.

Roster page: title 'Chase decisions by team, 2026' is fixed (template:1046). Under the roster the footer reads 'Every picture compares a hitter with the average hitter ... “Same side and hand” also matches batter side and pitcher hand.' (roster_1440_full.png), though the roster has no pictures and no such control. Lede: 'Tap a name for his decision card.' while the state line says 'Click a column to sort by it.'

Beat sort: template:1062 has 'const key = state.sort === "target" ? "excess" : state.sort;'. Sorted on Beat descending, the shown 'under N' values go up 11 times between neighbours, and the 73 'no target' and 16 'none: video only' rows are mixed in (first 'no target' at row 144).

3D summary, fixed markup at template:328: 'In 3D: the selected picture as a hill, taller where you swing more'. On the reference card the height is the league rate ('% of hitters swing here'), and in 'Misses on chases' mode it is the miss rate.

Count check vs card: the card never shows the verdict. For Yandy Díaz and Colt Keith the roster says 'hitting well' while their By count row reads 'Ahead in the count	240	25%29%	14%17%	28%42%	.348.358' and '.352.358' (xwOBA below league; the verdict uses a shrunk estimate).
Screenshots: skeptic_labels_v2/default_1440_vp.png, roster_1440_full.png, ref_rhb_1440_full.png, konnor_griffin_1440_full.png
issues.method: I read the page text in dump_2026.json (footer, countNote, evidence, guide, roster title/lede/glossary/state/head) and ran skeptic_labels_v2/measure.py over all 261 cards and 261 roster rows. It searches for definitions, counts the Beat cell kinds and the reasons behind them, compares tile values with Runs at stake, checks team separators, counts off-plate vs off-zone wording, finds bare-hand leaks, checks status words in rendered card text and simulates the Beat sort. countcheck.py compares roster Count check with the card's By count xwOBA. I read the template (player_cards.html: header 608-620, aside 912-944, numbers 978, roster 1011-1110, markup 255-352) and step 17 (GLOSSARY 1447, GUIDE ~1990, page data 2150-2163, leak_phrase 494-516, count_table 430-455), plus 02_build_chase_dataset.py:375-394 for far-off. I re-took screenshots of the default card, the full roster, the RHB reference card and Griffin with a copy of shot.mjs (port 9371).
issues.why_it_matters: xChase+ is the headline number, the roster column and the dropdown order. A reader cannot tell whether 73 is good, or why a hitter who chases 38% against 27% scores 106. That second part is by design: xChase+ counts what the chases produce. A coach scanning the roster sees "no target" beside a −11 choices hitter with a plan line, plus "noted" tags and step numbers, with nothing to decode them. The guide that would help is reachable only through a dropdown group. The rest is polish: two names or separators for one thing, "off the plate" for pitches above or below the zone, "Target: No target:". None of it changes a plan line, so the main instruction survives (medium, not high). Some pieces are by design but still unexplained: the blank Beat for the 32 hitters with no leaks, the bare "vs RHP" meaning every pitch came from right-handers, and the Count check using a shrunk estimate.
issues.root_cause:
The page-level strings were never given definitions for their headline terms:
- Footer and count note: scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:2158-2163, built from GLOSSARY (17:1447-1449).
- GUIDE (17:~1985-1999): shown only in the reference branch of aside() (player_cards.html:912-917). defaultSlug is README_EXAMPLE (17:2152), and nothing links to the reference slugs.
- Roster lede and glossary: template:1047-1048 have no xChase+, noted, 'no target' or blank-Beat entry. 'no target' itself is set at template:1020.
- 'Target: ' prefix: template:944, added before target_text (17:966-990), which already starts 'No target:', 'No chase target:' or 'No number to beat:'.
- 'off the plate': template:620, GLOSSARY 17:1449, GUIDE 17:1998.
- Separators: ' / ' at template:615, ', ' at template:1080.
- Column and section labels: 'Runs at stake' template:1033, 'Changeups' template:295, 'Where it missed' template:978, 3D summary template:328.
- Footer element sits outside the card and roster sections (template:352), so it shows on both views.
- Fixed roster title: template:1046.
- Beat sorts by excess: template:1062.
- Count check word: template:1011/1026, shown only on the roster.
issues.suggested_fix:
1. Add one line to the footer, the roster glossary and the guide: "xChase+: runs your chase decisions saved or cost, including what the chases produced; 100 is league average, higher is better." Label the dropdown number too ("(xChase+ 73)").
2. Put a "How to read this card" link to #average-right-handed-hitter on every card and on the roster. Add guide items for the cost tile, video items, the Target, the coach's note, the vs RHP/LHP tabs and xChase+.
3. Roster glossary:
   - "noted: the card has a coach's note".
   - "no target: with no change the forecast is already within 2 points of the league, or, for contact hitters, the number to move is contact".
   - "blank: no leaks".
   - "vs RHP without 'mostly': every pitch came from that hand".
   - Drop "(step 13)" and "(step 19)", say "a forecast fixed now" for "frozen line", and state the PA floor.
4. At template:944, skip the "Target: " prefix when target_text starts with "No".
5. Use "off the zone" in the tile, GLOSSARY and GUIDE.
6. Use one name and one format for each repeated item: "Cost of far-off chases" on both views, one team separator, "Changeups/splitters" on the control, "Where the pitch was" for the Zone numbers head, and "taller where the rate is higher" for the 3D summary.
7. Count note: replace the last sentence with "On a vs RHP/LHP tab, both columns count only that hand's pitches", and show it only on hand tabs.
8. Give the roster its own footer, without the pictures sentence and without "Built by step 17".
9. Evidence line: "Hitters who cut their chasing in a leak by more than expected...".
10. Sort Beat by the target number, with 'no target' and 'none' rows last.
refuted_items: Card 'productive' vs roster 'hitting well' (findings 62, 85, 159, 391): REFUTED. No card prints a count-status word: 0 occurrences of 'productive' or 'hitting well' in the rendered text of all 261 cards across 3 views each. 'productive' comes from the audit's dossier formatter (format_dossiers.py:23 adds r['status'] as a 'count status' column). The roster maps productive to 'hitting well' at template:1011. What does hold: the roster Count check has no counterpart on the card, and for Yandy Díaz and Colt Keith it says 'hitting well' next to a card row showing xwOBA below league.

'Count check' undefined: REFUTED. The roster glossary defines it ('Count check: how he hits once the count reaches the leak's counts, shrunk for noise, against the league in the same counts'), and it appears only on the roster, so its absence from the card guide is moot.

Blank Beat cells look like missing data (finding 62: Arráez, Caratini, Bolte): MOSTLY BY DESIGN. Blank only for the 32 hitters with no leaks. Their Top leak, Leak runs, Inches off and Count check cells are blank too, and their cards print no Target line (commit 0d64764). Only the missing glossary line holds.

Count note sentence means a switch hitter's table pools both batting sides (finding 493's reading): REFUTED as an interpretation. count_table runs on hand_view, which filters the hitter's pitches to that hand, and the avg column is the matched expectation for the same pitches. So 'both sides' means the you and avg columns, for every hitter. The sentence is still unclear and prints on every all-pitcher view, so the wording item holds.

Reference guide orientation (finding 496): REFUTED as an error. On the right-handed reference card, the guide's lefty sentence and the orient line's righty sentence ('A right-handed batter stands on the left, so inside is on the left.') are both true and together cover both cases. The 3D 'you' wording holds. 'This is the baseline every player card is compared against' is roughly true, since player cards compare pitch by pitch with the matched average: trivial.

Roster titled 'by team' (finding 495): WEAK. There is a Team filter and a Team column, so the title is defensible. It only fails to name the picked team, and the state line does that ('· NYY'). The footer-under-roster part holds (roster_1440_full.png).

Bare 'vs RHP' in Top leak (finding 489): holds only as unexplained. The label is correct: bare means 100% of the cell's pitches came from right-handers (step 17:508-516), and the glossary's 'when most of its pitches came from one' loosely covers it.

issues.statement: Confirmed, though part of it is by design. The flat hover prints a bold gap that has been shrunk toward zero, and under it the unshrunk smoothed rates, so the bold number is not their difference. The 3D view of the same spot prints a different 'you' (average + gap). Both rates are a local reading at the median of the chased pitches across all pitch types, so they differ from the leak row's whole-region rates for one pitch type. The Zone numbers panel defaults to all pitch types, so on 30 of 229 cards the region and count of the plan's first line read at or below average. For García's leak ① a reader can see four different pairs: plan 79/21, hover 94/23 '+50', 3D 73/23, Zone numbers 74/26.
evidence: García marker 1 hover (screenshot skeptic_picnums/garcia_tip.png): "+50 pts" / "Swings: you 94%, average 23%" / "about 7 nearby pitches, weighted" (94-23 = 71)

García, same spot in the 3D view (read from the page's Plotly text): "Swings: you 73%, average 23% (+50 pts)"; leak row: "79% vs 21% avg · 11 of 14"; plan: "You swung at 79% of them; hitters on average swing at 21%."; Zone numbers 'above the zone', Ahead: "74% / 26% (19)"

Each cell: chase rate, you then the average hitter on the same pitches") 'below the zone', Two strikes: "40% / 48% (72)"; with the page's Changeups filter the same panel reads "52% / 43% (25)"

García, Ohtani, Bohm 24%/30%, Beavers, Chapman, O. Cruz, Torkelson, Ewing, Tatís, Langeliers 36%/46%, Reynolds, Okamoto, Baty, Young, N. Lowe, Naylor, McMahon, Sheets, Soler, Mayo 25%/29%, Burger). issues.why_it_matters: A coach who hovers on the plan's marker, opens the 3D view (clicking a picture opens it) or opens the Zone numbers to show a hitter 'how much more you swing here' gets up to four different pairs for one spot. The bold '+50 pts' is not the 94% minus 23% printed under it. That makes the card hard to explain and hard to trust. Each piece is deliberate: the gap is shrunk for small samples, the marker sits at the median of the chased pitches, and the panel covers all pitch types. Putting them side by side without labels is not deliberate: the template comment claims the 3D view shows the same numbers as the flat picture. The plan's instruction survives because every pair points the same way. The exception is where the marked spot reads gray or blue: 35 first-line markers, 20 of them blue. That case belongs to the separate marker-on-gray/blue-spot pattern.
issues.root_cause: scripts/templates/card_surfaces.js:66-69: gap = extra/(weight + PRIOR_PITCHES), shrunk, while playerRate and leagueRate = observed/weight and expected/weight, unshrunk; so gap = (you-avg)·W/(W+3). player_cards.html:719-721: the flat tooltip prints the shrunk gap over the raw rates. player_cards.html:795-798: the 3D text uses you = leagueRate + gap, so it disagrees with the flat 'you', and the comment at line 766 claims they match. scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:482: the marker sits at the median of the chased pitches, and the picture counts every pitch type, so the spot reads higher than the leak's region-wide cell. player_cards.html:962-992 (note at 968): Zone numbers covers all pitch types unless the Pitches filter is set, and the note says only 'All pitchers.'
issues.suggested_fix: 1) In the flat tooltip (player_cards.html:720), print the same shrunk rate the 3D view uses, you = clamp(leagueRate + gap). Change the small line to 'about N nearby pitches, weighted; pulled toward average where pitches are few'. The bold gap then equals you minus average, and the flat and 3D views agree. Also fix the comment at line 766. 2) Under the leak list, add one sentence: 'A circled number marks where those chases were; the picture there counts every pitch type, so its rates differ from the leak's.' Filtering the picture to the leak's pitch type does not close the gap: the spot reads a median +19 points from the leak rate vs +11 with all pitches. 3) Change the Zone numbers note (line 968) to 'All pitchers, all pitch types. Pick a pitch type above to see a leak's own numbers.' With the filter set, the panel matches the leak rows (466 of 547 exact).
refuted_items: Finding 82's fix, 'Marked spots should show the leak's own pitch group', would not make the numbers agree. With the picture filtered to the leak's pitch type, the spot's 'you' moves further from the leak rate: median +19 points vs +11 with all pitches, and 459 vs 338 of 547 markers 10+ points off. The marker sits at the median of the chased pitches (step 17:482).

Finding 461 called it a 'contradiction', but the panel is right for what it covers. With the page's Pitches control set to the leak's type it reproduces the leak's numbers (Lane Thomas, Changeups: '52% / 43% (25)'; 466 of 547 exact). It is a labeling gap, not a wrong number. The count of 30/229 is confirmed exactly.

Finding 82's near-average-spot sub-claim holds (DeLuca +2, Caglianone +1 and +4, DeLauter marker 2 +2, Lee +2). Across all cards, 90 markers on 77 cards read +3 or less while their leak's rates are 5+ apart; 35 of those are the plan's first line, and 20 of the 35 read blue (e.g., Lane Thomas '−6 pts / Swings: you 48%, average 56%'). That is the marker-on-gray/blue-spot pattern, so it is listed for merging, not counted here.
No quoted number failed. All 22 marker quotes and Finding 215's '3D view would say you 80%' (page: 'Swings: you 80%, average 53% (+27 pts)') match the page.

issues.statement: Both parts hold, with some narrower claims refuted. (1) The no-target sentence says "with no change should be about at it in 2027" for any forecast that rounds to 2 or less, including 16 forecasts 2.6 to 8.6 points below the league. All 73 no-target sentences sit under a plan with a take line, and on the 13 of those without a framing line whose choices cost 1+ runs, it reads as "the problem fixes itself". (2) 103 of the 140 numbered targets grade a leak the plan leaves out (109 grade at least one leak the player is not told to take), and every one of those cards closes with "The only change(s) on this card...". On 17 cards those leaks carry half or more of the points.
evidence: Breakdown over all 261 cards (skeptic_target_argues2.py): 229 have a frozen target, 32 have none. 140 are numbered ('under N'), 73 say 'No target' or 'No chase target', and 16 are video-only ('No number to beat'). Affected: 73 no-target cards plus 109 numbered cards = 182. On every card the page's printed 'Target: ' text matches target_text (229 of 229).

Every reported card was re-checked against the data: the 30 numbered examples from batches 05, 07, 08, 11 and 13 all count an off-plan or video leak. In the dumped data, Perdomo, Alonso, Okamoto, McMahon, Chapman, García and Suzuki all have forecasts below -2.5, and Bregman, Wetherholt, Herrera, Swanson, Griffin, Díaz and Torkelson are all no-target cards under take plans.
issues.method: Read BRIEF.md, target_text, target_beat, leaks_named and keep_line in scripts/17_build_player_cards.py (lines 785-800 and 957-1030), step 19's prediction (scripts/19_freeze_leak_predictions.py: line 241, intercept -0.0383, slope 0.7195), the template's target and leak-note lines (930, 943-944), plan_checks.target_problems, and the 2026-10-17 evaluation's target items. I wrote skeptic_target_argues2.py over dump_2026.json for all 261 cards. It asserts each card's target equals the frozen hitter row in results/xchase/coaching/leak_predictions_2026.csv, and it checks the printed 'Target:' text on every card. For numbered targets it parses the counted leaks, matches them to the plan items' n and video flags, and splits the 2026 points into each leak's share using the frozen per-leak excess_2026 x pitches_2026 (the shares sum back to the printed excess within 0.15).
issues.why_it_matters: The no-target sentence is the card's last word on the leaks. Next to "let breaking balls below the zone go ... 71% vs 43%", "with no change should be about at it in 2027" tells a hitter the spot fixes itself and he need not act. That is the 10-17 "already" problem in softer words, and it is strongest on the 13 unframed losing-chooser cards like Griffin's. For a forecast of -6 to -9 the words are also false. On numbered cards, a player told "the only changes are the pitches above" is graded on leaks he was told to leave alone or to treat as video. On Ohtani, Cruz, Álvarez and Riley those leaks are nearly the whole number, so whether he passes depends mostly on spots the plan does not touch. The main instruction survives: the plan prints first and the target is small evidence text, so this is medium, not high. By design: the 2-point rule and the all-leaks pooling (step 19's freeze) are deliberate, and the 10-17 evaluation asked for the "with no change ... about at the league's rate" wording. "About at it" for negative forecasts is a side effect of a one-sided test.
issues.root_cause: scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:988 `if pred <= TARGET_MIN_PTS:` is a one-sided test (TARGET_MIN_PTS = 2 at :957), so every negative forecast takes the no-target branch. :997 then prints "with no change should be about at it in {nxt}." whatever the sign, and with no reason and nothing about the plan. :960-963 leaks_named and :1003-1006 grade "Leaks 1 to N together ... Under N is a fix" without saying which counted leaks are off the plan or video. keep_line at :795-796 says "The only change(s) on this card is/are the pitch(es) above." The pooling itself comes from step 19 (scripts/19_freeze_leak_predictions.py:241, one hitter row pooled over all card leaks, frozen 2026-10-14) and cannot be narrowed without breaking the freeze. The template prints the target right after the note "so it can leave a bigger one out" (scripts/templates/player_cards.html:943-944).
issues.suggested_fix: Change only the wording and leave the frozen numbers alone. (1) In target_text's no-target branch, pick the word by sign: "below it" when round(pred) < -TARGET_MIN_PTS, otherwise "about at it". Add the reason and that the plan still stands, e.g. "...; these spots drift back on their own, so a number could not tell a fix from luck. The pitch(es) above still cost you runs." (2) In the numbered branch, name the counted leaks the take plan does not cover, built from plan_items' n and is_video: "Leak 1 counts in the number but is not in your plan yet" / "leak 2 counts too, though it is for video". Or, on such cards, change keep_line's "The only changes on this card" to "The only changes to work on now". (3) Add plan_checks kinds for "about at it" with round(pred) < -2, and for a numbered target that counts a leak not on the take plan without naming it.
refuted_items: J. P. Crawford as a 'well below the league' example (batch_06): his forecast is -2.4, which rounds to -2, inside the 2-point band. 'About at it' is fair for him. Bregman (-2.2), Wetherholt (-2.3) and Díaz (-2.2) are the same: valid 1b examples, not 1a.

Ohtani, batch_08: 'He can beat the number only by doing what the plan says not to treat as a rule.' Refuted. The forecast of 5 already assumes no change on every leak, so any drop on leak 1 (the plan's take line, 66% of the pooled pitches) puts the pooled number under 5 in expectation. What holds is that 12.1 of the 12.1 points are the video item's.

batch_07: 'a player who follows the plan exactly can miss the target because of pitches he was never told to take.' True only as noise, not bias. Off-plan leaks are forecast to regress like the rest, so they dilute the plan's effect and add variance; they do not stack the target against him.

Off-plan leaks that are counted but add no points: Holliday (leak 3: -1.1), Rafaela (leak 2: -0.5), Harper (leak 3: 0.3), Brooks Lee (leak 3: 0.7), McNeil (leak 2: 0.9). Including them is true but does not change the number; only the wording confuses.

1b's 'argues with the plan' reading on 57 of the 73 no-target cards: a framing line there already says the plan is 'spots to tighten, not a new approach', which the sentence agrees with. The undercut is clear on the 16 unframed cards, 13 of them with choices of -1 runs or worse.

Part 2 as a fix to the target's scope: cannot be done. Step 19 froze one pooled row per hitter (2026-10-14) and refuses to rewrite it, and its line was fit on pooled leaks. Only the wording can change. The 10-17 evaluation raised 'these spots are not the plan's spots' (105 of 149), and naming the leaks (1ac1871) resolved only part of it.

'N points below the league's chase rate in 2026' beside a leak list showing the hitter above the league (Perdomo: '49% vs 46% avg' vs '4 points below'; Okamoto: '51% vs 49% avg' vs '7 points below') is the known open item on target-scale points, not part of this issue.

issues.statement: This one holds up. On the vs RHP and vs LHP tabs, three kinds of sentence are built from the all-pitchers summary: the framing line, the contact line/clause (its miss rates, its runs and its "not choices"/"bigger issue" verdict), and the fastball clause in the keep line. The pitch lines, the strength clause, the spread lines and the fallback lines on the same tab use that hand's table. So 126 of 261 cards print a hand-tab number that differs from the tab's own By count table. On 23 cards the sentence's verdict is the opposite of what the tab's table shows. The worst cases are 6 hand tabs whose only plan line says contact is the problem while that tab shows contact as a plus.
evidence: Luis Rengifo, vs LHP tab (rendered aside): "Overall your chase choices are better than average (+2.6 runs a season): the pitch above is one spot to tighten, not a new approach." The same tab's By count table shows "All counts 274 38%29% 30%21% 33%44% .291.309 −4.7 +1.2". The ahead count (−1.0), 0-1/1-1 (−0.8) and two strikes (−2.8) are all losses. The +2.6 is the header bar "Choices +2.6", which is the vs RHP +7.3 plus the vs LHP −4.7.

Cam Smith, vs LHP, the tab's only line: "Your bigger issue is contact: you miss on 49% of your chases, against 42% for other hitters on the same pitches." Tab total (341 pitches): misses 40% / 40%, choices −0.9, contact +3.0.

Josh Jung, vs LHP, the only line: "Your issue is contact, not choices: you miss about as often as other hitters do, but what you hit on a chase goes nowhere (over a season your chases cost you 2 runs more than an average hitter's would)." Tab total: misses 31% / 38%, choices +1.8, contact +1.1.

Kyle Manzardo, vs LHP, the only line: "...you miss about as often as other hitters do, but what you hit on a chase goes nowhere (over a season your chases cost you 5 runs more than an average hitter's would)." Tab total: misses 63% / 52% (11 points more), contact +0.6.

Josh Jung, vs RHP: the first line is "Your issue is contact, not choices", and the frame line says "Overall your chase choices are about average (+0.3 runs a season)". The tab's total shows choices −1.5 and 0-1/1-1 at −1.8.
Heliot Ramos, vs RHP: "Your issue is contact, not choices" and "Overall your chase choices are about average (+0.4 runs a season)". The tab shows choices −1.4 in total and −2.9 ahead in the count.
Jake Burger, vs RHP, contact clause: "You miss on 56% of your chases, against 46% ...: contact is your bigger cost". The tab shows choices −5.8 against contact −4.3, and misses 57% / 47%.

issues.method: Read plan_items() and its helpers in scripts/17_build_player_cards.py (lines 560-850, 1036-1070), the hand-tab label and the header() tiles in scripts/templates/player_cards.html, and problems()/plan_problems() in scripts/plan_checks.py. Wrote skeptic_handtab/sweep.py and final.py, which run over all 261 players and 522 hand tabs in dump_2026.json. For each tab they compare the framing-line runs, miss rates, 'goes nowhere' runs, the contact verdict and head, the 0.0 clause and the fastball clause against the tab's own 'total' row and its leak list. Also ran controls: the all-pitchers view; whether R+L equals all; fallback lines that use 'overall' for the tab's own total. skeptic_handtab/show.py prints the full tab text and tables for each example. A check showed the rendered aside text contains every plan_items_by_hand text (0 mismatches).
issues.why_it_matters: The tab says its plan is "for this pitcher hand only", and that hand's By count table sits directly under the sentence. A coach working the left-hander matchup with Rengifo reads "better than average... not a new approach" over a −4.7 total against left-handers. On Cam Smith's, Jung's and Manzardo's LHP tabs, the only instruction blames contact while the table shows contact as a gain against that hand. The same tab also uses "overall" for the season in the framing line and for this hand in its fallback lines, so an analyst gets two numbers for one thing and stops trusting the sentence. The pitch lines on these tabs are correct and the advice in the contact line is harmless, which is why this is medium and not high. The 6 contact-only tabs are the high-leaning subset, because there the table contradicts the tab's one instruction.
issues.root_cause: scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:1067 passes the all-pitchers summary into plan_items for each hand tab: plan_items(summary["leaks"][h], summary, summary["tables"][h], view=h). Inside plan_items, five things read that summary instead of the tab's rows: framing_line (:763-782, stored(summary["choices"]) and far_off_zero(summary)); contact_why/contact_line/contact_clause (:710-738, summary whiff, whiff_league, contact and choices); the contact_led gate (:823, summary["archetype"]); and keep_line (:798, summary["fastball_choices"]). strength_clause, spread_line and fallback_line read the tab's rows. plan_checks.py:138 and :252-255 test the hand-tab framing against player["choices"], so the check endorses the mismatch.
issues.suggested_fix: In step 17, give hand tabs their own numbers. Compute summary["fastball_by_hand"][h] in the summary loop. In plan_items, when view != "all", build s = dict(summary, choices=t["choices"], contact=t["contact"], whiff=t["whiff"], whiff_league=t["whiff_league"], fastball_choices=summary["fastball_by_hand"][view]) from the tab's total row t, and pass s to framing_line, contact_line, contact_clause and keep_line. Gate the contact line and clause on the tab: contact_led and t["contact"] < 0 and t["contact"] < t["choices"]. A tab whose own contact is a plus then falls through to fallback_line ("Nothing stands out" for Cam Smith L, Jung L and Edman R, and the costly-count line for Gonzales L). Drop the "0.0 at the top" clause on hand tabs, or say "against all pitchers", because no per-hand far-off cost is printed. Word the hand framing as "Against left-handers your chase choices are ...". Then make plan_checks.problems() pass the hand's totals for each tab, so 'framing misquoted' and 'good chooser unframed' check the tab's own number. Minimal alternative: keep the season numbers but say "Against all pitchers" in each borrowed clause, and skip the contact line on any tab whose own contact is 0 or better.
refuted_items: 'the 0.0 at the top' on 70 cards is not a contradiction. The count holds (83 tabs, 70 cards), but the clause points at the header tile, which never changes with the tab and does print 0.0. The tab's own far-off rate is within 2 points of league on 82 of 83 such tabs; the one exception is Max Muncy vs LHP, 23% vs 21%. This is a low-severity scope label. Antonacci's two-strike far-off 45%/29% vs LHP is a single count; his tab total is 19%/19%.

Of the 'fastball decisions are a strength over a fastball leak' cases, the 6 on hand tabs (Wells, Murakami, Pages, Taveras, Adell, Mayo vs RHP) are not specific to hand tabs. The same thing happens on 10 all-pitchers views (Troy Johnston, Swanson, Bazzana, Murakami, Pages, Hao-Yu Lee, Ramos, Josh Lowe, Brandon Lowe, Ty France), because keep_line looks at the plan lines and never at the leak list. Each hand's fastball runs are not in the page data, so the hand-level claim cannot be checked from the page. Report this as a separate pattern.

Reviewer i=0 said Conine vs LHP should get the choices fallback. With the tab's numbers no count costs 1+ run (the worst is 0-1/1-1 at −0.8), so the rules would print 'Nothing stands out'. The tab also does show him missing more, 46% vs 37%. Only 'bigger issue is contact' is false there: contact +0.8 against choices −1.7.

Edman vs RHP is weaker than reported. The tab shows misses of 47% vs 41%, so 'you miss more' still holds against right-handers. His contact runs there are +0.1 (neutral). What is wrong is the quoted 49%/43% and the existence of a contact line at all; under the rules the tab would print 'Nothing stands out'.

The reported counts mostly hold, with corrections. The framing is off by 1+ run or has the opposite sign on 81 cards (94 tabs, not 93). The miss rate differs from the tab's on 31 cards and 58 tabs, not 26 cards. 'Goes nowhere' runs differ on 12 cards (holds). Direction contradictions: 23 cards, not 22, once the fastball items (not specific to hand tabs) are left out and the 'not choices', 'about as often' and miss-gap cases are counted. Total cards with a misquoted number: 126, not 125.

Most framing differences are magnitude only. Every hand table uses the season's per-600-PA scale, so R + L equals the all-pitchers total on all 261 cards. The framing line prints the sum of both tabs, and the hand's part is naturally smaller. Examples: Crawford +17.3 vs +8.9, Walls +11.9 vs +3.2, Mullins 'cost you 4 runs' vs −2.6 and −1.8, Paredes R +3.4 vs +3.9, Freeman +0.5 vs +0.4. These are confusing, not reversed. The verdict changes on only 23 tabs, and average-or-better sits over a tab loss of 1+ run on 10.

The borrowed numbers are real, not fabricated. The framing number matches the header's 'Where the runs go · all chases' Choices bar on every card, so a careful reader can reconcile it. That is why this is medium rather than high: the main all-pitchers plan and the tab's pitch lines are unaffected.

High severity overall is not sustained. The contact line's instruction ('a pitch that is clearly off is a take even when you could reach it') does not lead a player to a wrong action. The high-leaning part is limited to 6 of the 38 contact-only hand tabs (Cam Smith L, Jung L, Manzardo L, Conine L, Edman R, Conforto L; Conforto's tab has 21 pitches), where the tab's only line rests on a premise its own table refutes.

issues.statement: The counts hold exactly. 39 of 229 all-pitchers first lines (each one also the roster's Start with) rest on a leak of fewer than 20 pitches, 68 on fewer than 25, and 21 on fewer than 10 chases. 83 cards open a hand-tab plan on fewer than 20 pitches. 119 cards have a plan line under 20 pitches somewhere, and 171 have one at 25 or under. 31 of the 39 small first lines are not leak 1: they are pre-two-strike cells that the take-first order moved up. In 20 cards (13 more on the vs RHP tab) that pushes a leak with twice the pitches and more runs off the plan entirely. The project's own backtest says only leaks under 20 pitches are mostly noise. Leaks of 20 to 25 pitches repeat about as well as bigger ones. So the problem is real under 20 pitches and overstated for 20 to 25.
evidence: Mayo, All pitchers, plan line 1: "When you're ahead in the count, let changeups and splitters below the zone go. You swung at 50% of them; hitters on average swing at 28%." It comes from leak 3 "Ahead in the count, changeups / splitters below the zone 50% vs 28% avg · 6 of 12 −0.9", ahead of leak 1 "Two strikes, breaking balls below the zone 59% vs 51% avg · 35 of 59 −2.6". Leak 2 "17 of 25 −1.3" is off the plan

Carroll, All pitchers: leak 1 "Two strikes, breaking balls below the zone 76% vs 47% avg · 31 of 41 −2.8" (8.5 in off) has no plan line. Line 1 comes from "Ahead in the count, mostly vs RHP, breaking balls below the zone 58% vs 32% avg · 11 of 19". Leak 1 is also left off for Ramírez (37 of 60, −3.1; line 1 from 9 of 15), Cowser (37 of 56, −4.0; line 1 from 14 of 21) and Jared Young (15 of 27, −2.0; line 1 from 7 of 12)

Trout's roster Start with: "When you're ahead in the count, let breaking balls below the zone go (56% vs 26%, 6 in off)". No pitch count; the card's leak row is "9 of 16", against leak 1's "26 of 49"

Luis García's coach note leads with an 11-of-14 cell: "When he is ahead in the count, fastballs above the zone: the plan's first line." Moniak's note (11 of 18): "is the bigger leak; fix the early one first."
