The only caveat, under every leak list: "the plan takes up to two, in the order to work on them, so it can leave a bigger one out." No plan line, note or roster cell mentions sample size (grep of the template and step 17: 'too few pitches' is used only for the pictures)

Backtest (results/xchase/coaching/leak_backtest_pairs.csv, the 530 hitter pairs with a single card leak, seasons and halves): leaks under 20 pitches (n=228) went from 15.7 points above the league to 2.4 ± 1.0 the next period, 15% kept, slope 0.37. Leaks of 20-25 pitches (n=95) went from 12.9 to 6.7 ± 1.5, 52% kept, slope 0.58. Leaks of 25+ pitches: slope 0.85

Leak size by count, all-pitchers leaks: ahead-count leaks median 23 pitches, 34% under 20. Two-strike leaks median 44 pitches, 5% under 20. The take-before-two-strikes order therefore promotes the smallest cells
The card opens on the small first line's picture in 39 of 39 cases. The picture at its marker is not faded (evidence 0.64-0.96)
issues.method: I wrote scripts in scratchpad/audit/skeptic_tiny/ that run over dump_2026.json for all 261 players and all three views. sweep.py counts plan lines by leak pitches and chases, step-1 lines, promotions, displaced leaks, plans whose only line is small, and plan totals. leak1off.py finds plans that leave leak 1 off. markers.py and markers2.py check the opening picture and the picture's evidence and gap at each marker. reported.py and check_quotes.py check every reported card and 210 quoted "N of M" samples against the plan items. persist.py and persist2.py test whether small leaks repeat, using the project's own leak_backtest_pairs.csv (single-leak pairs, so a pair's pitch count is that leak's own). I read the code in leak_rules.py (leak_cells, LEAK_MIN_PITCHES) and in step 17 (plan_pitch_items, pitch_line, start_with, plan_items), the template's leak-list caption, coach-note leads in the dump, and the README backtest section.
issues.why_it_matters: The first line is what a player works on first and what coaches see as the roster's Start with. For 39 hitters that line rests on a cell whose extra chasing mostly vanishes the next period, by the project's own backtest (15% kept). The session goes to noise while a well-measured leak waits at step 2 or drops off the plan, as Carroll's 31-of-41 two-strike breaking ball 8.5 inches off does. It also costs trust: when 6 of 12 turns into 2 of 12 next year, the card looks wrong. It is not a wrong action, though. Every take line is for pitches typically 4+ inches off the zone, so the harm is priority and displacement, which is why I rate it medium. The 20-card displacement subset (four with leak 1 off the plan entirely) is the strongest case for high. It is by design in part: the take-first order and the 12-pitch floor are deliberate (step 17 lines 631-635: "a take before two strikes can put a smaller leak on the plan ahead of a bigger two-strike one"). But no guard on sample size was designed, and the generic "can leave a bigger one out" is the only caveat. A separate issue, not part of this one: the frozen target line (slope 0.72) probably overpredicts small-cell leaks. Roughly 7.5 points predicted against 2.4 actual under 20 pitches in the backtest, so those targets could be beaten with no change.
issues.root_cause: scripts/leak_rules.py:52 sets LEAK_MIN_PITCHES = 12, and :137 keeps a cell on its raw rate with no shrinkage, while the count check is shrunk. scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:639 in plan_pitch_items sorts rest.sort(key=lambda it: (it[1]["count_group"] == "two", it[1]["choices"])), so any pre-two-strike leak leads whatever its sample. :546 PLAN_LINES = 2 lets that small cell push a bigger leak off the plan. pitch_line (:616-628) and start_with (:853-866) print rates but never the pitch count. The coach-note leads (note_start) for Luis García, Mickey Moniak and Colson Montgomery pin a small cell first.
issues.suggested_fix: Leave LEAK_MIN_PITCHES at 12. It is shared with steps 16 and 19, and the frozen 2026 targets count leaks 1-3. Change step 17 only. (1) In plan_pitch_items, let a pre-two-strike leak go ahead of a two-strike one only when it has at least 20 pitches (new PLAN_LEAD_MIN_PITCHES = 20); otherwise order by runs. Mayo, Carroll, Burleson and Ramírez would then lead with their 41-76-pitch leaks. (2) When a plan line's leak has fewer than 20 pitches, have pitch_line add "Only N of these pitches so far: a small sample, so check it on video before it becomes a rule", and have start_with append "N pitches". On a hand tab, do not make such a leak the tab's only firm rule without that clause. (3) Add a plan_checks.py guard: a first line on a leak under 20 pitches while the list holds one with twice its pitches. (4) Re-check the García, Moniak and Montgomery note leads, or back them by pooling all pre-two-strike counts, as Hunter Goodman's note already does ("48% of the time against 30%... about 5 runs").
refuted_items: 'Nothing on the card warns' only partly holds. Every leak row prints its sample ('11 of 16'). The plan line, the coach's note and the roster's Start with never show it, and no text calls a sample small

'12 to 25 pitches is tiny' does not hold for 20-25. In the backtest, 20-25-pitch leaks keep 52% of their excess (6.7 ± 1.5 of 12.9 points, n=95), similar to 25-40 (39%). Only under 20 pitches do they collapse (15%). The brief's 15-25 band should read 'under 20'

High severity as 'makes him do the wrong thing' does not hold. Every take line is for chased pitches typically 4+ inches off (CLEARLY_OFF_IN), and 17 of the 103 small all-view lines are labeled video items, not take rules. The harm is what gets worked on first and the bigger leak dropped, not a wrong swing decision

The 'moved ahead by the order rule' argument does not apply to the 14 cards whose only leak is small (Tawa 11 of 16, Loftin 10 of 15, Kirk 12 of 14, Langford 9 of 17 and others) or to the 8 where the small cell is itself leak 1 (for example García 11 of 14). Those are small-sample plans, but nothing was promoted

The pictures neither warn nor contradict more often for small leaks. A step-1 marker sits on a spot under +5 points in 7 of 39 small leaks against 36 of 158 big ones. Mayo's blue spot (gap −4) is real, but it is the general marker issue, not specific to small samples

The reviewers' quotes are accurate. All 210 checkable 'N of M' quotes are plan-line samples on the named card; the one other quote, Burleson's '53 of 72', is correctly given as off the plan. All 167 reported cards have a plan line at 25 pitches or under. Four more cards also qualify but were not reported: Jeff McNeil (first line 8 of 14), Willy Adames, Jake Mangum and Jarren Duran

issues.statement: On the vs RHP and vs LHP tabs, each plan line's circled "leak N" tag numbers that hand's own leak list. The pictures are not redrawn when the tab changes, so their circled markers and the selected outline still show the all-pitchers leaks. On 117 cards, 166 of the 456 hand-tab pitch lines carry a tag N where marker N on the pictures is a different pitch, count or row (151 lines), or where no marker N exists (15 lines). That includes 104 of the 289 hand-tab first lines. In another 11 lines (5 more cards) the marker is the same pitch but sits on the other hand's row or the other batting side's row. The tag's tooltip, the reference card's guide and step 17's docstring all say the number is the one on the pictures.
evidence: Salvador Pérez, vs RHP tab (shots/skeptic/salvador_perez_1440_tabR.png): plan step 1 "At 0-1 or 1-1, let breaking balls down and away go. You swung at 40% of them; hitters on average swing at 17%." is tagged "leak 3", and the list shows "3 0-1 or 1-1 vs RHP, breaking balls down and away". The only circled 3 on the pictures is on All pitchers / 0-1 or 1-1, below the zone, which is all-pitchers leak 3 "0-1 or 1-1, breaking balls below the zone". The vs RHP 0-1 or 1-1 picture has no marker, and the outline stays on All pitchers 0-1 or 1-1 (selected key 0|even before and after the click).

Brandon Marsh, vs RHP tab (shots/skeptic/brandon_marsh_1440_tabR.png): step 1 "When you're ahead in the count, let breaking balls below the zone go." is tagged "leak 3". On the vs RHP row, the ahead-count breaking-ball spot is marked 2 and the 3 sits on the vs RHP Two strikes picture (all-pitchers "Two strikes, mostly vs RHP, changeups / splitters below the zone"). The tab's list says "2 Two strikes vs RHP, changeups / splitters below the zone" and "3 Ahead in the count vs RHP, breaking balls below the zone", so 2 and 3 are swapped on the same row.

Gabriel Moreno, vs LHP tab (shots/skeptic/gabriel_moreno_1440_tabL.png): "With two strikes, let breaking balls below the zone go." is tagged "leak 1". The All pitchers list reads "None worth 0.75 runs per 600 PA.", so the card draws no marker anywhere.

Geraldo Perdomo (switch hitter), vs LHP tab (shots/skeptic/geraldo_perdomo_1440_tabL.png): the leak tagged "leak 1" is "Two strikes vs LHP, breaking balls below the zone", which he hits batting right. Marker 1 and the outline stay on the "Batting left, mostly vs RHP" Two strikes picture.

Jac Caglianone, vs LHP: leak 1 "Two strikes vs LHP, breaking balls below the zone". Marker 1 is drawn on the vs RHP row, because all-pitchers leak 1 is "Two strikes, mostly vs RHP, breaking balls below the zone".

DOM after clicking the hand-R or hand-L radio on all 4 cards: the first #zgrid canvas is the same element before and after (sameCanvas true), so the pictures are not redrawn. Each tag's title reads "This line's leak, numbered on the pictures and in the list below". The hand tab's caption reads "Ranked by what the choices cost, per 600 PA; the plan takes up to two...", without the all-view's "Numbered on the pictures, on the row of the hand a leak names."
The tag and the list numbers are drawn as circled digits in the same style as the picture markers (visible in the Pérez and Marsh shots), which invites matching them.

Reference card guide: "Numbers on the pictures match the leaks list ... each tagged with its leak's number." The step 17 plan_items docstring says n is "the leak's number on the list and the pictures (n, printed as a small tag)".

Sweep (skeptic_handtags.py over dump_2026.json): 166 of 456 hand-tab pitch lines are off. In 79, the tagged pitch is a different marker number. In 72, the tagged pitch has no marker and the tag points at an unrelated one. In 15, marker N does not exist. 104 of 289 first lines are off, on 91 cards. In 11 more lines, the marker is the same pitch on the wrong hand's row or batting side (Perdomo, Rutschman, Walls, Heim, Brooks Lee, Taveras, Raleigh, Carrigg, Caglianone), for 177 lines on 122 cards in all. 14 of the 29 switch hitters are affected.

Selected outline: on 84 of the 289 hand tabs that have a pitch line, the outlined picture is in a different count than the tab's first line (e.g. Mike Trout vs RHP: first line is two strikes, outline stays on "All pitchers, Ahead in the count").

The leak lists themselves (no plan tag): 223 of 545 hand-tab list rows, on 129 cards, carry a number whose picture marker is a different leak or does not exist. The hand caption does not claim these numbers are on the pictures, but the guide and the matching circled style do.
issues.method: I read the template code. zones() at scripts/templates/player_cards.html:655-676 places markers from p.leaks.all. Lines 748-752 pick the selected picture from the all-pitchers plan. The hand radio handler at line 1181 calls only aside() and stateLine(). The tag's title is at line 927 and the hand-tab caption at line 943. I also read plan_items() in step 17 (lines 803-820, 1067). I wrote skeptic_handtags.py, skeptic_handtags2.py and skeptic_handtags3.py in the audit folder and ran them over dump_2026.json. They check: markers per card equal leaks.all on all 261 cards, and none are undrawn. For every hand-tab pitch line, the tag's leak cell (count, pitch, region, batting side) is compared with leaks.all[n-1], with each mismatch classified. Hand list rows, the selected key against the hand-tab first line, and the 118 reported cards were checked against the sweep set. I took fresh 1440px screenshots with shot_layout.mjs (Pérez R, Marsh R, Moreno L, Perdomo L) and probed the DOM after clicking: canvas identity, the selected key, tag titles and the caption.
issues.why_it_matters: Coaches go over the card with the player in the room. On a hand tab, the plan's "leak ③" and the list's ③ look exactly like the circled ③ on the pictures, and the tag's own hover text says the number is there. Following it lands on a different pitch, count or row, or on nothing. The words of each plan line are correct and match the list below, so the instruction itself survives. Even so, the card contradicts itself and the picture can point a player at the wrong location. In the 151 different-leak lines, the marker is another real leak of his, so the harm is confusion, not a harmful instruction. That is why this is medium, not high. Keeping the pictures fixed on a hand tab is deliberate: the handler skips zones(), and the hand caption leaves out "Numbered on the pictures". The tag pointing at a different marker is not deliberate, since the tooltip, the guide and the docstring all claim the opposite.
issues.root_cause: scripts/templates/player_cards.html:664: zones() draws markers only from p.leaks.all. Lines 748-752: the outline follows p.plan_items (the all view). Line 1181: the hand control re-renders only aside() and stateLine(), never zones(). Lines 922-927: aside() tags hand-tab lines with it.n from p.plan_items_by_hand[hand], which step 17 (17_build_player_cards.py:1067, plan_items over summary["leaks"][h]) numbers within that hand's list, and gives the tag the title "numbered on the pictures". Line 943 drops the pictures sentence only from the hand caption. The guide text at 17_build_player_cards.py:1993 still says "Numbers on the pictures match the leaks list". The print card is not affected: it uses the all-view plan only.
issues.suggested_fix:
Redraw the pictures for the tab, using the template's existing row logic.
(1) Hand handler at line 1181: `state.hand = r.value; state.selFor = null; if (lastRender) { zones(lastRender); aside(lastRender); stateLine(lastRender); }`
(2) zones() at line 664: iterate `(p.leaks[state.hand] || [])` instead of `p.leaks.all`. Hand leaks carry hand = "R"/"L", so the existing lookup puts them on the vs RHP or vs LHP row. For a switch hitter it falls back to his batting side's row (lk.side), which is the right one.
(3) Selection at lines 749-750: take `items = state.hand === "all" ? p.plan_items : (p.plan_items_by_hand[state.hand] || [])` and `L = p.leaks[state.hand] || []`, then `lk = first ? L[first.n - 1] : L[0]`.
(4) Put "Numbered on the pictures, on the vs RHP row" (or "on your batting side's row" for a switch hitter) back into the hand caption.
A cheaper fallback, if the pictures must stay fixed: on hand tabs, drop the circled number, or print the all-pitchers number when the cell is in leaks.all and no number otherwise, and change the tooltip to "numbered in the list below". A check in plan_checks.py could confirm that each hand-tab tag's cell is the cell drawn for that number.
refuted_items: Nine reported cards have no hand-tab plan line whose tag points at a wrong marker. Kody Clemens, Griffin Conine, Pete Crow-Armstrong, Ildemaro Vargas and Coby Mayo: every plan tag matches its marker's pitch. Only a hand-list row number differs (e.g. Clemens vs RHP list 3 is changeups while marker 3 is ahead fastballs), and the hand caption does not claim those are picture numbers. That is the weaker list-level form (223 rows, 129 cards).

Geraldo Perdomo: tag 1 is the same pitch as marker 1, not a different leak. The marker sits on the other batting side's row (Batting left, mostly vs RHP), so it holds only as the switch-side variant. Rutschman, Walls, Heim, Brooks Lee and Caglianone vs LHP are the same kind of case.

Drew Gilbert, Nico Hoerner and J. P. Crawford: there is no mismatched tag. Their vs RHP tab has no leak, or fewer leaks, while an all-pitchers "mostly vs RHP" leak's marker sits on the vs RHP row. That is a different issue (all view vs hand tab). Hoerner's vs RHP plan reads "Nothing to change..." while his all-view first line is "0-1 or 1-1, mostly vs RHP, breaking balls below the zone", and Julio Rodríguez's all-view first line "Ahead in the count vs RHP, breaking balls down and away" is missing from his vs RHP tab. Both belong to that other issue type.

Severity high (batches 03 and layout): not upheld. The plan's words name the pitch, count and location correctly and match the list below. Following the tag lands on another real leak of his (151 lines) or on no marker (15). The main instruction survives, so medium.
Counts: the claim of 117 cards and 166 of 456 lines (151 different, 15 none) and 104 hand-tab first lines reproduces exactly. Marker lengths equal leaks.all on all 261 cards, with no undrawn markers.
Cards hit but not in the reported list: Carson Benge, Jazz Chisholm, Jo Adell, Luis Rengifo, Max Muncy, Ryan McMahon, Samuel Basallo, Tristan Peters.

A separate issue spotted while checking: the coach's note shows unchanged on hand tabs and can name a different first line. Pérez vs RHP reads "At 0-1 or 1-1, breaking balls below the zone: the plan's first line" while that tab's first line is "breaking balls down and away".

issues.statement: The issue holds, and it is wider than reported. Each pitcher-hand tab rebuilds its leaks and plan on its own. On 75 of 261 cards a tab's plan has a line from a leak the All pitchers list never shows and the pictures never mark, and on 51 cards that line comes first. On 66 cards the All pitchers first line is on neither tab's plan, and on 5 a near-tie sorts the same two leaks the other way. On 23 cards one view gives a pitch line while another says there is nothing to work on. The tab's "leak N" tags are numbered from a different list than the picture markers.
evidence: Counts over 261 cards (skeptic_tabdiff/*.py): 105 tab leaks on 90 cards are not on the All list. 83 of them are tab plan lines (75 cards), and 54 are a tab's step 1 (51 cards). 12 cards have a tab-only leak bigger than every All leak: Lukes, Caminero, Palacios, Rocchio, Adames, Bohm, Yandy Díaz, Suárez, Iván Herrera, Moreno, McGonigle, Antonacci. On 124 tabs (99 cards) the first line differs from the All view's. The All first line is on neither tab's plan on 66 cards. There are 5 pure order flips.

Lukes vs RHP list: '(1) Two strikes vs RHP, changeups / splitters below the zone 83% vs 54% avg · 24 of 29 −3.3'. Plan: '(2) With two strikes, let changeups and splitters below the zone go. You swung at 83% of them'. The All list tops out at '(1) Two strikes, mostly vs RHP, fastballs above the zone ... −1.9' and never names this pitch. Data: R1 choices −3.287, contact +3.12 (net −0.17).

skeptic_tabdiff/lukes_vsRHP.png: on the vs RHP tab, plan line 2 carries the tag 'leak 1' (changeups below), but marker 1 on the vs RHP Two strikes picture sits above the zone (the All view's fastball leak). Line 1 carries the tag 'leak 3', while its outlined picture has marker 2. The tag's tooltip says 'This line's leak, numbered on the pictures and in the list below'. Across all cards, 151 tab plan lines on 105 cards have a tag N that names a different leak than picture marker N.

Caminero vs RHP: '(1) With two strikes, let fastballs above the zone go. You swung at 88% of them; hitters on average swing at 49%.' The All view lists only two breaking-ball leaks (−1.5, −1.5). R1 net −0.33.
Palacios vs RHP: '(1) Two strikes vs RHP, breaking balls below the zone · 74% vs 55% avg · 28 of 38 · −2.5'. Data: choices −2.502, contact +2.494 (net −0.008). The All view lists one leak, '−1.3'.

Moreno, All: 'Nothing to change. You chase more than most hitters with two strikes (52% against 42%), but those swings have paid...'. vs LHP tab: 'With two strikes, let breaking balls below the zone go. You swung at 88% of them' (17 pitches, net −0.05). Antonacci, All: 'Nothing stands out. Your chase choices are about league average or better in every count.' vs LHP tab: 'With two strikes, let breaking balls off the plate away go. You swung at 85% of them' (13 pitches).

France, All (1): 'At 0-1 or 1-1, mostly against left-handers, let changeups and splitters below the zone go.' vs LHP tab: 'No single pitch stands out. Your chase choices are about average overall (-1.4 runs a season)...'. vs RHP closing line: 'Nothing on this card is a take rule for you yet: the staff takes the pitches above to video with you first.' 10 tabs print that sentence while the All view has a take.

Jung Hoo Lee, All (1): 'When you're ahead, mostly against right-handers, let breaking balls below the zone go.' vs RHP tab: 'Nothing to change. You chase more than most hitters with two strikes (48% against 41%)...' and 'None worth 0.75 runs per 600 PA.' The outlined picture is the vs RHP Ahead picture, which carries marker 2 (skeptic_tabdiff/lee_vsRHP.png).

Julio, All (1): 'When you're ahead against right-handers, let breaking balls down and away go. You swung at 59% of them; hitters on average swing at 16%.' The vs RHP tab never mentions it. All three of its leaks are two-strike (−2.8, −1.3, −1.2), and the same 17 pitches (−1.12) miss the three-leak cap by 0.05 runs, even though the tab's By count shows Ahead −3.3, its costliest count (skeptic_tabdiff/julio_vsRHP.png).

Reynolds, All (1): 'When you're ahead in the count, let breaking balls below the zone go.' Both tabs: 'Nothing stands out. Your chase choices are about league average or better in every count.' 16 cards have All-view pitch lines and none on either tab. Including Moreno-type cases and hand-named lines, 23 cards have one view with a line and another saying there is nothing to do.

The same note sits on every tab: 'The plan for this pitcher hand only; pick All pitchers for the full plan.' It calls the All view the full plan even when the tab leads with a leak that view does not list.

Carroll, All: '(1) When you're ahead, mostly against right-handers, let breaking balls below the zone go' / '(2) At 0-1 or 1-1, mostly against right-handers, let changeups and splitters...'. vs RHP: '(1) At 0-1 or 1-1, let changeups and splitters below the zone go' / '(2) When you're ahead in the count...'. Choices are −1.100 vs −1.095 on All and −1.01 vs −1.114 on RHP. The other pure flips are Grissom, Altuve, Buxton and Giménez.
issues.method: Python scripts in scratchpad/audit/skeptic_tabdiff (measure.py, buckets.py, reverse.py, numbers.py, keepline.py, union.py) run over dump_2026.json for all 261 cards. Each compares leak cells and plan cells between leaks/plan_items and leaks[h]/plan_items_by_hand[h]. They also check the leak tag number against the All-list index, which is what the picture markers use, and check the tab closing lines and fallbacks. I read step 17 leaks(), plan_pitch_items() and plan_items_by_hand, leak_rules.leak_cells, the template's zones()/aside(), and plan_checks.py. I checked each reported example against the card text and the underlying data. Screenshots of the vs RHP tabs for Lukes, Jung Hoo Lee and Julio came from skeptic_tabdiff/shot_tab.mjs, a copy of shot.mjs that clicks the tab.
refuted_items: 'With no note on why' only half holds. Every tab prints 'The plan for this pitcher hand only; pick All pitchers for the full plan.' There is a note, but it gives no reason, and 'full plan' is wrong in these cases.

Royce Lewis (LHP line 1 = All leak 1), Lindor (RHP line 1 = All leak 2), Riley (RHP line 2 = All leak 2), Mayo (RHP line 2 = All leak 2), Taveras (tab lines = All leak 2) and Trout (RHP line 2 = All leak 2): these lines ARE on the All list and drawn on the pictures. Only the order rule left them off the All plan, and the card says it can do that. 'Never lists or marks' does not hold for them.

Salvador Pérez: the tab's '0-1 or 1-1, breaking balls down and away' is the neighbouring region of the All plan's '0-1 or 1-1, breaking balls below the zone'. That is nearly the same instruction, not a contradiction. Francisco Álvarez is the same pitch (fastballs above the zone) one count group over, so it is mild.
Mayo's 'Two strikes vs RHP, fastballs above the zone −1.0', Taveras's tab (3) and Iván Herrera's bigger RHP leak are on the tab's leak list only, never a tab plan line. Low.

Joe Mack's reversed order, and the Murakami, Guerrero, Hoskins and Brooks Lee flips, come from a leak being a take on one view and a video item on the other. That is a separate take/video flip issue, not this tie-order cause. Pure order flips are 5 cards (Carroll, Grissom, Altuve, Buxton, Giménez). They are near-ties, so low severity.

The causes are inferred, not proven. Raleigh 'cut by the three-leak cap' and Lukes/Palacios 'rescued by the other hand's contact' fit the data: Raleigh's RHP part is −1.59 against an All third leak of −1.99; Lukes nets −0.17 and Palacios −0.008, and Palacios's All list is not full. The dump does not hold the other hand's half of each cell, so which part of the rule fails is not certain.

Not harmful advice: every tab-only line passes the leak rule for its own hand, so none tells a hitter to take a pitch he handles better than average against that hand. Two caveats: 16 of the 83 come from cells where contact offsets almost all the loss (net > −0.5 runs), and 41 come from fewer than 25 pitches (Wells 14, Carrigg 14, Antonacci 13, Yordan Álvarez 12).
issues.why_it_matters: Coaches use the card with the player in the room and switch to vs RHP for most at-bats. On 99 cards a tab's first instruction differs from the All view's. Sometimes it is a leak bigger than anything on the All view, which the pictures never mark. The tab's leak numbers point at different picture markers. Its closing line says these are 'the only changes on this card', and on 23 cards one view says there is nothing to do while another gives a line. All of this is by design: step 17 rebuilds each tab from that hand's leaks only. But the reader is never told why the views differ, and the tab note calls the All view 'the full plan'. It is not high: the All plan, the main instruction, holds on its own view, and every tab line is a real leak against that hand.
issues.root_cause: scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:1057 builds each hand's leaks independently. They go through leak_rules.leak_cells (scripts/leak_rules.py:137), whose choices+contact<0 test the other hand's pitches can flip either way, and are capped at three (17:458 .head(lr.LEAK_TOP)). 17:1067 plan_items_by_hand reruns plan_items with no anchor on the All plan. 17:639 sorts on choices alone, so near-ties flip. keep_line's 'on this card' wording is reused on tabs. In the template (scripts/templates/player_cards.html), :664 draws markers only from p.leaks.all, while :927 and :935 number the tab's tags and list from the tab's own list (tooltip 'numbered on the pictures'). :930 has the note 'pick All pitchers for the full plan', and :749 outlines the All plan's first picture on every tab. scripts/plan_checks.py checks each view alone and has no cross-view check.
issues.suggested_fix:
1. Anchor each tab on the All plan. In step 17, pass start= the first All-plan cell that is in that hand's leaks to plan_items(..., view=h). Let a tab line whose cell is not on the All list appear only with a mark: 'vs RHP only, not on the full plan: against left-handers your chases there pay off' (or 'outside the top three').
2. Number tab leaks and tags by their All-list number. Give tab-only leaks a letter and no picture marker, or draw the tab's own markers.
3. On a tab fallback where the All plan has a line naming that hand, say that line is too small against that hand alone, instead of 'Nothing stands out'.
4. Change the tab closing line from 'on this card' to 'against right-handers'.
5. Add a cross-view check to plan_checks.py.
Bigger option: drop the per-hand plan rebuild and show the All plan's lines on each tab with that hand's rates.

issues.statement: Partly confirmed. On 88 of the 229 roster rows that have a plan line, Top leak, Leak runs, Inches off and Count check describe leak 1 while Start with is a different leak. On 16 rows leak 1 is not in the plan at all, and the roster gives no sign of either. On 7 rows a video item (3.59 to 3.92 in) shows Inches off "4", which is the far-off cutoff. The count check verdict is printed on no web card. Two claims are overstated: there are 83 take lines beside 'hitting well', not 93, and the README treats that pairing as context by design. The Cam Smith example does not fit this pattern.
evidence: Checked all 261 roster rows. Every cell matches the card data: 0 mismatches on Top leak phrase, Inches off = Math.round(leak1.depth_in), and Count check = leak1.count_status. 229 rows have a pitch line. The other 32 have no leak and are not affected.

Start with is not leak 1 on 88 of 229 rows. 84 of these are in a different count group. On 38 of those only the count differs (same pitch and side), e.g. Pérez: "Two strikes, breaking balls below the zone | −4.6 | 5 | average | under 13 (was 24) | At 0-1 or 1-1, let breaking balls below the zone go (74% vs 42%, 4 in off)"

Two different inch figures in one row: 66 rows (64 numeric, plus 'within a ball' on Walker and Vivas), e.g. Lukes "| −1.9 | 4 | average | ... (62% vs 37%, 6 in off)" and Goodman 6 vs 8. On 22 of the 88 the two inch figures happen to agree.

Count check status differs from the Start-with count's own status on 31 rows, e.g. Josh Bell 'struggling' (two strikes) next to a first-pitch line whose count is hitting well; Caglianone the same; McNeil 'average' vs struggling; Monasterio 'average' vs struggling.

Leak 1 is not in the plan on 16 rows: 7 takes (Cowser −4.0, Olson −3.9, Y. Álvarez −3.3, Ramírez −3.1, Carroll −2.8, Rumfield −1.9, Jared Young −2.0) and 9 video items (Sanoja, House, Langeliers, Wells, Lewis, Ramos, Adames, Bazzana, Hao-Yu Lee). Cowser row: "Two strikes, mostly vs RHP, breaking balls below the zone | −4.0 | 6 | average | under 5 (was 12) | At 0-1 or 1-1, mostly against right-handers, let breaking balls below the zone go (67% vs 39%, 6 in off)". The card's only cue is the generic note "so it can leave a bigger one out".

Inches off '4' for a video item (depth < 4) on 7 rows: Gilbert 3.92, Machado 3.67, Walker 3.73, Wells 3.83, Langeliers 3.59, Gonzales 3.87, Lewis 3.81. Same row says both: Gilbert "| −1.4 | 4 | hitting well | none: video only | With two strikes, fastballs above the zone are one to go over on video ... within a ball of the zone)"; Machado "| −0.9 | 4 | hitting well | none: video only | ... (50% vs 32%, within a ball of the zone)". The card's count note says "Far-off: 4+ inches off the plate."

0 of 261 player cards contain 'hitting well', 'struggling' or 'count check'. README.md:385 says "On a hitter's card it is the xwOBA column of the count table", but that column is raw, not shrunk. Yandy Díaz roster "Ahead in the count, mostly vs RHP, breaking balls below the zone | −1.0 | 5 | hitting well" vs card "Ahead in the count	240 ... .348.358" (shrunk .376). Colt Keith roster 'hitting well' vs card "Ahead in the count	165 ... .352.358" (shrunk .370).

Glossary (template line 1048): "Top leak: ... and how far off the zone the chased pitches were (median inches). Count check: how he hits once the count reaches the leak's counts..." and "Start with: the plan's first pitch line". So the split is documented, but no column head or cell says which leak it describes.

Screenshot skeptic_rostercols2/roster_phone_KC_perez_open.png: on a phone the open row stacks TOP LEAK, LEAK RUNS, INCHES OFF 5, COUNT CHECK average and BEAT directly above START WITH "(74% vs 42%, 4 in off)". A closed row shows only Top leak directly above Start with (Caglianone: "Two strikes, mostly vs RHP, breaking balls below the zone" / "On the first pitch, let breaking balls below the zone go (49% vs 22%, 6 in off)").

Related layout issue (screenshots skeptic_rostercols2/roster_desktop_top.png and roster_desktop1920_BAL.png): on desktop the Start with column is past the right edge. The table is 1761 px wide in a 1390 px box at a 1440 window and a 1438 px box at 2560. 'Start with' starts at x=1560, so the instruction column is visible only after a horizontal scroll. Inches off and Count check sit directly right of Top leak, so the mix-up is less visible on desktop than on a phone.
issues.method: Wrote skeptic_rostercols2/measure.py, measure2.py and union.py over dump_2026.json. Each matches all 261 roster rows to data.players by name and compares each cell with leaks.all[0], with the first pitch item of plan_items and its leak, with start_with's 'N in off' and 'within a ball', with the plan's pitch cells, and with tables.all xwOBA vs league (raw, and under the same 10-point rule as the shrunk verdict). Also grepped all card text for the count-check words. Read the template's ROSTER build and CSS (player_cards.html:1009-1100, 202-217), step 17's start_with, is_video, plan_pitch_items and count_check_line, leak_rules.py's shrink, and README sections on the count check. Took desktop (1440/1600/1920/2560) and phone (390) roster screenshots with a copy of shot.mjs that can click a row (skeptic_rostercols2/shot_eval*.mjs).
issues.why_it_matters: The roster is the coach's scan view. On 38% of rows with a plan, its leak numbers belong to a different pitch from the instruction beside them. On 38 of those rows only the count differs, so the two read as one leak with two inch figures and a count check for the wrong count. On 16 rows the costliest leak, shown with its runs, is one the plan deliberately puts off (Cowser −4.0, Olson −3.9). A coach can start on it without knowing the card says to wait. A '4' beside a video item puts it at the far-off cutoff and invites a take rule on pitches the card calls within a ball of the zone. Start with itself matches the card on all 229 rows, so the main instruction survives: medium, not high. The column split is by design and is in the glossary. The video-item rounding to '4' is not.
issues.root_cause: scripts/templates/player_cards.html:1018-1028 builds the ROSTER row from top = p.leaks.all[0] (leak, leak_runs, check = STATUS_WORDS[top.count_status], depth = Math.round(top.depth_in)), but plan comes from p.start_with. scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:853-867 start_with() quotes the first pitch item's leak, and plan_pitch_items() at 631-642 orders takes before two strikes first and video items last, so that leak is often not leak 1 and leak 1 can be dropped. Math.round at template line 1026 ignores the is_video cutoff at depth_in < 4 (17:612-613, CLEARLY_OFF_IN=4 at 17:527). The shrunk count verdict (leak_rules.py:240-245, x_shrunk = league + level + extra) is printed only on the roster (template 1011/1026) and in noted_players/README.md (17:2237-2249, 2384), never on the card.
issues.suggested_fix:
In the template's ROSTER map, find the plan's lead leak: first = p.plan_items.find(i => i.kind === "pitch"); lead = first ? p.leaks.all[first.n - 1] : top. Then:
1. Take Count check from lead and name its count, e.g. "0-1 or 1-1: struggling".
2. Take Inches off from lead, or drop the column, since Start with already prints the inches. Print "under 4" when depth_in < 4 and keep a numeric sort key.
3. When first.n !== 1, prefix Start with with "Leak N:".
4. When leak 1's cell is not among the plan's pitch cells, add "(not in plan; see card)" to the Top leak cell.
5. Update the glossary (line 1048) to match.
For the count check, either add the shrunk verdict under the all-pitchers xwOBA cell on the card (tables.all[].status already exists) or drop the column. Add plan_checks guards: no roster Inches off of "4" when depth_in < 4, and a 'not in plan' marker whenever leak 1 is left out.
refuted_items: '93 rows pair hitting well with a take instruction': 93 rows say 'hitting well', but only 83 have a take Start with (10 are video lines), and only 52 of those are the same leak. README.md:431-446 also shows the count check does not change the payoff of fixing a leak ('the cards show the count check as context and keep every leak in the plan'). So this is an unexplained label, not a contradiction.

Cam Smith (finding 450): Start with is his only leak, leak 1, and the glossary defines Start with as 'the plan's first pitch line'. The contact line ahead of it on the card is by design, and the roster's Problem column says 'mostly contact'. Not an instance of this pattern.

'Count check appears only on the roster': true for the web page (0 of 261 cards print it). But noted_players/README.md prints a Count check line for all 17 noted hitters, and README.md:385 names the card's raw xwOBA column as the count check.

'Count check contradicts the card's xwOBA': it flips direction on only 2 of 229 rows (Yandy Díaz, Colt Keith, both 'hitting well' with raw xwOBA below the league). No row shows 'struggling' with raw xwOBA above the league. 40 more differ from a raw 10-point reading but are 'average' versus small raw gaps, which is the shrink working as intended.

Finding 129, 'Runs at stake' vs 'Cost of far-off chases': the numbers agree on 261 of 261, and the roster lede defines the column ('the runs his swing choices on far-off pitches cost'), so this is only naming polish.
'The row reads as one story' holds mainly on a phone. On desktop, Inches off and Count check sit right next to Top leak, and Start with is off-screen past the right edge (a separate layout issue).

issues.statement: On 86 of 261 cards (All pitchers view), at least one count costs 1.0 run or more of choices in the By count table, yet it gets no plan line and no sentence names it. On 83 of those 86 the plan then closes with "The only change(s) on this card is/are the pitch(es) above". The pattern is real and by design, but it is medium, not high: every flagged card still has valid pitch lines and nothing tells the hitter to do something wrong. What fails is that the table argues with the plan, and the closing line claims more than it should. In 36 cards the gap is large: the unnamed count is the card's costliest, or it costs more than the plan's own leaks.
evidence: Measured (All pitchers view, code threshold choices <= -1.0): 86 cards / 139 count rows. 73 of the 86 lose runs on choices overall (net), so no framing line of any kind; 13 are good choosers with a framing line or contact line that names no count. 75 have no framing line at all (the reviewers' '76'). 83 of 86 end 'The only change(s) on this card ...'. Counting the hand tabs: 95 cards (99 if rows that only print -1.0 are included).

Size: in 46 cards the unnamed counts total 3+ runs, and in 20 cards 5+ runs. In 34 the unnamed count is the card's costliest. In 31 the unnamed counts cost more than the plan's own leaks. In 9 every plan line sits in a count the table prints as a plus (Buxton, Crews, Suárez, Freeman, Aranda, Caissie, Devers, Pasquantino, Yordan Álvarez).

Caglianone: 'Ahead in the count 168 35%24% ... −3.1' and '0-1 or 1-1 255 41%30% ... −3.0'. The plan lines are First pitch and Two strikes, then 'Keep swinging at strikes. The only changes on this card are the pitches above.' The plan's leaks cover 4.8 of 15.9 runs (30%), so the spread line does not fire.

Harris: '0-1 or 1-1 297 52%31% 45%21% ... −5.0' and 'Ahead in the count 211 38%24% ... −3.5'. Both plan lines are 'With two strikes'. Staff note: 'His contact is among the best in this group, so nothing else needs to change.' He loses 9.6 runs before two strikes.

Pérez: 'Ahead in the count 183 50%25% 46%17% ... −7.0' gets no line. The plan covers 5.95 of 23.26 runs (25.6%), just over the 25% bar. His vs LHP tab, under the bar, does say 'Your chase choices cost 7 runs a season, across every count; the pitch above is the biggest piece of it.'

Same card, two rules: Buxton's vs LHP tab says 'you give back about 1 run a season when you're ahead in the count', while his All pitchers plan leaves 'Ahead in the count 132 34%26% ... −2.7' unnamed. Its line (1) says 'With two strikes, your choices are a plus overall (+0.2 runs in the count table)'. Ty France vs LHP: 'you give back about 2 runs a season when you're ahead in the count', while All pitchers 'Ahead in the count 170 42%24% 33%15% ... −4.7' (his costliest count) is unnamed. Griffin shows the same split.

Two-strike variant, not reported: José Ramírez 'Two strikes 416 45%39% ... −3.7' is his costliest count. His leak 1 there ('Two strikes, mostly vs RHP, breaking balls below the zone', −3.1, 6.5 in, a clear take) is cut by the take-before-two-strikes order. The plan is two lines in a −0.8 ahead count, then 'The only changes on this card are the pitches above.' Yordan Álvarez (Two strikes −6.1, plan in a +0.2 count), Matt Olson and Colton Cowser are the same.

Walker: tile 'COST OF FAR-OFF CHASES 6.0'. Plan: 'Keep swinging at strikes. Nothing on this card is a take rule for you yet: the staff takes the pitches above to video with you first.' Table: 'Ahead in the count 218 34%26% 28%19% ... −3.5' and 'First pitch 306 27%17% 21%12% ... −2.0'. Yet his vs RHP tab says 'At 0-1 or 1-1, let breaking balls off the plate away go. You swung at 80% of them; hitters on average swing at 35%.' He is the only All pitchers video-only plan with a far-off cost of 3+ (next is 1.1). Related: 14 views say 'Nothing on this card is a take rule' while the card's other view has one (4 All pitchers views, 10 hand tabs).

Contact line suppresses the fallback: Montgomery vs LHP, one line, 'Your bigger issue is contact: you miss on 68% of your chases...', beside 'Ahead in the count 49 47%28% 32%19% ... −1.0'. Same for Henderson vs RHP (Ahead −1.5), Bolte (First −1.2, Ahead −1.3), Norby (0-1/1-1 −1.1), Gonzales vs LHP and Caissie vs LHP.

Coverage is measured against the net loss, so plus counts hide costly ones: the plan's leaks equal 192% of Duran's net loss (First pitch −1.6 unnamed), 853% of Caissie's (Ahead −2.0 unnamed) and 130% of Mullins's (Ahead −3.1 unnamed).

Upstream: 21 flagged cards have all three listed leaks in two strikes while a pre-two-strike count goes unnamed (LEAK_TOP=3). In 26 cards a listed leak sits in the unnamed count but the plan cut it: 22 are video items, and 4 are takes cut by the order rule.
Nothing on the page explains it: countNote, guide and footer have no sentence about counts with no line. plan_checks.py has no check for it.
issues.method: Read plan_items, spread_line, fallback_line, framing_line and keep_line (scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:546-850), leak_cells and LEAK_TOP (scripts/leak_rules.py), the plan_checks.py KINDS list and coach_notes.py. Wrote costly_sweep.py and costly_measure.py in the audit folder and ran them over dump_2026.json for every player, in the All pitchers view and both hand tabs. A count row was flagged when its choices are <= -1.0 (also tested printed −1.0), no pitch item sits in that count, and no frame, fallback or contact item names it or says 'across every count'. For each flag I recorded the plan's leak coverage of the net loss, whether the row is the costliest count, whether every plan line sits in a plus count, cut leaks in the count, the closing line and the staff note. I re-read the rendered aside text in the dump for Caglianone, Harris, Pérez, Peraza, Buxton, Freeman, Castro, Álvarez, Ramírez, France, Tovar, Merrill, Giménez, Adell, Chourio, Walker, Montgomery and Jung to confirm the quotes. I checked every one of the 70 reported names against the sweep: all flag, with Harper, Jung, Gonzales and Rengifo flagging on hand tabs only.
issues.why_it_matters: The By count table sits right beside the plan. A coach or hitter sees the biggest red number in the table (Pérez ahead −7.0 at 46% vs 17% far-off, Harris 0-1/1-1 −5.0, France ahead −4.7) and finds no word about it. Then the closing line says the pitches above are the only changes, and for Harris the staff note adds that nothing else needs to change. The card applies its own 1-run rule unevenly: a fallback names a 1-run count ('you give back about 1 run a season when you're ahead in the count' on Buxton's vs LHP tab), while the same card's All pitchers plan stays silent on a 2.7-run count. Readers lose trust in the plan, or assume the costly count is fine. It is not high, because the pitch lines are sound and nothing prescribes a wrong action.
issues.root_cause: scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:817 builds `costly` (counts at −1.0 or worse). With pitch lines, counts are named only in spread_line, which runs only when `loss >= SPREAD_MIN_RUNS and named < SPREAD_SHARE * loss` (line 831): the plan's leak runs must be under 25% of the NET choices loss, and plus counts shrink that net. Otherwise framing_line (763) names no count, and keep_line (785-797) always says 'The only change(s) on this card ...'. fallback_line (693), which names every costly count, runs only when items is empty (842), so a contact line (840) suppresses it. Upstream, LEAK_TOP=3 (leak_rules.py:54) ranks cells by runs, so two-strike cells and video items fill the list. plan_pitch_items (631) then cuts video items, or the two-strike leak 1 when two takes before two strikes exist. plan_checks.py has no guard. Harris's closing clause is hand-written at coach_notes.py:52; its claim check (coach_notes.py:230-241) tests only the contact rank.
issues.suggested_fix: In plan_items, after the pitch lines: `uncovered = [g for g in costly if g not in {lk['count_group'] for _, lk in chosen}]`, deciding on the stored value so it matches what the table prints. When uncovered is non-empty and no spread line fired, add a frame item before the keep line. Example: 'Your choices also cost about N runs a season when you're ahead in the count, spread over many pitches with no single clear take; the count table shows where.' Use productive_line instead when contact pays for it. In that case also change the keep line to 'The pitches above are the changes to start with' instead of 'the only changes'. Add the same clause after a contact-only line. Alternatively, measure spread coverage against the gross loss (sum of negative counts), not the net. For a video-only plan whose header far-off cost prints 1.0 or more, say which count carries it. Say 'nothing on this plan', not 'nothing on this card', when another view has a take rule. Drop 'so nothing else needs to change' from Harris's note. Add a plan_checks kind 'costly count unnamed': a count printing −1.0 or worse with no pitch line and no plan sentence naming it.
refuted_items: Severity 'high' for the pattern as a whole: not upheld. Every flagged card has valid pitch lines and nothing tells the hitter to do something wrong; the failure is an unexplained table plus an overreaching closing line. The strongest subset (36 cards, Harris's note, Walker, and the four two-strike cuts) is borderline-high.

Luis Rengifo vs LHP (finding 45): Ahead prints −1.0 but is −0.97, under the code's 1-run bar, so it holds only by rounding, and he has no other flagged count. Lile 0-1/1-1 (−0.98), Crawford First pitch (−0.96) and Peraza First pitch (−0.97) are the same rounding edge, though those cards have other costly counts that do hold.

Daylen Lile (finding 110), 'all three are two-strike cells': wrong. His leak 3 is 'Ahead in the count, fastballs inside' (−1.1, 1.1 in, a video item cut from the plan). The point that his first-pitch 'below the zone 54% / 24% (61)' never surfaces holds.
Salvador Pérez (finding 252), '25.3%': the plan covers 5.95 of 23.26 runs, 25.6%. The point holds.

Hunter Goodman (finding 45), 'the note only says fastballs up ... look worse': partly wrong. The staff note also says 'Across every count before two strikes, not only ahead, he chases them 48% of the time against 30% ..., about 5 runs.' Only the player-facing plan is silent.

Brady House (finding 205), 'left out ... with no word': the generic sentence under the list ('so it can leave a bigger one out') is printed, and leak 1 is a video item (1.4 in), cut by the video-never-ahead-of-a-take rule. The Ahead −3.4 count itself is still unnamed.

Good choosers (Freeman, Pasquantino, Suárez, Seager, Crews, Hao-Yu Lee, Rumfield, Aranda, Devers, Cowser, Henderson vs RHP, Bolte, Norby): the issue holds but is weaker. A framing or contact line says their choices are about average or better overall, so the offset is explained; only the count is not named. Low for these.

Reviewers' sweep '76 cards': I count 75 All pitchers cards with a 1.0+ run count unnamed and no framing line of any kind (73 with pitch lines, 2 contact-only), 86 counting framed good choosers, and 95 including hand tabs.

issues.statement: Confirmed: the "Cost of far-off chases" tile and the roster's "Runs at stake" print a loss as a positive number with a floor of 0.0, while Choices, Contact and Leak runs print a loss as negative, and nothing on the page states either sign. 110 of 261 hitters print 0.0. 82 of them sit beside a costed leak, and on all 82 the plan says far-off pitches "cost you nothing net (the 0.0 at the top)": 71 directly under a take line (4+ inches off) and 63 under a line printing 5 to 10 inches off. One part of the report is wrong: the tile is not a single net figure clipped at 0. It is the net loss for fewer than two strikes plus the net loss for two strikes, each floored at 0 separately. So the card's "nothing net" is literally true whenever it prints, but a positive tile can sit over a far-off net gain (34 cards).
evidence: Aranda (live page, skeptic_faroff/aranda_1440.png): tile "COST OF FAR-OFF CHASES 0.0" beside "Choices +4.1". Plan line 1: "...The ones you swung at were typically 6 inches off the zone." Then the frame: "Overall your chase choices are better than average (+4.1 runs a season), and on far-off pitches they cost you nothing net (the 0.0 at the top): the pitches above are spots to tighten, not a new approach." Leak 1: "−3.4"

Sweep of 261 cards (skeptic_faroff/measure.py): 110 tiles print 0.0, every one exactly 0 (none is rounding). 109 of the 110 sit beside a positive Choices. 82 have at least one leak, and on all 82 the all-pitchers plan carries the 0.0 clause (the hand tabs repeat it 61 times on vs RHP and 22 times on vs LHP). 71 of the 82 have a take line, and 63 have a line reading 'typically N inches off' with N of 5 or more (by largest N: 5 on 20 cards, 6 on 24, 7 on 12, 8 on 5, 9 on 1, 10 on 1)
Costliest take line under the 0.0 clause: Carter Jensen −4.1 (6 in). Then Yastrzemski −3.6, Riley Greene −3.5, Aranda −3.4, Beavers −3.3, Hoskins −3.0 (5 in) and −2.8 (10 in), Muncy −1.1 (8 in)

Roster, live default sort: "261 of 261 hitters · sorted by runs at stake, most first." The 0.0 block is rows 152 to 261 (110 rows) in xChase+ rank order, starting "Taylor Ward | R | 154 · 1st | 606 | 0.0 | +27.1", then Perdomo (2nd), then Kwan (3rd). 82 of those rows have Leak runs and a take 'Start with', 68 have a top leak 4+ inches off, and 29 have a number to beat. Example: "| TB | Jonathan Aranda | ... | 0.0 | +4.1 | +11.4 | ... | −3.4 | 6 | ... | under 10 (was 19) |"

Opposite signs: 114 cards show a positive far-off cost beside a negative Choices, e.g., Diaz "11.2" / "−13.9", Rafaela "12.2" / "−16.6", Baldwin "6.6" / "−7.7". 147 roster rows show a positive Runs at stake beside a negative Leak runs, e.g., Pérez "16.9 | −23.3 | +7.8 ... −4.6". No card and no roster text says which sign is a loss (0 hits for negative / runs lost / minus). The glossary and count note both say "Choices is what the swing decisions cost" while Ward's row reads "0.0 | +27.1"

The roster column 'Runs at stake' has no glossary entry. The only description is the lede, "sorted by the runs his swing choices on far-off pitches cost per 600 plate appearances", and the card calls the same number "Cost of far-off chases"

Live check of the Leak runs sort: clicking it gives "sorted by leak runs, most first." and the first rows are "Kyle Tucker ... −0.8", "Alec Bohm ... −0.8", "Nick Loftin ... −0.8". The biggest loss (Josh Lowe −7.0) comes last

Fallback cards: 28 all-pitchers plans with a 0.0 tile have no pitch line. 27 read "Nothing stands out. Your chase choices are about league average or better in every count." and one is Henry Bolte's contact line. None explains the 0.0 (plan_checks.py:109-110 returns before its 'header 0.0 unexplained' check when there are no pitch lines). The far-off gain hidden behind 0.0 (step 13, classes A+B) has a median of +6.2 runs and goes up to Ward +16.5, Torres +16.1, Austin Martin +14.1 and Soto +12.2

Per-class floors (actionability_2026.csv): 76 of 151 positive tiles have one strike class showing a gain. On 34 of them the far-off net is a gain while the tile prints a cost: Acuña tile 0.8 vs net +7.1, Connor Norby 0.6 vs +6.9, Jacob Young 0.2 vs +4.9, Austin Wells 1.9 vs +3.7. Moreno: under-two-strike class +4.1, two-strike class −4.7 → tile 4.7 beside "Choices +0.1"

Owen Caissie: tile "4.6" beside "Choices −0.8". His By count Far-off column reads 23%/24% overall and 32%/34% with two strikes, yet both classes are losses (A −0.9, B −3.7). 7 cards show a tile of 3+ while the table's far-off rate is at or under the league's (Stott, Benge, Arenado, Pages, Heim, Caissie, Mayo), and 34 show a tile of 1+

issues.why_it_matters: On a card, the clause is accurate ("net") and ends "the pitches above are spots to tighten, not a new approach", so the take instruction survives. Still, a player reads that far-off pitches cost him nothing directly under a line telling him to stop chasing a pitch 6 inches off that costs 3.4 runs, and the tile's note never says it is a floored net loss. Two places can actually mislead: (1) The roster. A coach sorting by 'Runs at stake' finds 82 hitters with take plans (29 with a number to beat) in a 110-way tie at the bottom, ordered by an unstated rule. 'Leak runs, most first' lists the smallest leaks first. Nowhere does it say which sign is a loss. (2) The tile is called a net, but it is two separately floored nets. It can show a far-off cost for a hitter whose far-off choices gain runs (34 cards), and it can disagree in direction with the By count Far-off column (Caissie). No reader can resolve that from the page.
issues.root_cause: scripts/13_build_actionability_profiles.py:220-222 computes far_off_recoverable = −(A.clip(upper=0) + B.clip(upper=0)), so each strike class is netted and floored on its own. Choices price each pitch against the league's exact count × distance-bucket cell (step 04 expected_cost_per_pitch), not against the table's e_match. scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:1049 applies a redundant max(…, 0) to give runs_at_stake. Lines 754-760 (FAR_OFF_ZERO "on far-off pitches they cost you nothing net (the 0.0 at the top)") and 765-783 (framing_line) attach the clause to every plan with pitch lines when the tile is 0.0. plan_checks.py:109-110 skips plans with no pitch lines. scripts/templates/player_cards.html:618-620 draws the tile: eyebrow "Cost of far-off chases", value runs_at_stake.toFixed(1) with no sign, note "runs per 600 PA from your choices on pitches at least 4 inches off the plate". Lines 621-628 draw the signed Choices and Contact. Line 1033 names the column "Runs at stake". Line 1047 is the lede and line 1048 the glossary: no Runs at stake entry, "Choices is what the swing decisions cost", no sign rule. Lines 1064-1068 sort stably, so ties keep D.players order, which is xChase+ rank from step 17 line 1035, and "most first" sorts negative columns descending. Line 1089 is the state line. The count note is at step 17:1448 (GLOSSARY "Choices: what the swing decisions cost").
issues.suggested_fix: (1) Use one name and one sign rule. Rename the roster column to match the card ("Far-off runs lost"), and add the line "Choices, Contact, Leak runs: negative = runs lost, positive = runs gained" to the roster glossary and to the card's count note (step 17:1448, template:1048). (2) Make the tile say what it is. Change its note to "runs lost per 600 PA to your choices on pitches 4+ inches off, with fewer than two strikes and with two strikes, each net; 0.0 = no loss". When it prints 0.0, add the gain from step 13 (A+B) under it: "your far-off choices gain +N". (3) Reword FAR_OFF_ZERO so it agrees with a take line on a far-off pitch: "taken together, your far-off choices gain more than they give back (the 0.0 at the top); the pitch above is where they give some back". (4) On the roster, break ties by Leak runs, biggest loss first, and say so in the state line ("ties by leak runs"). Make "most first" on Choices, Contact and Leak runs mean biggest loss first, or label those sorts "biggest loss first". Optionally drop the redundant max() at step 17:1049.
refuted_items: "cost up to 5.8 runs (Hoskins, Muncy, Yastrzemski, Jensen)": wrong. The costliest take line under the 0.0 clause is Carter Jensen at −4.1. 5.8 is Yastrzemski's leak depth in inches (5.8 in), not runs. Hoskins −3.0 and −2.8, Muncy −1.1 and Yastrzemski −3.6 hold as quoted.

'The tile is the far-off net cost clipped at 0': partly wrong. Step 13 nets and floors the under-two-strike and two-strike classes separately and then adds them. A 0.0 therefore really means no net loss in either class, so the card's 'nothing net' sentence is accurate. A positive tile is not a net: 76 of 151 positive tiles hide a gain in one class, and on 34 the far-off net is a gain (Acuña 0.8 vs +7.1).

Owen Caissie (4.6 while far-off is 23% vs 24%): holds as printed, but the cause is not clipping, since both his classes are losses (−0.9, −3.7). The count is 7 such cards at 3+, not 4.

issues.statement: Every target sentence and every roster "(was N)" prints step 19's excess, which is measured against a different league rate from the "avg" in the leak rows printed just above it. In 198 of the 213 point sentences the target number is lower than the pooled gap of the leaks it names. It is 5+ points lower on 70 cards (32 of 140 numbered targets, 38 of 73 no-target sentences), up to 13.9 points lower (Yandy Díaz). On 9 no-target cards the sentence says "below" or "about at the league's chase rate" for leaks the list prints above the league. The issue holds. One of the reported sweep numbers and 6 of the 84 named cards do not.
evidence: Sweep (skeptic_tscale2/measure.py over dump_2026.json, all 261 players): 140 numbered targets, 73 no-target sentences, 16 video-only (no number), 32 with no leaks. The sentence's number always equals round(target.excess*100), and the roster Beat '(was N)' always equals the sentence (0 mismatches). Printed minus pooled card gap: numbered mean -3.45 (min -10.6, max +2.5): 81 are 3+ below, 32 are 5+ below, 9 are 8+ below, 2 are 10+ below. No-target mean -5.15 (min -13.9): 58 are 3+ below, 38 are 5+ below, 2 are 10+ below. Above by 2+: only 4 cards, all numbered (Soderstrom +2.5, Massey +2.2, Lukes +2.2, Eldridge +2.1).
Systematic direction: the league rate implied by the target is above the card's 'avg' on 201 of 213 cards (mean +4.1 points), so the target nearly always reads smaller than the list.

Nothing on the card or the roster names the other baseline. Roster glossary: "Beat: how far above the league's chase rate, in points, the frozen line expects the hitter to chase in all of the card's leaks next season with no change". Only the staff README written by step 17 (lines 2335-2337) says: "(on the backtest's scale, so it need not match any one leak's rates)".

issues.method: Read BRIEF.md and the code: step 17's target_text/target_beat, how the leaks are computed and the e_match expectation; step 19's docstring, df["e"] and the excess; leak_rules.BACKTEST_LEAGUE_CELL; template line 944 and the roster glossary/lede. Wrote skeptic_tscale2/measure.py, which runs over every player in dump_2026.json. For each one it parses the sentence's number and direction and which leaks it names ('Leak 1' / 'Leaks 1 and 2' / 'Leaks 1 to 3'). It pools the card gap as 100*sum(chases - league*pitches)/sum(pitches), and checks the sentence against round(excess), against the card's own aside text and against the roster Beat column. It splits numbered from no-target from video-only cards and finds the sign flips and the single-leak cases. Wrote skeptic_tscale2/reported.py to test each of the 84 reported cards (holds at |diff|>=3, weak at 2-3, refuted under 2) and each sweep claim. I also pulled the exact leak-row, plan and target text from the card asides for the quoted cards. Outputs: skeptic_tscale2/rows.json and rows.csv.
issues.why_it_matters: The target is the one number the card asks the hitter to beat in 2027. It sits two lines under a leak row that gives a different gap against a rate also called the league's ("avg"), and the plan says "hitters on average swing at". A player or coach who checks it (Tawa 69 vs 39 is 30, the card says 20; Winn 71 vs 52 is 19, the card says 9, "Under 3 is a fix") cannot tell what is measured or how to track it. On 9 no-target cards it says he chased less than the league in the very spot the plan tells him to take. The design reason is sound: step 19 freezes on step 16's baseline so the 2027 score compares like with like, and the number is correct on that scale. But the card shows two league rates under one name. The plan line itself survives, so this is medium, not high.
issues.root_cause: The two numbers use two league baselines and the card shows both as "the league's chase rate". The leak rows use the card's smoothed, location- and matchup-adjusted expectation: scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:328 (e_match), passed to lr.leak_cells(p, scale, "e_match") in leaks() at :456-479. The target uses step 19's raw cell mean by season x count_state x distance_bucket x pitch group x side: scripts/19_freeze_leak_predictions.py:175 (df["e"] = df.groupby(lr.BACKTEST_LEAGUE_CELL)...), with excess at :235 and BACKTEST_LEAGUE_CELL at scripts/leak_rules.py:62. target_text (scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:966-1016) prints t["excess"] as "points above the league's chase rate" with no mention of the scale, and the no-target branch (:988-1002) prints the 2026 number even though only the forecast triggers the branch. target_beat (:1019-1029) adds "(was N)" to the roster. The template puts the sentence directly under the leak list (scripts/templates/player_cards.html:944), and the roster glossary (:1048) has no scale note either. The step-19 numbers almost always come out lower because the leaks are picked for high excess over e_match, so the other baseline regresses them.
issues.suggested_fix:
The frozen numbers stay on step 19's scale, since step 20 scores against them. Change only the wording:
(1) No-target sentence: drop the 2026 number and say only the forecast, e.g. "No target: with no change these spots should be about at the league's rate in 2027." This removes all 9 sign flips and the 38 no-target gaps of 5+ points.
(2) Numbered target: either lead with the card's own pooled gap and then the frozen number on its named scale, e.g. "Leaks 1 to 3 together: 29 points above the average hitter on the list's rates (20 on the simpler league rate the target is scored on). With no change, about 11 there in 2027; under 11 is a fix." Or at least add the clause "measured against the league's raw rate for the same count, distance and pitch type, not the 'avg' above". Step 19 already writes card_league_rate_2026 on the hitter row, so the card-scale pooled gap is available.
(3) Add the same scale note to the roster glossary's Beat entry and to the lede.
(4) Add a plan_checks guard: if |round(excess) - pooled card gap| >= 5 or the sign differs, the sentence must carry the scale clause.
(5) While editing the sentence, print '1 point', not '1 points'.

issues.why_it_matters: The card outlines the first line's picture when it opens. The guide says "Numbers on the pictures match the leaks list", and the legend says "Blue: takes more." issues.statement: The pattern is real and the sweep numbers hold exactly. On 54 of 261 cards, a plan view leaves out a leak that is at least 1.25 times the line it displaced and has 20+ pitches; on 19 of them it is 2 times or more. The card never says which leak was left out or why. The closing line then calls the plan's pitches "the only changes on this card", while the leak list ranks the dropped leak higher and the target still counts it. About a third of the cards named in the report do not hold up: either no bigger leak was dropped, or the size gap is a near tie.
evidence: Sweep (skeptic_dropped_v2/sweep.py): every plan was rebuilt from step 17's plan_pitch_items, with 0 mismatches across 783 views. A leak bigger than a plan line is left out on 72 of 229 all-pitchers plans, 43 of 203 vs RHP plans and 1 of 86 vs LHP plans (86 cards). Leak 1 is left out on 16 all-pitchers plans and 11 vs RHP tabs (0 vs LHP). A leak 1 worth 2x or more of every plan line is left out on 5 all-pitchers plans (Olson, Álvarez, Ramírez, Cowser, Carroll) and 3 vs RHP tabs (Wells, Carroll, Jarren Duran). In those same 5 all-pitchers plans it is also bigger than both plan lines combined.

Why, on the all-pitchers view: the take-before-two-strikes order 44 times, the video sort 23, the coach's-note lead 4, order plus video 1. The dropped leak sits in the hitter's costliest count on 40 of 72.
Size of the gap: of the 72 all-pitchers omissions, 25 are near ties (under 1.25 times the line they displaced), 2 rest on under 20 pitches, 28 are 1.25 to 2 times, and 17 are 2 times or more.

Álvarez, all pitchers: the leak list starts with "Two strikes, mostly vs RHP, changeups / splitters below the zone 73% vs 52% avg · 36 of 49 −3.3". The plan is leaks 2 (−1.3) and 3 (−1.0), and line 1 says "When you're ahead in the count, your choices are a plus overall (+0.2 runs in the count table)". The By count table shows Two strikes −6.1, his only costly count. The plan closes "The only changes on this card are the pitches above." The target reads "Leaks 1 to 3 together ... Under 5 is a fix." The vs RHP tab does plan it: "With two strikes, let changeups and splitters below the zone go. You swung at 70% of them".

Cowser: "Two strikes, mostly vs RHP, breaking balls below the zone 66% vs 56% avg · 37 of 56 −4.0" is left out. issues.why_it_matters: The rules work as written: a take before two strikes goes first, video items go after takes, and two lines at most. But on the strongest cases the player reads a plan worth a third of the biggest leak on his own list. The plan then tells him those pitches are the only changes, while the target he is graded on still counts the left-out leak. Nothing says the leak was parked on purpose, or why: costs no strikeouts, video item, or comes next. For example, Álvarez is sent to work in a count where his choices are a net plus, and his only costly count goes unaddressed. The vs RHP tab plans the same leak, so the full plan and the tab disagree on whether he works on it. The main instruction still survives, because every plan line is a real leak, so this is medium, not high.

issues.statement: Plans tell hitters to take (or review on video) pitches they chase at about the league's rate (the two printed rates under 5 points apart). There are 55 such lines across all views, on 39 hitters. On 14 all-pitchers plans and 13 hand tabs such a line is step 1, and on 4 cards (Mead, Okamoto, Perdomo, McMahon) it is the plan's only pitch line, while that card's Target says the leak was at or below the league's rate. The leak list also shows 15 rows at that rate (8 All pitchers, 7 vs RHP, on 11 hitters) that are not on that view's plan, and nothing on the view explains why they are leaks.
evidence: Sweep over all 261 players (skeptic_leaguerate/sweep.py). Plan lines containing 'You swung at these about as often as other hitters do': 55 in total (28 All pitchers, 24 vs RHP, 3 vs LHP) on 39 hitters. Every one sits on a leak whose rates print under 5 points apart, and every leak like that on a plan gets this wording. Printed gap: 0 pts on 7 lines, 1 on 7, 2 on 11, 3 on 14, 4 on 16. 46 are take lines and 9 are video items. 29 of 55 rest on fewer than one net extra chase over the league (14 on under 0.5).

issues.method: Read BRIEF.md and the code: leak_rules.leak_cells, and in step 17 leaks(), rate_clause(), pitch_line(), plan_pitch_items(), plan_items(), target_text() and the template's leak list. Wrote scripts in audit/skeptic_leaguerate/ that run over dump_2026.json for all 261 players and all three views. sweep.py matches the exact plan phrase 'You swung at these about as often as other hitters do' and asserts it appears exactly when the printed gap is under 5. My first pass also matched the contact clause 'You miss about as often...', so I tightened the match. The other scripts: cross.py (markers, the hand tab on the same pitch, the Target sentence), unplanned.py (listed rows not on the plan, checked against the view text, guide, footer and count note), order.py (ordering, dropped real-gap takes, hand splits).
