issues.why_it_matters: The card says it shows where he swings at balls more than other hitters, but its first or only instruction is often a pitch he swings at like everyone else. On 4 cards the Target line on the same view says that leak was at or below the league's rate, so 'take it' has no number behind it: by the card's own grading scale (points above the league) there is nothing to beat. Most of these lines rest on less than one net extra chase. The cost comes from moving a handful of swings between counts and distances on 17 to 80 pitches, which is likely noise. The plan sometimes ranks such a line ahead of, or instead of, a pitch he chases 11 to 22 points too often. The advice itself is safe, since these pitches are typically 4 to 13 inches off and taking them is right. So this misleads about what to work on first rather than telling him to do the wrong thing: medium, not high.
issues.root_cause: scripts/leak_rules.py:137-138: the leak rule keeps any cell with extra_chases > 0 and choices <= -0.75, with no minimum rate excess, so a cell 0.03 chases over the league qualifies. scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:631-641 plan_pitch_items: orders only by video, then two-strike, then choices; the rate gap plays no part, so a league-rate cell worth more runs leads or pushes out a real-gap take. :591-610 rate_clause writes 'about as often ... more of yours came at {excess_counts}'. :467-475 sets excess_counts to the counts with the most extra swings; any count with extra swings qualifies when the net is about 0, and nothing checks that those counts are the costly ones. scripts/templates/player_cards.html:936-943 prints the leak row 'X% vs Y% avg' with no note when the two rates sit together. scripts/plan_checks.py checks only the roster start line for near-identical rates (lines 61, 236).
issues.suggested_fix: 1) In plan_pitch_items, sort by (is_video, rate_gap < RATE_GAP_MIN_PTS, two-strike, choices). A real-gap take then always leads, and a league-rate leak with extra_chases < 1 does not become a step 1 take; it stays in the list. 2) When such a line stays on the plan, name the count or hand instead of the whole group. If a hand tab shows the same pitch 5+ points over, say so ('mostly against right-handers: 61% vs 55%'). Otherwise write 'At 3-2 and 2-2, let ... go: overall you swing at these about as often as other hitters, but more than them in those counts.' 3) Under the leak list, when any row's rates print under 5 points apart, add one sentence: 'Leak N is at about the league's rate; it costs runs because more of its swings came at <counts>.' 4) Add a plan_checks guard: no plan or tab should open on, or consist only of, a line with gap < 5 and extra_chases < 1 when the card has a real-gap take.
refuted_items: 'Take lines' is not exact: 9 of the 55 lines are video items, not take rules. Teoscar Hernández vs RHP line 2 reads 'fastballs off the plate inside are one to go over on video with your coaches, not a take rule'. The same holds for Gilbert (both lines), DeLauter, Henderson, Mack All and vs RHP line 2, Hoskins vs LHP and Ty France vs RHP.

Lewis 'first line ahead of a dropped 13-point leak': the dropped leak (61% vs 48%) is a video item (3.8 in off). It is left out by the by-design rule that takes come before video items with two lines at most, and the card says so under the list. The real problem on Lewis's card is step 2 at 56/45 (vs RHP 64/47) ranked behind the league-rate line.

Okamoto 'the picture, the zone numbers and the target all say he chases it less': this holds only in part. The zone-numbers cell 'below the zone ... 45% / 49% (130)' counts every pitch type (130 pitches, against the leak's 76 breaking balls). The marker's −6 is one spot on the picture. The target's '7 points below' is the known open item about the target's scale. A reader still sees the tension, but two of the three surfaces measure something else.

'The hitter cannot act on "more of yours came at 0-2"': this holds only in part. excess_counts are the counts where he swung more than the league expects, so the line does say where the extra swings were. But 'more of yours came at' reads like count exposure, the instruction still covers every two-strike count, and 0-2 is named first on 9 lines although the code picks those counts by extra swings, not by cost.

Raleigh ('52% vs 48%') and Caissie ('52% vs 50%') are weak examples of the unexplained list rows: the printed excess is visible. The clear cases are Holliday 52/52, Brooks Lee 43/43, Burger 52/51 and Ketel Marte vs RHP 48/47.
Pederson ('25% vs 22% avg · 5 of 20') holds as a small-sample line (0.56 extra chases), but the pitches were typically 13 inches off, so the take itself cannot mislead him.

issues.statement: Confirmed on all 261 cards. Every contact sentence, the extra "Misses on chases" row and the roster Problem label come from step 13's archetype, and that archetype only exists when the hitter's net chase result is a loss. This creates a hard edge at a net of zero. Norby (+8.8 / −9.1, net −0.3) is told "Your issue is contact, not choices". Reynolds (+9.0 / −8.7, net +0.3) never hears the word contact. Thirty 'mixed' hitters lose 3 or more runs on contact, all of it their only or bigger cost, and get no contact word: 11 lose 5 to 10.5 runs, and 8 read "Nothing stands out". Five execution-led hitters with contact losses under 3 runs get the contact framing (Lindor −0.9, Jung, Gonzales, Edman, Hamilton). The contact sentence also says "you miss about as often" for Mullins (32% vs 42%) and Jung (38% vs 44%), who miss far less, and for Mack and Manzardo, whose rates print 5 points apart. On the roster, 160 of the 172 'mixed' rows have no split loss at all: 58 lose nothing, 39 lose only on choices, 63 only on contact. The glossary calls the label "the share of the loss that is choices", and the 'contact' filter option matches 0 hitters.
evidence: Step 13 code (13_build_actionability_profiles.py:216-232): decision_share = np.where(table["runs_saved_per_600"] < 0, decision/runs_saved, np.nan); execution-led = decision_share < 0.5; no net loss falls to "mixed". The card's choices and contact match step 13's decision_per_600 and execution_per_600 to 1e-4 on all 261.

Knife edge at a net of zero. Norby: tiles "Choices | +8.8 | Contact | −9.1", roster "mostly contact", plan "Your issue is contact, not choices: you miss on 53% of your chases, against 44% for other hitters on the same pitches." Reynolds: "Choices | +9.0 | Contact | −8.7", roster "mixed", misses 60%/44%, no contact word in any view. Muncy (+7.2/−7.5) and Okamoto (+5.3/−5.6) get the contact clause; Yelich (+6.9/−6.7), Jensen (+8.7/−8.1) and Semien (+5.9/−5.3) do not.

Stephenson: tiles "Choices | +13.6 | Contact | −8.4"; By count "All counts 931 22% 33% 12% 24% 63% 40% … +13.6 −8.4" and "Two strikes 325 … 62% 36% … +7.8 −9.3"; plan "Nothing stands out. Your chase choices are about league average or better in every count."; roster "mixed" (screenshot arch/shots/stephenson.png)
Torkelson: "Choices | +12.3 | Contact | −10.5", misses 67% vs 43%, rowheads only All pitchers / vs RHP / vs LHP, roster "mixed"; his plan has take lines but no contact clause

11 hitters with contact ≤ −5 that is their only cost, all 'mixed', none with a contact word or Misses row: Torkelson −10.5, Reynolds −8.7, Stephenson −8.4, Jensen −8.1, Murakami −6.9, Yelich −6.7, Soderstrom −6.4, Busch −5.7, Collins −5.4, Semien −5.3, Mitchell −5.0. 'Nothing stands out' with a contact loss of 3 or more runs: Stephenson, Busch, Mitchell, Martin (−4.8, 47%/37%), Kelly (−3.9), Carter (−3.3, 58%/41%), Hernandez (−3.3, 59%/40%), Caratini (−3.1)

Lindor: "Choices | +0.4 | Contact | −0.9", plan "You miss about as often as other hitters do, but what you hit on a chase goes nowhere (over a season your chases cost you 1 run more than an average hitter's would): contact is your bigger cost", plus the Misses on chases row

Jung: tiles "COST OF FAR-OFF CHASES | 2.2" and "Contact | −1.5", but line 1 says "contact is your bigger cost" and the hand tabs say "Your issue is contact, not choices". He is the only one of 43 execution-led cards where the far-off tile exceeds the contact loss.

contact_why is wrong as printed. Mullins: plan "You miss about as often as other hitters do" while the table reads "All counts 1,048 … 32% 42%" and his Misses row is mostly green (arch/shots/mullins.png). Jung: same sentence, table "38% 44%". Joe Mack (46%/41%) and Manzardo (50%/45%) also get "about as often", because the 5-point test uses raw rates, not printed ones.
Rounding: Gonzales (contact −1.496) and Jung (−1.543) both show a "Contact | −1.5" tile; Gonzales' sentence says "1 run more" and Jung's says "2 runs more"

Roster Problem: 172 'mixed' = 58 with no loss, 39 losing only on choices, 63 losing only on contact, 12 losing on both (raw values; by printed values 60/39/62/11). Glossary: "Problem: the share of the loss that is choices (step 13)." Ward "+27.1 | −0.8 | mixed"; Altuve "−7.7 | +2.9 | mixed" vs Clemens "−9.1 | +4.6 | choices" (8-run floor). The filter option "contact" maps to 'execution-only', which step 13 never produces, so it matches 0 rows.

Counter-evidence on the design: across 261 hitters corr(choices, contact) = −0.38, and hitters at +8 choices or better average −1.7 contact. Some contact loss is the flip side of chasing only the hardest pitches, but Stephenson (expected −2.4), Torkelson (−2.1) and Busch (−1.3) lose far more than that.
issues.method: Read the archetype rule in 13_build_actionability_profiles.py and every use of the archetype in 17_build_player_cards.py and templates/player_cards.html. Wrote arch/m1-m7.py over dump_2026.json: checked that the card's choices and contact equal step 13's numbers; listed every non-execution-led hitter whose contact loss is his only or bigger cost and tested every plan view (all, R, L) and the plan block for contact wording, plus rowheads for the Misses row; listed all 43 execution-led hitters with contact size, miss gap and far-off tile; checked the 'about as often' text against printed miss rates; split the roster's 'mixed' rows by the sign of Choices and Contact; tested the filter options; measured corr(choices, contact); tried a rule keyed on contact runs (+30 hitters, −5). Screenshots of the Mullins and Stephenson cards taken with shot.mjs at 1440px.
refuted_items: Brandon Lowe (−5.4/−3.9, misses 62%/46%) and Royce Lewis (−5.9/−5.3) do not show a contact misclassification. Both lose more on choices than on contact, so 'mixed' is a fair label and no contact sentence is owed.

Curtis Mead (+13.6/−2.2, misses 34%/38%), Kevin McGonigle (+16.4/−1.9, 33%/38%), Taylor Ward (−0.8), Dane Myers (−0.3) and Masyn Winn (−0.2) lose too little on contact, and the first two miss less than average. Only the roster-label part holds for them; no contact sentence is owed.

'His biggest problem is never shown' holds only in part. The By count table prints Misses (Torkelson 67%/43%), and the page's Show control, 'Misses on chases', draws the misses picture for any hitter. What is missing is the words and the default extra row.
'Left with no plan' holds for 8 cards ('Nothing stands out' with a contact loss of 3 or more runs). The other 22 of the 30 have take lines; only the contact reason is missing.

Severity high is not upheld. Every 'mixed' contact-loser has a net chase gain, choices and contact are negatively correlated (r = −0.38), and no line tells a player to do the wrong thing. This is medium: inconsistent and missing, not wrong advice.
Jung's 'contact, not choices' vs his 2.2 far-off tile holds, but on only 1 of 43 execution-led cards.
'Goes nowhere' printed for about a 1-run loss holds for Lindor (−0.9), Gonzales (−1.5) and Jung (−1.5).
issues.why_it_matters: Cards that look the same give opposite messages. A coach comparing Norby and Reynolds, or Okamoto and Jensen, sees the same numbers and the opposite diagnosis. Hitters whose largest negative number is contact, missing 15 to 24 points more than the league on chases, are told "Nothing stands out" or get take lines with no reason. Hitters with a one-run contact loss, some of whom miss less than average, are told contact is their bigger cost, and two of those sentences say the opposite of the By count table. On the roster, the Problem column and its filter do not do what the glossary says: 'mixed' covers the best choosers, pure choices losers and pure contact losers, and 'contact' finds nobody. This is by design (step 17 deliberately keys on step 13's documented net-loss archetype), but nothing on the page explains it.

issues.statement: The framing and spread lines do misfire, but on few cards. Most of what was reported is the rules working as written, and only the House line is a real contradiction. On a pitcher-hand tab, "runs a season" means the hand's share in the spread line but the whole season in the framing line. Separately, three different thresholds decide whether a hitter's choices are "about average".
evidence: Measured over 261 cards x 3 views = 783 plans (script: scratchpad/audit/skeptic_framing/measure.py, output out.json)

(a) 'biggest piece': 14 views on 13 cards, all on hand tabs and none on All pitchers. Coverage is 12% to 21% (under 25% by construction), and on all 14 a single count row on the same tab costs more than the named pitch(es). Turner vs RHP: "Your chase choices cost 7 runs a season, across every count; the pitch above is the biggest piece of it." The leak is "−0.9" and the table shows "Ahead in the count ... −2.5". The others: Goldschmidt R 0.84/5.76, Sanoja L 0.76/4.16, Lowe L 0.76/3.98, DeLuca L 0.81/5.35, Castro L 0.84/5.61, Giménez L 1.0/5.31, Pérez L 1.48/6.98, Clement R and L, Diaz R 2.36/11.2, García R 2.23/12.59, Rafaela R 1.87/12.0, House R

(b) House vs RHP, the only view where the plan's pitch sits outside the counts the line names (1 of 783). "With two strikes, let fastballs above the zone go... With two strikes, your choices are a plus overall (+0.6 runs in the count table); this pitch is where they give some back." Then: "Your chase choices cost 4 runs a season, on the first pitch, when you're ahead in the count and at 0-1 or 1-1 rather than in one spot; the pitch above is the biggest piece of it." vs RHP table: First pitch −1.2, Ahead −2.9, 0-1 or 1-1 −1.0, Two strikes +0.6

(c) Of the 5 spread lines that list counts, 2 list one that costs under 0.5 runs. Ballesteros vs LHP lists 0-1 or 1-1 at −0.34 and Peraza vs LHP lists it at −0.48: "Your chase choices cost 4 runs a season, when you're ahead in the count, at 0-1 or 1-1 and with two strikes rather than in one spot; the count table shows where."

(d) 7 views say 'Start ...' with no pitch to act on, all vs LHP tabs with no leak: Albies, Schmitt, Mangum, Moniak, Ballesteros ('Start with two strikes'), Abrams ('Start on the first pitch') and Peraza ('Start when you're ahead in the count'). Albies vs LHP: "No single pitch here is a clear take. Your chase choices cost 9 runs a season, across every count; the count table shows where. Start with two strikes, where it costs the most." All 7 hitters have two pitch lines on All pitchers

(e) None of the 23 hand-tab 'cost N runs a season' sentences names the hand. On 3 views N is larger than the header tile's total: Crow-Armstrong vs RHP 7 vs tile "−6.2", Goldschmidt vs RHP 6 vs tile "−2.4", House vs RHP 4 vs tile "−2.5"

(e2) The reverse case, not in the report: on 126 hand-tab views the framing line quotes the all-pitchers total, and on 20 cards the tab's own table shows a loss. Rengifo vs LHP: "Overall your chase choices are better than average (+2.6 runs a season): the pitch above is one spot to tighten, not a new approach." while the same tab shows "All counts 274 ... −4.7". Others: Swanson, Edman, Chisholm, Jung, Ramos, Devers, Abreu, Moreno, Guerrero, Machado, Crews and 9 more

(f) 10 hitters at −1 < choices ≤ 0 have pitch lines but no framing line on All pitchers: Taveras −0.33, Ohtani −0.67, Palacios −0.42, Realmuto −0.95, Harper −0.93, Hamilton −0.71, Adames −0.43, Cam Smith −0.36, Gorman −0.28, Caissie −0.78. Meanwhile 19 hitters at 0 < c < 1 are framed 'about average'. Taveras: tile "Choices −0.3", leaks "−2.9" and "−1.2", and the plan goes straight from line 2 to "Keep swinging at strikes; your fastball decisions are a strength."

(f2) The fallback calls losses down to −2.9 'about average', on 12 hand-tab views, and prints an ASCII hyphen. Brandon Marsh vs LHP: "Your chase choices are about average overall (-2.9 runs a season); you give back about 1 run a season when you're ahead in the count."

(g) The 'X, Y and Z rather than in one spot' form appears on 5 views (Massey all, DeLuca L, Ballesteros L, Peraza L, House R). Massey: "Your chase choices cost 9 runs a season, when you're ahead in the count, at 0-1 or 1-1 and with two strikes rather than in one spot; the two pitches above are two of the pieces, the ones to work on first."
issues.method: I read BRIEF.md and step 17's plan_items, spread_line, framing_line and fallback_line (lines 644-850), plus plan_checks.py's checks on the framing line. I wrote skeptic_framing/measure.py over dump_2026.json's data.players, covering the plan_items, plan_items_by_hand, tables and leaks of all 261 cards in 3 views. For each claim it computes coverage (plan leaks' runs / the view's loss), whether the pitch's count row is a plus, listed counts costing under 0.5 runs, 'Start' lines with no pitch, hand-tab N against the tile's choices, and whether the framing line fires near zero. I checked the quotes against the cards' printed aside text and the dossiers for House and Albies, and read the plan heading in the template (player_cards.html:929).
issues.why_it_matters: The framing line tells a hitter how big the problem is and where it sits. "The biggest piece" of a loss that is 85% somewhere else reads as most of it. On House's vs RHP tab the line puts the loss in three counts and then calls a pitch from the fourth its biggest piece. On a hand tab, a seasonal run number that is sometimes the hand's and sometimes the whole season disagrees with the header tile or the tab's own table (Rengifo is "better than average" over a −4.7 table). None of this changes what a hitter should take, so the pitch instructions stand. It does weaken the trust coaches put in the numbers when the player is in the room. Most of it is by design: the spread line only fires under 25% coverage, "biggest" means the plan took leaks 1..k, a view with no leaks names its costliest count, and the framing line needs choices above 0.
issues.root_cause:
All in scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:
- spread_line:684 and :681 call the plan's pitch(es) "the biggest piece(s)" whenever they are leaks 1..k (plan_items:832), with no share and no check that the pitch's count is among the counts named.
- spread_line:672 lists every count below 0 (neg), not the 1-run COSTLY_COUNT_RUNS bar the fallback uses.
- spread_line:689: with no pitch, the line ends on a count ("Start ..., where it costs the most").
- spread_line:679: the cost sentence takes the view's own total and never names the hand.
- plan_items:837 passes the all-pitchers summary to framing_line on a hand tab, so that line quotes the season total.
- framing_line:771 gates on c > 0.
- fallback_line:703 calls any c < 1 "about average" and prints it with {choices:+.1f}, an ASCII sign.
- The "rather than in one spot" wording is built at :678.
issues.suggested_fix:
1. In spread_line, say the share instead of "the biggest piece of it", e.g. "the pitch above is the largest single spot in it (about 0.9 of those runs); the rest is spread thin".
2. When a chosen leak's count_group is not in the counts named, drop the "piece" clause.
3. List counts from rows ≤ −COSTLY_COUNT_RUNS rather than < 0, and write "spread over ahead in the count, 0-1 or 1-1 and two strikes" in place of "..., X, Y and Z rather than in one spot".
4. When there is no pitch, end with something to act on. On a hand tab: "The All pitchers plan has the pitches to work on." Otherwise name the far-off rate in the worst count.
5. Pass the view into spread_line and framing_line. On a hand tab write "Against right-handers your chase choices cost N runs a season", and use that hand's rows["total"]["choices"] in framing_line, so one tab never mixes scopes.
6. Use one "about average" band, −1 < c < 1: gate framing_line on c > −1, have fallback_line say "cost you N runs" at −1 or below, and print through fmt_runs. Add the matching checks to plan_checks.py.
refuted_items: Coverage does not set the wording, so the 'flip between tabs with the same coverage' is by design. 'Biggest pieces' vs 'two of the pieces, the ones to work on first' follows whether the plan took leaks 1..k. Diaz All pitchers takes leaks [3, 1] and vs RHP takes [1, 2]; Turner All pitchers takes [3, 1] and vs RHP takes [1]. Every spread line is under 25% coverage by construction, so a 12-21% share is the rule working, not a misfire

Clement and Schmitt are not cases where the hand's N exceeds the card total. Clement's 11 and 7 sit against −17.4 and Schmitt's 4 against −9.2. Only 3 views exceed the tile: Crow-Armstrong, Goldschmidt and House

'The sentence names no hand' holds only for the sentence itself. The heading directly above reads 'What to work on vs right-handers/left-handers' (player_cards.html:929), and N matches the tab's own 'All counts' row in all 23 cases. Only the header tile disagrees

House was reported as high; it is medium. His two-strike instruction stands and the plus-count clause explains it, and the All pitchers plan covers first-pitch and 0-1/1-1 fastballs above the zone. The line confuses where the loss is but does not tell him to do anything wrong

Albies's empty vs LHP leak list does not mean a bug. It is the leak rule (12 pitches, 0.75 runs) applied to a 472-pitch split, his All pitchers plan has two take lines, and the coach's note on that tab covers the vs LHP far-off rate. Only the 'Start with two strikes' wording holds

Taveras holds, but it is by design: plan_checks' 'good chooser unframed' and the BRIEF both define the framing gate as c > 0. It is reported here as an inconsistent band (−0.3 gets no frame, +0.3 gets 'about average', and the fallback calls −2.9 'about average'), not as a broken rule
No 'biggest piece' line appears on any All pitchers view. All 14 are on hand tabs

issues.statement: A switch hitter's leaks count pitches from both batting sides, but each leak's marker, and the picture that opens under the plan's first line, sit on the side where he chased most often, not the side where he chased more than other hitters. On 8 cards the plan's first leak is drawn on the side with less of its excess. For Perdomo and Nuñez that side is one where he chases at the league rate. The caption, the 'mostly vs RHP/LHP' row labels and the unlabeled misses row do not describe any of this. Two of the reported examples are not switch-hitter problems: Reynolds' blue spot and Brooks Lee's inches.
evidence: Scope: 29 of 261 cards are switch hitters. 27 of them have leaks (71 in all). Edwards and Caratini have none. All 71 leaks mix pitches from both sides. On 60 of them (25 cards) the side that is not drawn holds 20% or more of the leak's pitches, and on 36 it holds 30% or more (median 30%, max 64% for Rengifo leak 1).

Side choice: 18 of the 71 leaks get more of their extra chases from the side that is not drawn. 8 of those 18 are the plan's first line, so the card opens on the wrong side: Perdomo, Nuñez, Happ, Bell, Reynolds, Vargas, Heim and Taveras.

Perdomo: plan line 1 is 'With two strikes, let breaking balls below the zone go...', drawn on row 'Batting left', Two strikes, gap -5 (you 60% vs avg 65%), and that picture opens selected: 'Batting left, Two strikes: chases compared with the average hitter. 339 pitches.' Batting left he chased 28 of 60 (46.7%) against a league 46.9%. Batting right he chased 12 of 21 (57% vs 45%). The vs RHP tab says 'Nothing stands out. Your chase choices are about league average or better in every count.' The vs LHP tab says 'With two strikes, let breaking balls below the zone go. You swung at 57% of them; hitters on average swing at 45%.'

Nuñez: plan line 1 is 'With two strikes, let breaking balls below the zone go. You swung at 50% of them; hitters on average swing at 44%.' (28 of 56). Batting left: 19 of 44, 43.2% vs 43.6%. Batting right: 9 of 12, 75% vs 47%. So 3.3 of the leak's extra chases come from batting right and -0.2 from batting left. The marker is on Batting left, Two strikes (gap -2), and the vs LHP tab says 'Nothing stands out.' Screenshot skeptic_switch/nunez_1440.png shows markers 1 and 2 on a pale Batting-left picture, while Batting right, Two strikes has an outlined red spot under the zone with no number.

5 cards draw numbered markers on the 'Batting left · mostly vs RHP' row while their vs RHP tab says 'Nothing stands out. Your chase choices are about league average or better in every count.': Perdomo [1], Rengifo [3], Happ [1,2,3], Bell [1,2,3] (marker gaps +20/+26/+28) and Reynolds [1,2].

Blue spots: 12 of 71 switch-hitter markers (17%) sit on a negative gap, against 50 of 476 (10.5%) on other cards. Only 3 of the 71 leaks have zero or negative excess on the drawn side: Perdomo 1, Nuñez 1 and Brooks Lee 3 (16 of 36, 44.4% vs 45.5%).

Row labels: 'Batting leftmostly vs RHP; inside is on the right' appears on all 29 cards, yet pitches.bin shows 0 batting-left pitches from left-handers for every one of the 29. 'Batting right … mostly vs LHP' has 0 right-handed pitches on 20 of 29. Heim is the only real mix (56 of 358).
Caption: 'Numbered on the pictures, on the row of the hand a leak names.' appears on all 29 switch-hitter cards. Neither of their rows is a hand row, and 56 of the 71 leaks name no hand.

Misses row: 'Misses on chasesswing-and-miss per chase, vs the average hitter: purple more, green fewer' has no side. On all 4 execution-led switch hitters (Lindor, Edman, Taveras, Bailey) it is drawn from batting-left pitches only (Edman 399 of 625). Edman's plan clause 'You miss on 49% of your chases, against 43% for other hitters' uses all pitches (whiff 0.495 vs 0.425).
The design intent is not met: the print-row docstring at 17_build_player_cards.py:1721-1722 says 'so every number sits on a picture of the pitches it counts'.
Screenshots: skeptic_switch/perdomo_1440.png, skeptic_switch/nunez_1440.png, skeptic_switch/edman_1440.png
issues.method: I wrote Python over dump_2026.json covering the 29 switch hitters, their 71 leaks, each marker's row and gap, the hand-tab leak lists and plans, and the row heads. I split every leak cell by batting side using data/cleaned/card_pitches_2026.parquet (pitches and chases match all 547 card leaks exactly), cross-tabbed batting side against pitcher hand from pitches.bin, and read the code in step 17 and the template. I took 1440px screenshots of Perdomo, Nuñez and Edman with a copy of shot.mjs. The scripts are skeptic_switch/measure.py, sides.py and tabs.py, with output in switch.json and sides.json.
issues.why_it_matters:
Drawing a switch hitter's leak on one side is on purpose ("a switch hitter's leaks on the side they came from"), but the code picks that side by how many chases it has, not by where the extra chases are. For Perdomo and Nuñez, the picture that opens under the main instruction shows a side where he chases at the league rate, with the number on a blue or gray spot. The real red spot sits unnumbered on the other row, and the matching hand tab says 'Nothing stands out'. A coach looking for the leak looks at the wrong side of the plate. The plan sentence itself still holds, so this is medium, not high. The caption, the 'mostly' labels and the side-less misses row add confusion on all 29 cards.

Refuted or out of scope:
- Reynolds' -13 spot is not caused by mixing sides. The drawn side does carry extra chases (8 of 22, 36% vs 30%). That is the general marker-spot issue, which also hits 50 of 476 markers on other cards.
- Brooks Lee's 6.6 vs 3.95 inches is real but not a switch-hitter issue. Take-or-video flips between the all-pitchers view and a hand tab hit 15 of 388 leak/tab pairs on other cards. Regions are measured from the batter's side, so mixing two sides works like mixing two pitcher hands. Lee's vs LHP plan leads with breaking balls anyway.
- Heim's 'fallback row' is harmless. All 15 hand-named switch-hitter leaks land on the row whose label names that hand.
- Edman 1, Rengifo 1, Raleigh 3 and Carrigg 3 sit on the side that carries the excess (for example Edman batting right 9 of 13, 69% vs 54%, against batting left 8 of 19, 42% vs 51%). Only the 'picture shows part of the pitches' point holds for them.
- 'Neither hand tab lists it' (Rengifo, Bell) is the general all-pitchers-vs-hand-tab issue: 127 of 476 leaks on other cards appear on neither tab.
issues.root_cause: scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:465-466 and :482 set `side = chased["stand"].mode()`, the side with the most chases, and take x/z from that side's chases only. The leaks themselves pool both sides (leaks(hand_view(p,"all")) at :1059). scripts/templates/player_cards.html:664-666 places markers and :751-752 picks the selected picture. Switch hitters have no hand rows, so both always land on lk.side. Row sublabels are hard-coded 'mostly vs RHP/LHP' at player_cards.html:641-642 and 17_build_player_cards.py:1500-1501. The misses row uses the larger side with no side in its label at player_cards.html:649-650. The caption at player_cards.html:943 is one text for every card.
issues.suggested_fix:
1. At 17_build_player_cards.py:465, pick the side by extra chases, not by chase count: `side = s.assign(_x=s.is_chase - s.e_match).groupby("stand")["_x"].sum().idxmax()`, and take x/z from that side's chases. This moves 18 leaks, including Perdomo's and Nuñez's first lines, and the picture each card opens on. Better still, when the other side holds 20% or more of a leak's pitches, draw the number on both side rows at each side's own spot.
2. Give switch hitters their own caption: 'A switch hitter's leaks count both sides; each number is on the side where most of its extra chases came.'
3. Build the row sublabel from the actual hand share: 'vs RHP' when every pitch came from right-handers (all 29 left rows), and 'mostly vs LHP' only where it is true.
4. Add the side to the misses row label: 'Misses on chases, batting left'.
A bigger option: batting side and pitcher hand are the same split here (0 batting-left pitches from left-handers on all 29 cards), so the leaks could be built per side and the side named in the leak.

issues.statement: On 27 cards, all on the vs LHP tab, the plan says "Nothing stands out. Your chase choices are about league average (or better) in every count." The table right beside it disagrees in one of two ways. On 14 tabs it shows a clear gap: a count where he chases 10+ points more than the league on 30+ pitches, an overall gap of 5+ points, a count printed as −1.0, or a total of −1.5 or worse. On 18 tabs (5 of them overlap the 14) he saw fewer than 150 pitches from that hand, so there is too little to judge any count. The narrower claim does not hold. A single count at −0.5 to −0.99 runs, or a 5 to 9 point gap, sits within what the card itself calls "about average", so the "31 hand tabs and 2 all-pitchers plans" sweep is mostly harmless; 128 of the 190 fallback views are clean.
evidence: Sweep of all 783 views (261 cards x All/RHP/LHP): 190 print 'Nothing stands out' (28 all-pitchers, 162 hand tabs). 128 are clean. 35 are mild only (one count with a 5-9 point gap or −0.5 to −0.99 runs, nothing else). 27 hold: 14 with a rate, print or total contradiction and 18 thin (5 both). All 27 are vs LHP tabs on 27 different cards.

Sánchez vs LHP: "Nothing stands out. Your chase choices are about league average in every count." The table beside it reads "First pitch | 21 | 43% / 19% ... −0.6", "Ahead in the count | 15 | 53% / 26% ... −0.9", "0-1 or 1-1 | 5 | 100% / 37% ... −0.5", "Two strikes | 16 | 56% / 37% ... −0.7", "All counts | 57 | 54% / 28% ... −2.6". Per pitch his choices cost 46 runs per 1,000 pitches vs LHP, against 18 per 1,000 in his All pitchers view, which gets a two-line plan.
Simpson vs LHP: same sentence; "First pitch | 88 | 32% / 22% ... −0.8", "Ahead in the count | 34 | 47% / 28% ... −0.8", "All counts | 302 | 37% / 29% ... −1.6". This is not a small sample.
Benintendi vs LHP: same sentence; "Ahead in the count | 11 | 55% / 27%", "Two strikes | 39 | 49% / 38% ... −0.8", "All counts | 96 | 41% / 28% ... −1.8".

Printed −1.0, opposite verdicts. Montgomery vs LHP gets "Nothing stands out..." beside "Ahead in the count | 35 | 43% / 26% | 33% / 13% | 33% / 42% | .308 / .354 | −1.0 | −0.7" (raw −0.987); McCarthy vs LHP has ahead at −1.0 (raw −0.977) at 32%/22%. Buxton vs LHP has ahead at −1.0 (raw −1.041) at 39%/26% and reads "No single pitch stands out. Your chase choices are about average overall (-0.7 runs a season); you give back about 1 run a season when you're ahead in the count." Luis García vs LHP (ahead raw −1.011) is treated the same way.

Thin tabs: Cortes vs LHP "Ahead in the count | 2 | 50% / 12%", "All counts | 30 | 30% / 22%"; Keith vs LHP "All counts | 37" with every count at 8-11 pitches; Yastrzemski 67, Pederson 88, Benintendi 96, Vivas 103, Lowe 104, Gilbert 107, Larnach 110, Meckler 111, Peters 114, Palacios 116, Nootbaar 119, Beavers 139, Carter 140, Sheets 146, Lukes 148.

Structural: of the 31 hand tabs under 150 pitches, none has a pitch plan (18 'Nothing stands out', 11 contact lines, 2 'No single pitch'). From 150 to 250 pitches, 7 of 39 do; above 400, 215 of 298 do.

Other plan kinds on thin tabs (asked for): 11 contact lines and 2 'No single pitch' lines. The contact line quotes the season's miss rates, not the tab's. Conforto vs LHP (21 pitches) reads "you miss on 51% of your chases, against 42%" above "All counts | 21 | 24% / 32% | 14% / 24% | 60% / 52%".

Related, belongs to the hand-tab vs All pitchers pattern and is not counted here: Grissom's All pitchers step 1 is "With two strikes, mostly against left-handers, let breaking balls below the zone go. You swung at 63% of them; hitters on average swing at 45%." while his vs LHP tab says "Nothing stands out. Your chase choices are about league average or better in every count." Andrew Vaughn and Paul Goldschmidt match this; James Wood, Drew Gilbert and Jorbit Vivas match it with a video item.
issues.method: Read fallback_line, plan_items and count_table in scripts/17_build_player_cards.py and the hand-tab rendering in player_cards.html; confirmed plan_checks.py has no fallback check. Ran skeptic_nso/sweep.py and skeptic_nso/classify.py over all 261 players and 3 views in dump_2026.json. For each 'Nothing stands out' view I compared the raw and printed count runs, the printed chase gaps (with pitch counts), the total and the tab size. I also checked plan kind by hand-tab size, runs per pitch against the All pitchers view, counts printed −1.0 that other cards name as costly, and the rendered aside text for every reported card.
issues.why_it_matters: The fallback firing is by design: no count reaches −1.0 raw runs. Hand-tab runs are scaled to the whole season (600 season PA), so a hand he rarely faces almost never reaches that bar. The sentence turns "too little volume to cost a run" into a verdict, "about league average in every count", and the Chases column beside it shows 47% against 28%, or 54% against 28%. The code's own comment (line 545) promises "Nothing stands out" only "when the count table agrees". A coach reading the vs LHP tab with the player is told there is nothing to work on against lefties exactly where the hitter is worst per pitch, or where there are too few pitches to know. The All pitchers plan, the card's main instruction, is untouched on these 27 cards, so this is medium, not high.
issues.root_cause: scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:817 tests the raw value (rows[g]["choices"] <= -COSTLY_COUNT_RUNS) rather than the printed one, so −0.98 prints as −1.0 and still counts as not costly. strength_clause at :747 decides on the printed value, so the two disagree. fallback_line (:693-699) checks runs only, never the Chases column or the tab's pitch count, and asserts "about league average ... in every count". count_table (:446, called at :1056) scales hand-tab runs by the season's 600/PA on that hand's pitches only, so thin tabs cannot reach the 1-run bar. plan_checks.py has no fallback check.
issues.suggested_fix: (1) At :817, decide on the printed value: costly = [g for g in COUNT_GROUPS if round(stored(rows[g]["choices"]), 1) <= -COSTLY_COUNT_RUNS]. Montgomery and McCarthy then get the 'No single pitch stands out ... about 1 run when you're ahead' line, as Buxton does. (2) Pass view into fallback_line. On a hand tab with under 150 pitches, return "Too few pitches against left-handers to say; pick All pitchers for your plan." (3) Change the claim to what the rule tests: "Nothing stands out. No count costs you a full run a season." When a count with 30+ pitches prints a 10+ point gap, add "(you do chase more than most hitters when you're ahead, 47% against 28%, but it has cost little)". (4) Add a plan_checks.py guard: no 'Nothing stands out' beside a printed −1.0, a 10+ point gap on 30+ pitches, a 5+ point overall gap, or a hand tab under 150 pitches.
refuted_items: A count at −0.5 to −0.99 runs or a 5 to 9 point gap, with nothing else wrong, is not a contradiction. The card calls up to about a run 'about average' (fallback_line even calls −2.9 overall 'about average'). This clears the 2 all-pitchers plans: William Contreras (+2.8 total; first pitch 20%/17%, −0.5) and Jacob Young (+5.9; 0-1 or 1-1 36%/36%, −0.6). It also clears Pete Alonso (+0.5), Isaac Collins (+0.4), George Springer vs RHP (+5.2) and all (+9.0), Austin Martin (+7.4), Vladimir Guerrero (+2.5), A. J. issues.statement: Confirmed, and wider than reported: (a) "So a pitch that is clearly off is a take" followed by "Nothing on this card is a take rule" appears in 6 views on 5 cards, not 2. (b) "You miss about as often" is printed beside tables showing a 5+ point gap in either direction in 16 views on 9 cards. (d, new) On every pitcher-hand tab, the contact sentence uses the all-pitchers miss rate, contact runs and head. On 10 cards, that tab's own table shows contact as a plus or as the smaller cost. (c) holds only weakly: the clause's reason is about his contact overall, the leak's contact is never printed, and the take still stands on choices.
evidence: (a) 6 views / 5 cards with a contact line plus the video-only closing line: Cam Smith all and vs RHP, Josh Jung vs RHP, Nick Gonzales vs RHP, Francisco Lindor vs LHP, Heliot Ramos vs RHP. Cam Smith all: "Your bigger issue is contact: you miss on 49% of your chases, against 42% for other hitters on the same pitches. So a pitch that is clearly off is a take even when you could reach it." ... "Keep swinging at strikes. Nothing on this card is a take rule for you yet: the staff takes the pitch above to video with you first."

(a)+(e) On 4 of those 5 cards, the hand tab's 'Nothing on this card is a take rule' is also false for the card itself, because the All pitchers plan has take lines: Jung R (all view has 2 takes, e.g. "At 0-1 or 1-1, let changeups and splitters below the zone go."), Gonzales R, Lindor L, Heliot Ramos R (all view: "When you're ahead in the count, let breaking balls below the zone go."). The same keep line appears on 6 other hand tabs with no contact line: Josh Bell L, Kyle Karros L, Paul Goldschmidt R, Jo Adell L, Ty France R, Trea Turner R.

(b) 'You miss about as often' while the shown table has him missing 5+ points LESS: Cedric Mullins all "You miss about as often as other hitters do, but what you hit on a chase goes nowhere" vs table "All counts 1,048 31%29% 21%19% 32%42%" (vs RHP 32%/41%, vs LHP 33%/43%); Josh Jung all 38%/44% (vs RHP 41%/46%, vs LHP 31%/38%); David Hamilton vs RHP 37%/43%; Jake Cronenworth vs LHP 37%/42%. 8 views / 4 cards.

(b) 'About as often' beside a printed gap of 5+ points MORE: Joe Mack all 46%/41% (raw 0.4633 vs 0.4138 = 4.95 pts) and vs RHP 48%/41%; Kyle Manzardo all 50%/45% (raw 0.5000 vs 0.4508 = 4.92) and vs LHP 63%/52%; David Hamilton vs LHP "you miss about as often as other hitters do" vs table 47%/36%; Jared Young vs LHP 52%/43%; Jazz Chisholm vs LHP 56%/48%; Gunnar Henderson vs LHP 51%/46%. 8 views / 6 cards.

(d) Cam Smith vs LHP, the tab's only plan line: "Your bigger issue is contact: you miss on 49% of your chases, against 42% for other hitters on the same pitches." The table directly below: "All counts 341 31%33% 19%24% 40%40% .319.309 −0.9 +3.0" (misses even, contact +3.0 runs). The tab also says "The plan for this pitcher hand only".

(d) Josh Jung vs LHP: "Your issue is contact, not choices: you miss about as often as other hitters do, but what you hit on a chase goes nowhere (over a season your chases cost you 2 runs more...)" vs table "All counts 256 25%31% 16%22% 31%38% .385.309 +1.8 +1.1".

(d) Francisco Lindor vs RHP, step 1: "...contact is your bigger cost, so this one is a take even when you could reach it." The vs RHP table: "All counts 720 ... 44%43% .336.317 +0.7 +0.7" (contact is a plus on that hand).

(d) Patrick Bailey vs RHP: "You miss on 50% of your chases, against 43% for other hitters on the same pitches: contact is your bigger cost" vs table "All counts 555 32%31% 24%22% 47%44% .311.317 −3.3 −1.7" (on that hand, choices are the bigger cost and misses differ by 3 points).
(d) Tommy Edman vs RHP: "Your issue is contact, not choices: you miss on 49% of your chases, against 43%" vs table "47%41% .297.317 +2.4 +0.1".

(d) Counts: the tab's Contact total is a plus on 7 hand views (Cam Smith L +3.0, Jung L +1.1, Griffin Conine L +0.8, Lindor R +0.7, Manzardo L +0.6, Conforto L +0.5 on 21 pitches, Edman R +0.1). The tab's choices loss exceeds its contact loss on 3 (Bailey R −3.3/−1.7, Jake Burger R −5.8/−4.3, Gonzales R −1.4/−1.3). On 58 of 62 hand views that quote a miss rate, the rate is not the tab's own. On 22 of 24 'about as often' hand views, the quoted runs are not the tab's (Cronenworth vs LHP "cost you 8 runs" vs table −1.0). All 43 execution-led cards are affected.

(d) Head mismatches on hand tabs: 'Your bigger issue is contact' where the tab's choices are a plus (7 views: Cam Smith R +0.6, Bailey L +1.3, Burger L +0.6, Walker L +0.4, Adames L +0.2, Gonzales L +0.1, Duran L +0.1). 'Your issue is contact, not choices' where the tab's choices cost runs (8 views, e.g. Jung R −1.5, Heliot Ramos R −1.4).

(c) The clause sits on a take whose own leak contact is meaningfully positive (≥ +0.25 runs) on 9 views / 8 cards: Hamilton all +1.78 (choices −3.09), Stowers R +0.65, Lindor R +0.62, Austin Riley R +0.57, Cronenworth R +0.52 and all +0.49, Taveras all +0.44, Jung all +0.43, Okamoto R +0.33. Across all views, 24 have contact > 0, but 15 of those are below +0.25 and 10 are effectively zero (≤ +0.05).
Script output: scratchpad/audit/contact_misfires.py, contact_misfires2.py, contact_union.py over dump_2026.json. 43 execution-led hitters, 129 views carrying a contact sentence.
issues.method: I read contact_why / contact_line / contact_clause / keep_line / plan_items / start_with in scripts/17_build_player_cards.py (lines 549, 710-738, 785-847, 853-865, 1061-1069), the roster fallback in scripts/templates/player_cards.html:1028, and the plan_checks.py 'contact first' guard. I then ran three Python scripts over dump_2026.json covering all 261 cards × 3 views (plan_items, plan_items_by_hand, per-view tables and leaks). The checks: every view with a contact item and the video-only keep line; every 'miss about as often' sentence against the raw and printed gap of the view's own All counts row; every 'contact is your bigger cost' pitch against its leak's contact (and other takes in the plan); every hand-tab contact sentence against that tab's miss rates, contact and choices totals. I also checked the roster rows and re-read the printed right column (card aside text) for Cam Smith, Jung, Mullins, Mack, Manzardo, Hamilton, Lindor, Conforto, Edman, Conine, Heliot Ramos, Gonzales, Cronenworth and Bailey.
issues.why_it_matters: These are the only lines that tell a contact-led hitter what kind of problem he has. Several are contradicted by the table printed right under them. Cam Smith's vs LHP tab says contact is his bigger issue beside 40%/40% misses and +3.0 contact runs. Mullins is told he misses 'about as often' beside 32% vs 42%. Some tabs say a pitch 'is a take' and, in the same plan, that 'nothing on this card is a take rule'. A coach going through the card with the player in the room loses trust in the numbers and has to explain the card away. The player's actual action is not reversed in any case: take clearly-off pitches, and the video items stay video items. That is why this is medium, not high. Partly by design: the contact reason is folded into the first take on purpose, and archetype is a hitter-level label from step 13. But nothing in the code anticipates a contact line next to video items, a negative miss gap, or hand-tab numbers.
issues.root_cause: scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:715. contact_why gates on the RAW gap and only upward, so any gap below +5 (including −10) and raw 4.9 gaps that print as 5 fall to 'you miss about as often' (line 718). rate_gap (589) uses printed ints for pitch lines. :731 contact_line always adds 'So a pitch that is clearly off is a take'; its docstring calls it 'the plan's one line', but plan_items:840-841 also inserts it when every pitch item is a video item. keep_line:791-793 then adds 'Nothing on this card is a take rule'. :737 contact_clause says 'so this one is a take' and is appended to takes[0] (:825) whatever that leak's contact is. :1067 the hand-tab plan_items gets the all-pitchers `summary`, so contact_why / contact_line's head (:729, summary['choices']) / contact_clause quote all-pitchers whiff, contact and choices on a tab that says 'The plan for this pitcher hand only'. contact_led (:823) is also the hitter-level archetype, so a hand where contact is a plus still gets the contact sentence. Not guarded: plan_checks.py:112 only flags a contact line placed before a take.
issues.suggested_fix: 1) In plan_items for a hand tab, pass a per-hand summary: {**summary, whiff/whiff_league/contact/choices from tables[h] 'total'}. Add the contact sentence on that tab only when that hand's contact < 0 and −contact ≥ max(−choices, 0); otherwise use the normal fallback or plain take lines. 2) In contact_why, use printed ints g = pct(whiff) − pct(whiff_league): g ≥ 5 quote the rates; g ≤ −5 'you miss less often than other hitters do (X% vs Y%), but what you hit on a chase does less'; else 'about as often'. 3) In keep_line's video-only branch, drop 'Nothing on this card is a take rule'. Say instead 'The pitch above is not a take rule yet: the staff takes it to video with you first'. This fixes both the clash with the contact line and hand tabs whose all-pitchers plan has takes. 4) contact_clause: say 'contact is your bigger cost, so a pitch that is clearly off is a take even when you could reach it' (about his contact overall, not this pitch). Or keep 'this one' only when the leak's contact < 0. 5) Add plan_checks guards: a contact sentence's rates and runs must match its view's All counts row; 'about as often' only when the printed miss gap is within ±4; no view has both a contact item and 'Nothing on this card'.
refuted_items: 'Cam Smith is the only card whose contact line leads a pitch line': true only for the All pitchers view. On hand tabs, a contact line leads video items on 5 more views (Cam Smith R, Jung R, Gonzales R, Lindor L, Heliot Ramos R).

Roster 'Start with skips the contact line' (Cam Smith): by design. The roster glossary says 'Start with: the plan's first pitch line', and start_with() takes the first pitch item. Harmless. The real inconsistency is the reverse: Connor Norby and Henry Bolte (contact-only plans) show the contact line in Start with through the template fallback (player_cards.html:1028), which is not a pitch line. Low.

'Both shown a Misses row' (Mack, Manzardo) is not evidence of a miss gap. Every execution-led card gets the 'Misses on chases' row by archetype (step 17:1507), including Mullins and Jung, who miss less than average.

(c) on the near-zero cases is refuted as a misfit. On Lindor all +0.014, Edman all/L +0.01, Adames R +0.05, Gorman all/R +0.05, Mayo all +0.02 and Montgomery all/R +0.01, contact on that pitch is simply average. And even on the clear cases (Hamilton +1.78), the take stands on choices (−3.09), the leak's contact is not printed anywhere on the card, and the clause's 'contact is your bigger cost' is true of his chases overall in the All view. So it is a misleading reason, not a wrong instruction.

Severity 'high' for (a) (finding 208): not upheld. The contact line's take rule covers clearly-off pitches, while the video items are within a ball of the zone and explicitly 'not a take rule'. The player's action does not change, so it is a wording contradiction (medium).
Mack/Manzardo 'about as often' at 46%/41% and 50%/45%: real but borderline (raw gap 4.9-4.95). Low on its own. It matters mainly because pitch lines use the printed gap for the same 5-point rule.

The 'did not qualify' claim is never false on the page's own paths: no player id changes slug across 2021-2026, and slug() has not changed since it was added (d39c2e4). The false claim needs a hand-typed or mis-cased hash, so finding 480's medium is too high; low is honest.

issues.why_it_matters: The roster exists so a coach can scan who to work with and what to start with. On every desktop and tablet width, the Start with column (the plan's first line) and Beat are hidden behind a sideways scroll inside a scroll box, with no sign it is there apart from a cut column. Scrolling to them loses the hitter's name, and the off-screen text pads rows with blank space. Landing past the filters, losing your place after each card, sorts that put the smallest leaks or 'none: video only' first, and a filter that always returns nothing make the list harder to work down. The hash notice can tell a coach that a real hitter with a card 'did not qualify', but only for a hand-typed link. The card's own plan is untouched, so this is medium, not high. Some of it is deliberate: Beat sorts by the 'was' number on purpose (key = "excess"), scrollTop = 0 is meant for a new sort or filter, and the notice was written for the season switcher. Each still confuses the cases described here.
issues.root_cause:
All in scripts/templates/player_cards.html unless noted:
- Off-screen columns: COLS puts plan last (1031-1037), with .roster table min-width 1560px (184) in a .scroll box (183) inside .wrap max-width 1440px (55), and no sticky first columns. The phone card layout only starts at max-width 720px (205).
- Landing past the controls: section id="roster" (343) matches the #roster hash, so the browser jumps to it.
- Phone glossary: it is placed after the table (350); the Team cell is bold and first (209); td flex space-between (208) puts the noted tag at the far end.
- Sorts: Beat uses key = "excess" (1063); numeric columns start descending (1056); text columns sort with localeCompare; the state line uses .toLowerCase() and ', most first' for any reversed column (1089).
- Dead filter: the 'contact' option is hard-coded (273), and scripts/13_build_actionability_profiles.py:232 never assigns execution-only.
- Lost place: renderRoster always sets scrollTop = 0 (1071), and applyHash calls renderRoster on every return.
- Hash notice: applyHash's fallback (1138-1142) treats any unmatched slug as a hitter from another season, title-cases the slug, and always uses D.references[0] (the right-handed reference). parseHash (391-395) matches slugs and 'roster' exactly. The season switcher stores only the name (407). render() rewrites the hash to the reference slug (1006).
issues.suggested_fix:
1) Roster columns:
- Move Start with (and Beat) right after Hitter in COLS, or move Bats/PA/Contact behind the row tap.
- Make Team and Hitter sticky (th/td:nth-child(-n+2) { position: sticky; left: 0; background: var(--surface) }).
- Let the phone card layout run up to about 1100px.

2) Rename the section id (e.g. id="roster-view", updating the #roster .scroll selectors) or call scrollTo(0,0) in applyHash for the roster view.

3) Lost place: set scrollTop = 0 only in the sort, search and filter handlers. Save the box's scrollTop (or window.scrollY on phones) when a name is clicked and restore it on return.

4) Sorts:
- Beat by t.predicted, with 'no target' and video-only rows last.
- First click on Leak runs (and Choices) shows the biggest loss first.
- Rank maps for Problem (choices < mostly choices < mixed < mostly contact) and Count check (struggling < average < hitting well).
- Keep the label's case, and say 'Z to A' rather than 'most first' for word columns.

5) Build the Problem options from the kinds present in ROSTER.

6) Phone: put the glossary in a <details> above the list, lead each row with the hitter, and keep the noted tag next to the name.

7) Hash notice:
- Match slugs case- and accent-insensitively (fold, and squash non-alphanumerics to '_'), and match 'roster' case-insensitively.
- Say 'did not qualify' only when chaseFrom is set. Otherwise say 'No 2026 card matches "<hash>"', without title-casing the slug.
- Store bats with chaseFrom and open the matching reference card.

issues.statement: The coach's note is printed word for word on the vs RHP and vs LHP tabs, directly under that tab's plan. On those tabs it names "the plan's first line", "second line", "two lines" or "first take", and in most cases that line is not the one printed above it. This hits 15 of the 17 noted hitters and 26 of their 34 hand tabs. On 20 tabs (12 hitters) the first line is wrong: 13 tabs open with a different pitch and 7 have no pitch line at all. Only Peña and Neto are clean. The note always matches the All pitchers plan, so the main instruction survives, and the severity is medium, not high.
evidence: Code: scripts/templates/player_cards.html:931 `if (p.coach_note) sec.append(el("div", { class: "coach" } ... p.coach_note));` has no state.hand condition. In the dump the note text is inside aside['all'], aside['R'] and aside['L'] for all 17 noted hitters.

Rendered order on a hand tab (salvador_perez vs RHP, shots/salvador_perez_1440_tabR.png): "What to work on vs right-handers" / "1 At 0-1 or 1-1, let breaking balls down and away go." / "The plan for this pitcher hand only; pick All pitchers for the full plan." / "COACH'S NOTE, FOR THE STAFF At 0-1 or 1-1, breaking balls below the zone: the plan's first line, where the take costs nothing in strikeouts."

Pérez vs LHP: plan (1) "With two strikes, let breaking balls below the zone go." The same note says the first line is the take "where the take costs nothing in strikeouts". Goodman's "the free part, since the take costs nothing in strikeouts" has the same problem: both his tabs open with "With two strikes, let breaking balls below the zone go."

Duran vs RHP: plan (1) "When you're ahead in the count, let fastballs above the zone go." (2) "When you're ahead in the count, let breaking balls below the zone go." The note says "With two strikes, mostly against right-handers, breaking balls below the zone: the plan's first line", and that pitch is the tab's leak (1), "55% vs 40% avg · 31 of 56 −2.3", which is not on the tab's plan.

Duran vs LHP and Montgomery vs LHP: the only plan line is "Your bigger issue is contact: you miss on 60% [68%] of your chases...". The notes still say "the plan's first line" and "the plan's first take ... the plan's second line".

Moniak vs RHP: plan (2) "At 0-1 or 1-1, let breaking balls below the zone go." The note says "The second line, breaking balls below the zone with two strikes, mostly against right-handers, is the bigger leak". The two-strike breaking ball is the RHP tab's leak (1), −2.8, and it is not in the RHP plan.

Harris vs RHP: the note is explicitly about right-handers ("that right-handers throw him with two strikes ... the changeups and splitters among them are the plan's second line"), but the vs RHP plan's (2) is "With two strikes, let breaking balls down and in go."

Albies vs RHP: plan (1) "At 0-1 or 1-1, let breaking balls below the zone go." The note says "With two strikes, changeups and splitters below the zone: the plan's first line and his biggest leak." On this tab that pitch is leak 2 and is not in the plan. Albies vs LHP: "No single pitch here is a clear take. Your chase choices cost 9 runs a season, across every count", with the leak list "None worth 0.75 runs per 600 PA."

García vs RHP: plan (1) "When you're ahead in the count, let breaking balls below the zone go." The note's "fastballs above the zone: the plan's first line" is neither in the RHP plan nor on its leak list. García vs LHP: "No single pitch stands out. Your chase choices are about average overall (-2.3 runs a season)..."

Clement: note "On the first pitch, fastballs above the zone: the plan's first line." The vs RHP tab's (1) is "When you're ahead in the count, let fastballs above the zone go." (its first pitch choices are −1.5 with no leak). The vs LHP tab's (1) is "With two strikes, let fastballs above the zone go."
