issues.method: I read player_cards.html aside() (lines 918-950), step 17's summary build (lines 1050-1070) and plan_pitch_items/plan_items (lines 631-847), coach_notes.py NOTED and check() (lines 433-460), and plan_checks.py (lines 245-256). I wrote skeptic_coachnote/measure.py over dump_2026.json covering all 261 players, 17 of whom have a note. For each note I hand-coded the plan lines it names, in order, and asserted that they equal the All pitchers plan's pitch cells (true for all 17). I asserted that the note text appears in all three rendered asides (true for all 17). Then I compared each hand tab's pitch-line cells with the note's lines and found where the note's lead leak ranks on that tab's leak list. I re-read the rendered aside text for Duran and Pérez, viewed shots/salvador_perez_1440_tabR.png, and checked every quote in the 13 reviewer findings against the dump. I also counted how many tabs would be fixed by passing note_start to the hand plans.
issues.why_it_matters: The coach's note is the staff's script, and the brief says coaches use the card with the player in the room. On 26 of the 34 hand tabs, the note says "the plan's first line is X" right under a plan that opens with Y, has no line at all, or puts the lines in the other order. A coach then has to choose between the staff text and the player text, or concludes the card is wrong. The sharpest cases are Duran vs RHP, Moniak vs RHP and Harris vs RHP: each note talks about right-handers, and the vs RHP plan leaves out the very pitch the note names. The ordering rule causes that and works as designed, but the note makes it look like an error. Severity is medium, not high, for three reasons. The note always matches the All pitchers plan, which is the default view, the card's main instruction, and is enforced by coach_notes.check. The tab says "pick All pitchers for the full plan" just above the note. Following either the note or the tab's plan gives the player a legitimate take that the card supports, so no player is pushed into a wrong action.
issues.root_cause: The template, scripts/templates/player_cards.html:931, adds p.coach_note to the plan section on every view: `if (p.coach_note) sec.append(...)` has no `state.hand === "all"` test. The hand plans are rebuilt from the hand's own leaks without the note's lead, at scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:1067: `plan_items(summary["leaks"][h], summary, summary["tables"][h], view=h)` has no start=. The guard in scripts/coach_notes.py:449-452 checks only p["plan_items"] (the all-pitchers plan), and plan_checks.check (lines 252-255) checks hand plans but never the note. So nothing catches the mismatch. Not by design: commit 4a9572a meant notes to "open where the card does", but it only handled the All pitchers view.
issues.suggested_fix: At player_cards.html:931, show the note only on All pitchers: `if (p.coach_note && state.hand === "all") ...`. On a hand tab, add one muted line in its place, e.g. "The coach's note is on the All pitchers view." That fixes all 26 tabs in one place, and it matches the print card and static images, which already show the note only with the all-pitchers plan. Passing start=summary["note_start"] to the hand plans at step 17:1067 is not enough on its own. plan_pitch_items ignores a start cell that is not on that hand's leak list, so it fixes only 4 of the 20 first-line tabs (Martínez R, Albies R, Duran R, Giménez R). It fixes none of the 7 tabs with no pitch line and none of the later-line mismatches. Also add a check to coach_notes.check, or to plan_checks: whenever the note is shown with a plan, the first pitch cell of that plan must equal note_start. That way a later change cannot bring the mismatch back.
refuted_items: Severity 'high' (reviewers i=1, 102, 207, 342, and the issue): not supported. The note always matches the All pitchers plan (default view, checked by coach_notes.check), the tab says 'pick All pitchers for the full plan' just above the note, and acting on either the note or the tab plan gives a take the card supports. No wrong action or missing plan results, so medium.

Count '9 of 17 noted hitters (15 tabs) by first line' (issue and i=441): undercount. 12 hitters and 20 tabs have a first line different from the note's (13 a different pitch, 7 no pitch line). 9 hitters and 13 tabs is the count if tabs with no pitch line are left out.

Count '19 of 34 tabs disagree with the note in some way' (issue and i=503): undercount. 26 of 34 tabs (15 of 17 hitters) disagree on the first line or on a later line the note names. Only Peña and Neto are clean on both tabs.

Rafaela vs LHP (i=138: 'one line only, but the note still says ... it is next'): weak. The note's first line matches that tab's only line, two-strike fastballs above the zone. 'it is next' points to early-count chasing that the LHP tab has no leak for, so it is a soft mismatch and is not counted in the 26.

Caballero vs LHP and Peraza vs RHP, which reviewers named for the other tab: both of these tabs match the note exactly. Only Caballero R (second line: breaking balls off the plate away instead of below the zone) and Peraza L (no pitch line) are affected.

Montgomery vs RHP: matches the note (ahead breaking balls below the zone, then the same pitch with two strikes). Only his vs LHP tab is affected. Severity 'low' (i=328) is too low for the shared pattern.

Every quoted plan and note text in the 13 reviewer findings was checked against the dump and is accurate, including Clement vs RHP first pitch −1.5 with no first-pitch leak, Duran vs RHP leak '55% vs 40% avg · 31 of 56 −2.3', and García vs RHP having no fastball-above-the-zone leak.

issues.statement: On a hand tab with no leak and a choices loss under 3 runs, the "No single pitch stands out" fallback calls the hitter "about average overall" for any total below +1. That puts nine vs LHP tabs with losses of −1.4 to −2.9 in the same bucket as −0.2, while −3.75 (Mangum) is told it costs 4 runs. The same line prints its number with Python's ASCII hyphen ("-2.9") where every table and tile on the page uses "−". That hits all 12 negative fallbacks.
evidence: Scope: 783 views (261 cards x all/R/L). 14 'No single pitch stands out' fallbacks, all on hand tabs (12 vs LHP, 2 vs RHP), none on the all-pitchers view or the print card. 9 print a total of −1.0 or worse as 'about average'. 12 print an ASCII '-'. The 9 are a subset of the 12. In the rendered aside every text matches the data exactly, hyphen included.

Marsh vs LHP: "No single pitch stands out. Your chase choices are about average overall (-2.9 runs a season); you give back about 1 run a season when you're ahead in the count." Same tab's table: "All counts | 246 | 42%33% | 32%22% | ... | −2.9 | −1.9"

Diaz vs LHP: "Your chase choices are about average overall (-2.7 runs a season); you give back about 1 run a season at 0-1 or 1-1." Table: "0-1 or 1-1 ... −1.1", "Two strikes ... −1.0" (raw −0.983, so it is not a costly count and the line leaves it out), "All counts | 171 | 43%33% | 32%21% ... −2.7"
Marte vs LHP: "about average overall (-2.6 runs a season); you give back about 2 runs a season with two strikes." Table: "All counts | 270 | 37%30% | 28%22% ... −2.6"
Crawford vs LHP: "(-2.5 runs a season); you give back about 2 runs a season with two strikes". Table: "All counts | 122 | 40%32% | 35%23%"
Johnston vs LHP: "(-2.4 runs a season); you give back about 1 run a season at 0-1 or 1-1". Table: "All counts | 193 | 39%29% | 32%20% ... −2.4"
García vs LHP: "(-2.3 runs a season); you give back about 1 run a season when you're ahead in the count". Table: "All counts | 166 | 42%31% | 30%22%"

Lee vs LHP: "(-2.1 runs a season); ... with two strikes". Griffin vs LHP: "(-2.1 runs a season); ... when you're ahead in the count". France vs LHP: "about average overall (-1.4 runs a season); you give back about 2 runs a season when you're ahead in the count"

Hyphen only, level correct: Buxton "(-0.7 runs a season)" (table −0.7), Wells "(-0.3 runs a season)" (table −0.3), Frelick "(-0.2 runs a season)" (table −0.2). The template's runs() prints '−' (player_cards.html:481).
Contrast: Mangum vs LHP (raw −3.750): "No single pitch here is a clear take. Your chase choices cost 4 runs a season, across every count; the count table shows where."

The named counts cover only 36-57% of the loss in 8 of the 9 cases: Marsh 1.16 of 2.92, Diaz 1.06 of 2.66, Johnston 1.05 of 2.35, García 1.01 of 2.33, Griffin 1.10 of 2.11, Lee 1.40 of 2.13, Marte 1.51 of 2.62. Crawford is 2.23 of 2.47.
League context, vs LHP tab totals over 261 hitters: median +0.2, SD 3.2. −2.9 is in the bottom 13%, −2.1 in the bottom 20%, −1.4 in the bottom 26%.
Scripts: skeptic_fallbackavg/measure.py, context.py, verify.py; results in skeptic_fallbackavg/rows.json
issues.method: I read fallback_line, framing_line, spread_line and plan_items in scripts/17_build_player_cards.py, plus the framing check in scripts/plan_checks.py. A script over dump_2026.json pulled every plan item of kind 'fallback' in plan_items and plan_items_by_hand for all 261 hitters. For each 'No single pitch stands out' text it parsed the level and number, compared them with the view's By count table (the raw values and the rendered aside text), and checked the ASCII hyphen, which counts are named against those the table prints at −1.0 or worse, the printed chase gap, and that tab's percentile among all hitters. I also grepped step 17, coach_notes.py and the template for other signed formats that would print an ASCII minus in page text (none).
issues.why_it_matters: A hitter who chases 9 to 11 points more than other hitters against left-handers and loses 2 to 3 runs a season on it reads "about average" next to a table that says otherwise. Losing a bit more (−3.0) flips the wording to "cost 3 runs", so two nearly identical tabs get opposite verdicts. This is not by design: the same file's framing_line already says "cost you N runs" for c <= −1, and plan_checks.py holds framing lines to ±1 run for "about average", but fallback lines are not checked at all. The hyphen is cosmetic, but it is the only signed run figure on the page not printed with fmt_runs. The main instruction survives (no pitch on that tab is a take rule, and the all-pitchers plan is unaffected), so medium, not high.
issues.root_cause: scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:703 `level = "better than average" if choices >= 1 else "about average"` has no c <= −1 branch, unlike framing_line at :773-776. Line 706 `f"({choices:+.1f} runs a season)"` uses Python's ASCII-minus format on the raw value instead of fmt_runs(stored(...)). The fallback is reached at :843 only when no leak makes the tab and the loss is under SPREAD_MIN_RUNS = 3.0 (:552, :831). That is why the wording flips at −3 and why every case is on a hand tab. scripts/plan_checks.py checks only frame lines starting "Overall your" (lines ~140-150) and never checks fallback text.
issues.suggested_fix: In fallback_line, set `c = stored(choices)`. If `c <= -1`, write `f"No single pitch stands out. Your chase choices cost you {runs_phrase(-c)} a season, spread across the counts; the most, about {runs_phrase(cost)}, {where}."`. Otherwise keep the level, but print `({fmt_runs(c)} runs a season)` and set the level from c (>= 1 better, else about average). This ends the 'average' wording for losses, removes the hyphen and a possible '-0.0', and says the named count is only part of the loss. Then add a plan_checks.py rule: any plan text containing 'about average overall (' must quote a value strictly between −1 and +1, and no plan, note or target text may contain an ASCII '-' directly before a digit inside a run figure.
refuted_items: Overstated: 'chases 8 to 11 points above the league against that hand' holds for 5 of the 9 cards (Marsh +9, Diaz +10, Crawford +8, Johnston +10, García +11). Marte is +7, Lee +6, Griffin +4 and France only +2 (33%/31%).
Griffin (i=225): '−2.1 ... is not average (he is 241st of 261)' mixes up his overall xChase+ rank (241) with his vs LHP tab, which is about the 20th percentile of hitters vs LHP, not 241st.

Mostly by design: 'names only one count's 1 run of a 2.7-run loss'. The brief says fallbacks name the costly counts (≤ −1.0 run), so leaving out smaller counts is intended. Only Diaz has a count the table prints as −1.0 (two strikes, raw −0.983) that the line skips, which is a rounding edge, not a missed costly count. It is still confusing next to 'about average', which is why it is folded into the fix.
Not wrong: Buxton (−0.7), Wells (−0.3) and Frelick (−0.2) are correctly 'about average'. Only their hyphen is a defect. Tawa (+0.8) and Acuña (+1.4) are correct on both counts.

France at −1.4 with a 2-point gap is within half an SD of the vs LHP median, so 'about average' is statistically defensible for him. It is still flagged because it breaks the card's own −1-run convention.

issues.statement: 12 of the 17 coach's notes have at least one number or phrase the card cannot back up. They quote a different population, season, baseline or measure than the card prints next to them, give runs with no unit, or mix scales. Two notes (García, Peraza) add a three-ball rule while the player's plan says its pitches are the only changes. Three noted plans (Rafaela, Albies, Duran) start with a two-strike take ahead of a pre-two-strike take. That order is by design, because the note picks the lead, but the web guide and the print card's own "How to read your card" page state the opposite rule with no exception. Several reported sub-claims do not hold: Rafaela's note does not contradict the chart, and its "about 4 runs" is correct. The headline still stands.
evidence: Rafaela note: "His early-count chasing came down in 2025 (35% to 28% of far-off pitches) but is still well above the league's 17% and costs about 4 runs; it is next." coach_notes.py:266-272 checks the 2024 and 2025 rates against the 2026 league rate. The 2026 rate is 27.1% (actionability_2026.csv far_off_chase_rate_lt2k) and appears nowhere on the card. The "4 runs" is decision_A_early_far 2026 = -4.43 per 600 PA, part of the header tile "COST OF FAR-OFF CHASES 12.2", but no unit is given.

Neto note: "The sliders among them from right-handers are the steady part ... in 2026 pitchers threw him far more (290, up from 184)." The leak it says "among them" of: "Two strikes, breaking balls below the zone 69% vs 47% avg · 66 of 95". coach_notes.py:373-384 counts 2026 SL/ST below the zone from RHP in ALL counts (290), and 184 is 2024, not the 2025 the sentence names last. He had 600 PA in 2024 and 697 in 2026.

García note: "Three-ball counts sit inside it, and with three balls his choices cost about 5 runs" vs the table row "Ahead in the count | 176 | ... | −3.9". coach_notes.py:300-301 sums balls == 3, which includes 3-2, and 3-2 is under the column head "Two strikes 0-2 1-2 2-2 3-2". Peraza's note gets this right: "they sit inside 'Ahead in the count' and the 3-2 part of 'Two strikes'".

Peraza note: "(62% chase against about 40%, about 5 runs in 45 pitches ...): swing only at strikes there." The 5 is net of contact per 600 PA (coach_notes.py:395, d.net), while 45 is raw pitches over 367 PA. The plan on the same card says "Keep swinging at strikes. The only changes on this card are the pitches above." García has the same "swing only at strikes there" beside the same closing line, and both notes say the card "cannot show" those counts "yet".

Harris note: "... are about half of what his chases cost him". The check (coach_notes.py:232-236) is a share of the net, choices plus contact (-12.8). The card prints only "Choices −21.8" and "Contact +9.0". "His contact is among the best in this group" means rank 2 of the 9 'easiest' notes (coach_notes.py:239-241), a group the card never names. "so nothing else needs to change" sits beside "0-1 or 1-1 | 297 | 52%31% | 45%21% | ... | −5.0 | −1.2".

Goodman note: "... he chases them 48% of the time against 30% on the same pitches, about 5 runs." The figure has no unit and is net of contact (coach_notes.py:316), while every runs figure on the leak list is choices only. The nearest printed leak is "Ahead in the count, breaking balls below the zone 63% vs 28% avg · 15 of 24 −1.7".

Albies note: "Against left-handers he chases far-off pitches of every kind more (35% vs 19%)." The vs LHP table on the same tab reads "All counts 472 44%26% 35%18%". The note uses the BACKTEST_LEAGUE_CELL expectation (coach_notes.py:91,296; leak_rules.py:62), while the table uses e_match (17_build_player_cards.py:443). "of every kind" is not checked at all.

Caballero note: "(55%, 65%, 77% since 2024)" is two-strike far-off fastballs above the zone only (coach_notes.py:279). The leak reads "Two strikes, fastballs above the zone 81% vs 51% avg · 57 of 70" and Zone numbers show two-strike "above the zone ... 79% / 53% (77)".

Peña note: "The two-strike slider away ... video items, not take rules." The card's leak is "Two strikes, mostly vs RHP, breaking balls away". It is not on the plan, which has only one video line: "At 0-1 or 1-1, mostly against right-handers, breaking balls below the zone are one to go over on video".

Martínez note: "More of what they cost him comes from right-handers than from left-handers, and the contact is there on the swings that stay." He faced RHP on 517 of 767 pitches (67%). Leak RHP shares are 76% and 72%. By the vs RHP tab, leak 2 costs -1.73 over 29 RHP pitches and the rest, -1.23, over 11 LHP pitches.

Tovar note: "With two strikes, breaking balls below the zone: the plan's first line, and a take in every count, so the earlier counts come next." The next sentence names a two-strike second line, and the plan closes with "The only changes on this card are the pitches above."

Order: Rafaela's plan reads "(1) With two strikes, let fastballs above the zone go." then "(2) At 0-1 or 1-1, let fastballs above the zone go." Albies has the same with changeups and splitters. Duran's is "(1) With two strikes, mostly against right-handers, let breaking balls below the zone go." then "(2) When you're ahead, mostly against right-handers ...". The reference card guide says "The plan's lines are numbered in the order to work on them, a take before two strikes first" (17_build_player_cards.py:1994-1995). Page 2 of each noted print PDF tells the player "a take before two strikes comes first, because it costs nothing in strikeouts" (PLAYER_GUIDE, 17_build_player_cards.py:1702-1703).

Sweep: across 261 cards and 783 views (all, vs RHP, vs LHP), only these 3 noted all-pitchers views put a two-strike take ahead of a pre-two-strike take. 0 hand tabs and 0 un-noted cards do. Notes with runs and no unit: 4 (García, Rafaela, Goodman, Peraza). Clean notes: Giménez, Montgomery, Clement, Moniak, Pérez.
issues.method: I read scripts/coach_notes.py in full: the 17 notes (lines 49-69) and every claim check (193-430). In step 17 I read plan_pitch_items (631-640) and the guide text (1692-1715 print, 1985-1997 web). I dumped each noted hitter's note, plan_items, leaks, tables (all, R, L), trend and side_pitches from dump_2026.json (skeptic_coachnote2/dump_noted.py, noted.txt) and checked every number in each note against the printed aside (all three views), tiles, header and Zone numbers. For Rafaela's 2024-26 early-count far-off rates and costs I read results/xchase/coaching/actionability_202{4,5,6}.csv, and for Neto's PA by season the xchase_leaderboard CSVs (read only, no recompute). I then ran skeptic_coachnote2/order.py and measure.py over all 261 cards and 783 views.
issues.why_it_matters: The staff read the note with the player in the room and reconcile it against the card. A number they cannot find on the card, one that is a point off the table beside it, or a cost larger than the row it is said to sit inside costs trust and time. Two notes also hand the staff a three-ball rule while the player's card says its two pitches are the only changes. On the three order cards, the player's own print card tells him on page 2 the opposite of the order on page 1. By design: the note picks the lead, and only the noted README explains that.
issues.root_cause:
The notes are written by hand in scripts/coach_notes.py:49-69. Their checks test the value only, not the scope, unit or season the wording implies:
- :266-272 checks Rafaela's 2024 and 2025 rates against the 2026 league rate.
- :300-301 counts García's balls==3, which includes 3-2.
- :373-384 counts Neto's all-count sliders and compares with 2024.
- :392-396 puts Peraza's per-600 net runs next to 45 raw pitches.
- :232-236 measures Harris's share against the net.
- :316 gives Goodman's cost net of contact.
- :296 uses BACKTEST_LEAGUE_CELL for Albies, while the card uses e_match (17_build_player_cards.py:443).

The order comes from 17_build_player_cards.py:637-640, which puts the note's lead first whatever its count. The guide text at :1994-1995 (web) and :1702-1703 (print) states the rule with no exception.
issues.suggested_fix:
Reword 11 notes in coach_notes.py:
- Rafaela: "fell from 35% in 2024 to 28% in 2025 and stayed at 27% in 2026 ... about 4 of the 12.2 far-off runs per 600 PA".
- Neto: "right-handers' sliders below the zone, in any count: 290 in 2026, up from 184 in 2024".
- García: "inside it and the 3-2 part of 'Two strikes' ... about 5 runs per 600 PA".
- Peraza: "about 5 runs per 600 PA, net of contact, from 45 pitches".
- Goodman: "about 5 runs per 600 PA, net of contact".
- Harris: "about half of the 12.8 runs his chases cost net; second-best contact of the nine 'easiest' hitters, so the two lines are the only changes".
- Albies: 18%.
- Caballero: "far-off (4+ in) two-strike fastballs above the zone; 81% counting the near ones".
- Peña: "breaking ball away (mostly sliders)".
- Martínez: "right-handers threw him two in three of his pitches and three in four of these".
- Tovar: "he chases this pitch above league in every count, so after the two lines, the earlier counts next".

For García and Peraza, have the closing line or the note make clear that the three-ball rule is the staff's addition. Add checks in coach_notes.check: "about N runs" must carry "per 600 PA"; runs are choices unless the note says "net"; "vs N%" uses e_match; a note's season list must include the card season. For the order, add "(a noted hitter's plan starts where his coach's note says)" to the guides at 17_build_player_cards.py:1994 and :1702, or move note_start for Rafaela, Albies and Duran to their pre-two-strike take.
refuted_items: Rafaela, "the chart shows 38%, 31%, 35% (up in 2026)" as a contradiction: does not hold. The chart is far-off chasing in all counts. The note is about early counts, which were 27.1% in 2026, level with 27.5% in 2025. The 2026 rise is two-strike far-off chasing (36.3% to 45.8%), which the plan's first line targets. What holds is only that the 2026 figure is missing.

Rafaela, "his early counts cost 7.5 runs, not about 4": does not hold. The 4 is the far-off part (2026 decision class A, -4.43 per 600 PA, a piece of the 12.2 header tile). The table's -2.4, -1.8 and -3.3 include near pitches. The number is right; only its unit and scope go unsaid.

Harris, "8.5 runs lost before two strikes": the printed figures are -1.1, -3.5 and -5.0 = -9.6. "About half" does hold in the data (inside 40-60% of the net -12.8); it just matches no printed number. "Nothing else needs to change" is partly backed: xwOBA of PAs reaching first pitch, 0-1/1-1 and two strikes is above league (.343/.315, .297/.276, .254/.234). Only the stated reason, contact, fails before two strikes, where contact sums to -0.1.

Caballero, 77% vs 81%: not a wrong number. It is a different population, and the note flags it with "far-off". The "every year" trend does not contradict the season chart's 2025 dip, since the chart covers all counts and the note says "even in 2025".
Martínez's hand claim: true in total, and not only because of volume. Leak RHP shares of 76% and 72% are above his 67% exposure. Only the vague wording holds.

Plan order: by design. plan_pitch_items leads with the note's leak, and the BRIEF says so. 0 of 522 hand-tab views and 0 un-noted cards break the rule. What holds is that the guides state the rule without the exception.
Peña's "slider": a staff note, and staff know the word, so this is polish only. Neto's note uses "sliders" the same way.

issues.statement: Confirmed: every 'Nothing to change ... those swings have paid: N runs' line quotes the tab's All counts contact, not the contact of the counts it names. That is 14 of 14 such lines, on 11 hitters. On 10 views N differs from the named counts' contact as printed (5 are off by 1.5+ runs). On 2 views, Church vs LHP and Freeman vs LHP, the sentence is false: the named count's chases lost runs. The 'None worth 0.75 runs' and far-off tile part holds only for Arráez and Moreno, and it is by design. Norby and Bolte do not hold. High severity is overstated, because in no case is a take line lost.
evidence: Measured on 783 views (261 hitters x All/vs RHP/vs LHP): 14 'Nothing to change' lines (2 All pitchers, 4 vs RHP, 8 vs LHP; 10 from fallback_line, 4 from spread_line). In 14 of 14, N = round(All counts contact). N differs from round(sum of the named rows' contact) on 10 views; by 1.5+ runs on 5 (Vargas L 6 vs 3.2, Langeliers L 4 vs 1.6, Church L 2 vs −0.1, Martínez L 8 vs 6.1, Freeman L 2 vs 0.4). Conclusion false (named contact < named choices cost) on 2: Church L, Freeman L.

Church vs LHP: "Nothing to change. You chase more than most hitters when you're ahead in the count (37% against 25%), but those swings have paid: 2 runs more than an average hitter's chases, more than the extra swings cost." Table: "Ahead in the count 35 37%25% ... 54%45% .232.354 −1.0 −0.1"; "Two strikes 58 ... −0.6 +2.2"; "All counts 191 ... −1.5 +1.8". The 2 runs are two-strike contact, which is not the count named.

Freeman vs LHP: "Nothing to change. You chase more than most hitters when you're ahead in the count (37% against 31%), but those swings have paid: 2 runs more..." Table: "Ahead in the count 73 37%31% ... −1.2 +0.4"; "All counts 452 ... +0.2 +1.5". His All pitchers table: ahead −3.3 choices / −0.1 contact, his only negative count.

Vargas vs LHP: "...when you're ahead in the count and with two strikes, but those swings have paid: 6 runs more..." Rows: Ahead −1.4/+1.9, Two strikes −1.2/+1.3 (3.2 together); All counts −3.4/+5.9 (6 includes 0-1/1-1 +3.3).

Martínez vs LHP: 'paid: 8 runs' vs 0-1 or 1-1 +2.2 and Two strikes +3.9 (6.1); All counts +7.7. Langeliers vs LHP: 'paid: 4 runs' vs Ahead −1.2/+1.6; All counts +4.1. Hand tab vs main plan (by design, but 'Nothing to change' is absolute). 5 hitters' hand tabs say 'Nothing to change ... with two strikes' while the All pitchers plan has a two-strike take not marked 'mostly vs' the other hand: Hoerner vs RHP vs All step 2 "With two strikes, let fastballs above the zone go" (31 of 45; 73% of those pitches from RHP). Lee vs RHP vs All step 2 same pitch (36 of 58; 78% RHP). Vargas vs LHP vs All step 2 same pitch (32 of 39, vs RHP 21 of 28, so 11 of 11 vs LHP). Arenado vs LHP vs both two-strike steps (35%/37% LHP). Mangum vs LHP, the reverse: "No single pitch here is a clear take. Your chase choices cost 4 runs a season, across every count; the count table shows where. Start with two strikes, where it costs the most." Row: "Two strikes 81 62%45% ... −2.0 +3.7". It is the only 1 of 7 'Start ...' lines whose named count's contact covers its choices. (32 All pitchers). 46 of them sit beside a count row of choices <= −1.0, 4 on All pitchers (Arráez −8.3, Moreno −7.2, Bolte −1.3, Norby −1.1). Side note (separate pattern): fallback_line prints the minus as an ASCII hyphen, e.g. Jung Hoo Lee vs LHP "about average overall (-2.1 runs a season)", while tables and other lines print "−". Seen on 12 views, 12 hitters.
issues.method: Read productive_line, spread_line, fallback_line and plan_items in scripts/17_build_player_cards.py (lines 644-702, 803-850), the leak rule in scripts/leak_rules.py:137, the empty-leaks text in scripts/templates/player_cards.html:942 and the roster builder (lines 1017-1030). Wrote skeptic_productive.py and skeptic_none.py in the audit folder and ran them over dump_2026.json (261 hitters, 783 views). For each 'Nothing to change' line, the scripts parsed N and found the costly counts (choices <= −1.0, the code's rule; all named counts appear in the text). They compared N with total and named-row contact and flagged named rows with choices + contact < 0. They also listed every 'No single pitch here is a clear take ... Start X' line against X's contact, every empty leak list beside a −1+ count row or a tile >= 3 with its roster position, and every hand-tab productive line against the All pitchers plan's pitch lines in the same count (with share_rhp). Re-read the printed asides and By count tables for Church, Freeman, Vargas, Mangum, Hoerner, Lee, Arráez and Moreno.
issues.why_it_matters: An analyst who checks 'those swings have paid: N runs' against the row it names finds a different number on 10 views. On Church and Freeman vs LHP, a player is told there is nothing to change in a count where the table shows his chases lost runs. Church's ahead-count xwOBA there is .232 vs .354, and the ahead count is Freeman's costliest count on All pitchers. The code's own docstring says the line is for counts whose contact covers their cost, and that is never enforced. Not high, because no take line is lost. No leak qualifies in those counts, so the correct fallback has no take either. Both are minority-hand tabs on small samples (35 and 73 ahead pitches). The by-design parts are still confusing. On 5 hand tabs, 'Nothing to change ... with two strikes' sits against a two-strike take in the main plan whose pitches largely come from that hand (73% for Hoerner, 78% for Lee). Arráez and Moreno print 'None worth 0.75 runs' and a 6.3 / 4.7 far-off cost tile under a 'Nothing to change' plan, while the roster ranks them 46th and 60th by runs at stake. No sentence ties these together.
issues.root_cause: scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:644-658. productive_line(rows, costly, contact) prints `{contact:.0f}`, and both callers pass rows["total"]["contact"]: fallback_line:695/701-702 and spread_line:668-670 (via plan_items: `spread_line(rows, loss, rows["total"]["contact"], ...)`). The gate is `contact >= sum(-rows[g]["choices"] for g in costly) and contact >= -choices`, which tests total contact, not each costly count's own contact. The docstring (645-646: 'counts where the hitter's chases have produced more than his choices cost') is never checked. The Mangum reverse case is spread_line:688. Its `rows[worst].get("status") != "productive"` guard uses the xwOBA count check, which hand tables do not carry, so every hand tab prints 'Start ...' even where contact covers the cost. The empty-leaks text is in scripts/templates/player_cards.html:942 (and the print card at step 17:1636 and 1891). It does not say the leak rule (leak_rules.py:137, choices + contact < 0) is what emptied the list. scripts/plan_checks.py has no check of this line.
issues.suggested_fix:
1. In step 17, add `pays_back(rows, costly) = bool(costly) and all(stored(rows[g]['contact']) >= -stored(rows[g]['choices']) for g in costly)`. Gate productive_line on it in fallback_line (with contact > 0 and contact >= -choices) and in spread_line (n_pitches == 0 and contact >= loss). Have productive_line quote `runs_phrase(sum(rows[g]['contact'] for g in costly))` instead of the total. Church vs LHP and Freeman vs LHP then read 'No single pitch stands out. Your chase choices are about average overall (...); you give back about 1 run a season when you're ahead in the count.' The other 12 lines keep the verdict with the named counts' number (Vargas 3, Langeliers 2, Martínez 6, Hoerner 5, Arráez 18).
2. In spread_line:688, replace the status guard with `rows[worst]['choices'] + rows[worst]['contact'] < 0`, and pick the costliest count that does not pay back. Mangum vs LHP then starts at 0-1 or 1-1 (−1.0 / −0.5), or the 'Start' sentence is dropped.
3. On a hand tab where the All pitchers plan has a pitch line in a named count, open with 'Against left-handers alone, nothing to change ...' or add 'the two-strike line on All pitchers still applies'.
4. On a view whose plan is the productive line, have the empty leak list say 'None that cost runs overall: where your choices cost 0.75+ runs, your contact paid it back'. When the tile is 1+, add a clause to the line, e.g. '(the 6.3 at the top is what those choices cost before what the swings produced)'.
5. Add a plan_checks.py guard: the 'paid: N runs' figure must equal the rounded sum of the named rows' contact, and every named row must have choices + contact >= 0.
refuted_items: Severity high: does not hold. The conclusion is false on only 2 of 783 views (Church and Freeman vs LHP). Both are minority-hand tabs with 1.0 to 1.2 run counts on 35 and 73 ahead pitches. No leak qualifies there, so the correct fallback also gives no take, and no player loses a plan line. Medium.

Connor Norby and Henry Bolte: refuted as part of this pattern. Neither card has a 'Nothing to change' line; both plans are the contact line, with choices +8.8 and +5.8 overall. 'None worth 0.75 runs per 600 PA' beside a −1.1 or −1.3 count row is not a contradiction, because a leak is a count x pitch x side cell and the count row sums about 20 of them. Those rows also lose on contact (−1.1/−1.0 and −1.3/−0.5), so the contact test did not empty the list. Tiles are 0.6 and 0.0.
Josh Naylor vs LHP: 'paid: 2 runs' matches the named Two strikes contact as printed (+1.6 rounds to 2). Only the source of the number differs, so no reader can catch it. Holds as code behaviour only.
Arráez vs RHP (14 vs +13.6), Arráez vs LHP (4 vs +4.3), Moreno vs RHP (11 vs +10.6): the quoted N rounds to the named row's contact. Nothing visible is wrong.
Jung Hoo Lee vs RHP (5 vs +6.2), Nolan Arenado vs LHP (2 vs +2.6), Moreno All (17 vs +17.5): the quote understates the named count's contact, so the sentence stays true. Cosmetic.

Tile and roster 'contradiction' for Arráez and Moreno: not literal. The tile is labeled as choices on far-off pitches only, the line itself says the swings paid 'more than the extra swings cost', and the roster lede says it sorts by 'the runs his swing choices on far-off pitches cost'. It holds as by design but confusing, because nothing on the card ties the 6.3 / 4.7 to 'Nothing to change'.
'Freeman ... in his costliest all-pitchers count' holds: ahead −3.3 choices / −0.1 contact is his only negative count on All pitchers, and his All plan has no ahead-count line.

Vargas 'tells a hitter chasing 59% vs 42% with two strikes to change nothing' holds, but per count his vs LHP contact covers both named counts (+1.9 vs 1.4, +1.3 vs 1.2). The problem is the number (6 vs 3.2) and the clash with the All pitchers two-strike fastball line (11 of 11 chased vs LHP, under the 12-pitch leak minimum), not the verdict.

issues.statement: All five oddities are real on the page, and none of them changes a plan line. (1) In every By count table (261 cards, all three views), the First pitch xwOBA equals the All counts xwOBA. That is by design, and nothing on the card says so. (2) 38 cards print a vs LHP Misses rate from 1 to 4 chases, 27 of those rows as 0% or 100%, with no sample flag. (3) 25 cards print a bare '–' in the Zone numbers panel, in 28 cells. (4) 15 cards draw the far-off trend line straight across seasons the hitter did not qualify. (5) The chart's 'avg' line is the league's overall rate, but the table's 'avg' is the average hitter on his own pitches. One part of the report does not hold: the count status ('struggling') is never printed on the card, so it cannot read as a first-pitch problem.
evidence: (1) First pitch xwOBA = All counts xwOBA, with the league figure equal too, on 783 of 783 tables (261 cards x 3 views). The printed aside text matches on 783 of 783. Walls on screen (skeptic_tabletrend/bycount_walls.png): 'First pitch 186 14% 16% ... .251 .315' and 'All counts 859 25% 29% ... .251 .315'. Meckler on the vs LHP tab: '.267 .309' in both rows. Code comment at 17_build_player_cards.py:436: '# every plate appearance passes through 0-0, so "first" is the total'.

(1) The card has no status column: the web table's columns are Pitches, Chases, Far-off, Misses, xwOBA, Choices and Contact (template countTable). 0 of 783 asides contain 'struggling', 'productive' or 'hitting well'. The reviewers' 'struggling' came from the dossier's extra 'count status' column, which format_dossiers.py adds from the data.

(2) Misses rate from fewer than 5 chases (chases = pitches x chase rate): 56 rows on 38 cards, all on the vs LHP tab. The fewest chases behind a printed rate is 8 on All pitchers and 6 on vs RHP. 27 of the 56 rows print 0% or 100% (19 cards). Trout vs LHP on screen (bycount_trout_lhp.png): 'First pitch 86 2% 17% 2% 9% 100% 55%'. Kwan vs LHP First pitch: 95 pitches, 1 chase, Misses '0% / 29%'. Nootbaar vs LHP: First pitch 26 pitches, 2 chases, '0% / 30%'. 89 vs LHP rows rest on fewer than 30 pitches (Drew Gilbert and Mike Yastrzemski: 9 pitches Ahead).

(3) In the Zone numbers panel (chase metric), 28 of 8,352 cells on 25 cards print a bare '–'. 26 of them are 'up and in'. Caratini on screen (numbers_caratini.png): 'up and in | 0% / 13% (1) | 0% / 13% (1) | – | 25% / 22% (4)'. On the 'Misses on chases' metric the dash is common: 10 of 32 cells for Taylor Ward and Víctor Caratini, 8 for Steven Kwan (numbers_whiff_taylor_ward.png). The panel note says only '...and how many pitches' (or 'chases').

(4) 15 cards have 3 or more trend seasons with a gap, and a single path runs straight through the gap. On screen: Clemens (trend_clemens.png) goes 2023 to 2025 with no 2024 point; Palacios (trend_palacios.png) goes 2022 to 2024 to 2026. 3 more cards with 2 seasons and a gap (Garrett Mitchell, Vaughn Grissom, Jonny DeLuca) get dots only, which is correct. A season is left out when the hitter saw fewer than 150 far-off pitches (TREND_MIN_FAR_PITCHES), and the card never says so.

(5) The chart's 'avg' line is D.leagueTrend, the swing rate of all hitters on all far-off pitches: 21.8% in 2026. The table's far-off 'avg' is the average hitter on this hitter's own far-off pitches and ranges from 18% to 25%. It rounds to a different number from 22% on 178 of 261 cards, and by 3 or more points on 18 (Kwan 18%, Jonah Heim 25%, Heliot Ramos 25%). On 20 cards the table and the chart disagree on which side of average he is. Example: Mullins's table reads 'Far-off 21% / 19%' (above), but his 2026 point (20.6%) sits below the 21.8% 'avg' line. Every one of these gaps is 2.4 points or less.

Side note, not visible on the page: the chart's 2026 'you' point differs from the table's far-off 'you' by 1 point on 12 cards (Gabriel Moreno 22% vs 23%), because the trend uses a different pitch file. The chart prints no values, so a reader cannot see this.
issues.method: I wrote skeptic_tables_trend.py, which runs over dump_2026.json (all 261 players x 3 views). It compares the first and total rows on xwoba, xwoba_league and status, and parses the printed aside text. It works out chases as round(pitches x chase) and flags printed Misses rates with fewer than 5 chases. It parses every Zone numbers cell, looking for exact '–' and the cell pattern. It finds year gaps in p.trend and compares the 2026 trend values with the table's far and far_league (rounded and signed). I re-shot the page with a copy of shot.mjs on its own port that adds element clipping and pre-shot JavaScript (skeptic_tabletrend/shot_clip.mjs and shot_probe.mjs): trend charts for Clemens, Palacios and Kwan; By count tables for Walls, Trout vs LHP and Meckler vs LHP; the Zone numbers panel for Caratini, plus Ward, Caratini and Kwan on the misses metric. I read countTable, trendSvg and numbersTable in the template, and count_table, league_trend, draw_trend, GLOSSARY and the uses of status in step 17.
issues.why_it_matters: These are polish items: no plan line, leak or target changes. Each one, though, makes an analyst or coach suspect a bug or read too much into a number. An identical xwOBA in two rows looks like a copy error. A '100% / 55%' Misses figure from 2 chases looks like a finding. A line drawn across a season he did not qualify suggests data that does not exist. Two different 'avg' baselines on one card can put the hitter above average in the table and below the avg line on the chart (20 cards). Item (1) is deliberate in step 17, and so is the '–' for an empty cell. Items (2), (4) and (5) are oversights: no small-sample guard, the line not broken at gaps, and the word 'avg' used for two baselines.
issues.root_cause: (1) scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:437 builds the total row's xwOBA from the 'first' count check ('\"first\" if g == \"total\"'), and scripts/templates/player_cards.html:868 prints xwOBA on both rows. GLOSSARY at 17:1448-1450 (the web countNote and the print card) does not say the First pitch row covers every plate appearance. (2) 17:444 averages whiff over any number of chases, and the template's line 866 prints pct(r.whiff) with no guard on the chase count. (3) Template line 987 prints '–' when n is 0. (4) Template line 899 draws one path through every point once there are 3 or more seasons; the print card does the same at 17:1478-1479. (5) Template line 905 (and 17:1474 on the print card) labels D.leagueTrend (17:230, every hitter's far-off swing rate) 'avg', the same word the table uses for far_league (17:443, the average hitter on his own pitches).
issues.suggested_fix: (1) Add to GLOSSARY: 'Every plate appearance starts at 0-0, so the First pitch xwOBA is the whole season's.' Or leave the First pitch xwOBA cell blank ('same as all'). (2) Add 'chases': int(len(ch)) to each count_table row. In countTable, print the Misses cell as 'k of n' (or a muted '–' with a 'fewer than 5 chases' title) when chases < 5. (3) In numbersTable, print 'no pitches' (or 'no chases' on the misses metric) instead of '–', or add 'a dash: none' to the panel note. (4) In trendSvg and draw_trend, split the series into runs of consecutive years and draw one path per run, leaving the dots for lone seasons. Add '(seasons with under 150 far-off pitches left out)' to the heading when there is a gap. (5) Rename the chart label 'avg' to 'league' in trendSvg line 905 and draw_trend line 1474, so it is not read as the table's same-pitches average.
refuted_items: Refuted: "'struggling' on the First pitch row then reads as a first-pitch problem." The card never prints a count status; the word came from the dossier's extra data column. The status reaches the page only indirectly. The roster's 'Count check' gives the all-PA verdict for Oneil Cruz, the one card whose top leak is on the first pitch. CJ Abrams's fallback gate adds 'Start on the first pitch, where it costs the most' when the first-pitch status (the all-PA status) is not productive.

Partly refuted: the 'Grisham 22% vs 20%' comparison. The trend chart prints no numbers (only 0/20/40% axis ticks), so 22% and 20% appear only in the dossier. On the page the mismatch is the shared label 'avg' plus a slight difference in line position. The label problem holds, and 20 cards flip above/below average.
Not an issue: Wade Meckler vs LHP First pitch Misses '–'. He had 0 chases on 24 pitches, so there is no rate to print.

Qualified: the claim that every other Zone numbers cell shows '(n)'. That holds only on the chase metric (28 cells on 25 cards). On the misses metric '–' is the panel's normal empty marker (8 to 10 of 32 cells on the cards checked), so this is a convention to explain, not a one-off glitch.

Held as reported: xwOBA equality on 261/261 cards (783/783 views); 38 cards with Misses from 1 to 4 chases; trend lines bridging gaps for Clemens (2023 to 2025) and Palacios (2022, 2024, 2026), 15 cards in all.

issues.statement: All five wording slips are on the cards. Every one of the 229 cards with a target sentence has at least one: (1) the hand-tab line "The target counts all pitchers." on all 89 no-target cards (73 "No target"/"No chase target", 16 "No number to beat"); (2) "1 points" on 6 cards; (3) no unit on the forecast and threshold on all 140 cards with a number to beat; (4) the clumsy video-only sentence on 16 cards, 9 of them with one leak; (5) "The number to move is contact on chases" on 24 execution-led cards. Several of the reviewers' framings do not hold, though. Item 1 is what commit 0d64764 set out to do. Item 3's "6%" reading is unlikely. The plural/singular complaint in item 4 is wrong. Item 5 does have a number on most of its cards.
evidence: (1) Kyle Schwarber, vs RHP and vs LHP tabs: "The plan for this pitcher hand only; pick All pitchers for the full plan. The target counts all pitchers." His All pitchers view: "Target: No target: leaks 1 to 3 together were 4 points above the league's chase rate in 2026, and with no change should be about at it in 2027."
(1) Cam Smith: the same hand-tab line, while All pitchers says "Target: No number to beat: every leak on this card was mostly within a ball of the zone, one for video, not a take rule."

(1) Count: the hand-tab line is on 89 of 89 cards with target_text but no 'under N' beat (73 notarget + 16 video). It is on 0 of the 32 cards with no target object (Steven Kwan, Kevin McGonigle, Evan Carter omit it), and on all 140 cards with a number. R and L tabs always agree.

(1) Commit 0d64764's message: "on 2022-2026 31 to 40 cards a season have none ... only the no-target cards lose the hand tab's sentence". 31 to 40 is the count of target-null cards (32 in 2026), so the template does what the commit described.
(1) Related: the All pitchers view prints a label that contradicts itself, "Target: No target:" (73 cards) and "Target: No number to beat:" (16 cards).

(2) Jakob Marsee: "No target: leak 1 was 1 points above the league's chase rate in 2026". Also Seiya Suzuki (above), Maikel García ("leaks 1 and 2 together were 1 points below"), Ian Happ ("leaks 1 to 3 together were 1 points above"), Spencer Torkelson (below), Jorge Soler ("No chase target: leaks 1 and 2 together were 1 points above"). Exactly 6 cards. No other '1 points' in any view on any card.

(3) Wyatt Langford: "Leak 1: you chased 13 points above the league's chase rate in 2026. Those spots get better on their own, so with no change you'd be about 6 in 2027. Under 6 is a fix." Roster Beat: "under 6 (was 13)". The same pattern is on all 140 cards with a number to beat; 2026 has no retrospective targets.

(3) The web card defines the unit only in the first clause. The roster glossary explains Beat "in points", and the print card's guide (step 17 line 1707) says "in points above the league's chase rate". The web 'How to read' guide (d['guide']) never mentions the target.

(4) Alejandro Kirk (one leak, "Two strikes, mostly vs RHP, fastballs inside"): "No number to beat: every leak on this card was mostly within a ball of the zone, one for video, not a take rule." Cards with one leak: James Wood, Alejandro Kirk, Alec Bohm, Lawrence Butler, Nick Loftin, Jared Triolo, A. J. Ewing, Fernando Tatís, Cam Smith. Two leaks: Chase DeLauter, Drew Gilbert, Ronald Acuña, Manny Machado, Jorbit Vivas. Three: Vladimir Guerrero, Jordan Walker.

(5) Kazuma Okamoto: "No chase target: leak 1 was 7 points below the league's chase rate in 2026, and with no change should be about at it in 2027. The number to move is contact on chases." His plan line 1 does give a number: "You miss on 58% of your chases, against 43% for other hitters".

(5) Gunnar Henderson, same target ending. His plan line 1 says the opposite of a miss problem: "You miss about as often as other hitters do, but what you hit on a chase goes nowhere (over a season your chases cost you 4 runs more than an average hitter's would)". Of the 24 cards, 16 quote a miss rate in the plan and 8 say "miss about as often".

Side note, outside this item: "within a ball of the zone" is printed for every leak with depth_in < 4. The video-only leaks' depths run 1.4 to 3.9 in, and 15 of 25 are over a baseball's roughly 2.9 in diameter.
issues.method: Read BRIEF.md, target_text()/target_beat() in scripts/17_build_player_cards.py (lines 958-1030), template lines 930 and 944, plan_checks.py target_problems(), and the diff and message of commit 0d64764. Wrote skeptic_targetwording/measure.py over all 261 cards in dump_2026.json. It sorts each card by its target kind (null / number / notarget / video) and, from the rendered asides, checks: the hand-tab sentence in R and L; ' 1 points' in any view; the forecast pattern "you'd be about N in YYYY. Under N is a fix."; the video sentence with leak counts; the contact sentence. verify_reported.py re-checked every card the reviewers named (all held). contact.py compared the 24 contact-sentence cards with their plan lines and picture rows.
issues.why_it_matters: The main instruction is never at risk: the plan lines and the "Under N" number are right, so severity stays low. (1) is by design: the template tests target_text, exactly as commit 0d64764 described. But on 89 cards the hand tab points the reader to "the target" while the All pitchers view opens "Target: No target:" or "No number to beat", so a coach flipping tabs meets a target the card says it does not have. The line is literally true, since that paragraph does count all pitchers; it is just worded around a target that does not exist. (2) is a plain grammar slip on 6 cards. (3) "about 6 ... Under 6" leaves out the unit given one clause earlier. A 6% reading is unlikely next to the 30-60% rates in the leak list, but repeating "points" would make the number trackable on its own, as on the roster's "under 6 (was 13)". (4) Reviewers 124 and 266 are wrong about agreement: "every leak" is singular, so "one" agrees. The real problems are that "one for video" dangles after "the zone" and that "every leak" is odd on 9 one-leak cards. (5) The phrase is vaguest on the 8 cards whose plan says misses are average: there the thing to move is what contact produces (the Contact tile), not a miss rate.
issues.root_cause: scripts/templates/player_cards.html:930 tests p.target_text, which is set for all three no-number sentences. Template :944 prefixes "Target: " even when the text opens "No target:". scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:982-983 has the fixed video-only sentence (no singular branch). :992-994 has f"{x} points above/below" with no case for x == 1 (the same risk at :1003). :1005-1006 has "you'd be about {pred} in {nxt}. Under {pred} is a fix." with no unit. :1001 adds " The number to move is contact on chases." to every execution-led no-target card.
issues.suggested_fix: (1) Template :930: show the line only when there is a number, e.g. `(p.target_beat || "").startsWith("under") ? " The target counts all pitchers." : ""`, or have step 17 send a has_number flag. At :944, drop the "Target: " prefix when target_text starts with "No ". (2) In target_text, use a helper `pts = lambda x: f"{x} point{'' if x == 1 else 's'}"` at :992-994 and :1003. (3) Change :1005-1006 to "...so with no change you'd be about {pred} points above it in {nxt}. Under {pred} points is a fix." (4) Change :982-983 to "No number to beat: the one leak on this card was mostly within a ball of the zone, a video item, not a take rule." when there is one leak, else "...every leak on this card was mostly within a ball of the zone, so all are video items, not take rules." (5) Change :1001 to name the printed number: "The number to move is how often you miss on a chase (Misses in the By count table)" when the plan quotes a miss rate, else "The number to move is what your chases produce (Contact, at the top of the card)". Add plan_checks rules for ' 1 points', for a hand-tab target line without an 'under' beat, and for 'Under N is a fix' without 'points'.
refuted_items: (1) The claim that commit 0d64764 meant the hand-tab line only for cards with a number to beat is refuted. The commit counts '31 to 40 cards a season have none', which is the target-null set (32 in 2026), and the template does exactly that. The line is also literally true (the Target paragraph counts all pitchers). The wording confusion stands; the 'bug against the commit's intent' framing does not.

issues.why_it_matters: The leak numbers link the plan and leak list to the pictures. Plan, leaks and table: vs all pitchers, compared with your side and hand." refuted_items: '75 of 547 markers sit half inside the white strike-zone box': no marker's centre is inside the box. 75 markers (67 cards) overlap the zone line, the most by 31% of the circle and the median by 4%; 71 of the 75 are video items whose chased pitches really were 1-4 in off the zone.

'Twice into another region than the leak's name' (Trout, Marte): true only on paper. The nudged centres sit 0.5 and 0.6 in past the zone's side line, still under the box's corner; the picture draws no region lines.

'13 pairs overlap': 12 pairs have overlapping circles (0.514-0.590 ft apart against a 0.594 ft marker), 17 counting the outline stroke. Six are not nudges at all: their natural spots are 0.51-0.59 ft apart.

'Outlines cut by the zone box or picture edge show as open': most ends at the zone box (1,844) look closed against the box line. The truly loose ends (1,059) stop where evidence drops below 0.5, by design. The blue spots already exist in the default view, which is a different issue.

issues.statement:
The wording problems in this report are real, but none would make a player do the wrong thing. Each one's instruction is still the first sentence of the plan line.

1. **Leak caption with no leaks.** The leak-list caption ("Numbered on the pictures... so it can leave a bigger one out") prints under "None worth 0.75 runs" on 32 all-pitchers views, 58 vs RHP tabs and 175 vs LHP tabs (188 cards).
2. **Left-out leak never named.** On the 72 all-pitchers plans that really do skip a bigger leak, the same generic caption is all the card says. On 92 more cards the plan takes every leak listed, so the caption has nothing to apply to.
3. **First lines over 75 words.** 31 all-pitchers first lines run over 75 words (35 cards in any view), up to 113 words (Cronenworth) and 124 on a hand tab (Jared Young vs RHP). 67 all-pitchers plans run over 140 words.
4. **Count phrase said twice.** Every plus-count clause restates the line's own count. That is 73 exact repeats in the all-pitchers view, plus 8 where the opener says "When you're ahead," and the clause says "When you're ahead in the count,".
5. **Two forms of the "ahead" opener.** The short opener is used on 38 cards. The roster's Start with column has 34 short and 33 long.
6. **Plan and leak list name the same pitch differently.** "off the plate away/inside" vs "away/inside" on 25 cards; "changeups and splitters" vs "changeups / splitters" on 73.
7. **"Nothing stands out" undersells good choosers.** 21 cards whose choices are worth +9 runs or better (Ward +27.1) read "about league average or better".

In the default view, 153 of 261 cards show at least one of items 1, 3, 4 or 5. Counting hand tabs and item 6, 247 of 261 do.
evidence: 1. Ward, all pitchers (screenshot skeptic_boilerplate/ward_1440.png): "None worth 0.75 runs per 600 PA." then "Numbered on the pictures, on the row of the hand a leak names. Ranked by what the choices cost, per 600 PA; the plan takes up to two, in the order to work on them, so it can leave a bigger one out." The same caption follows "None worth" on all 32 empty all-pitchers views. The hand-tab version ("Ranked by what the choices cost... so it can leave a bigger one out.") follows it on 58 vs RHP and 175 vs LHP tabs.

2. Yastrzemski: the plan's lines are tagged leak 3 and leak 1. "(2) Two strikes vs RHP, changeups / splitters below the zone ... −2.5" is left off the plan, and the only mention is the generic "so it can leave a bigger one out". This happens on 72 all-pitchers plans (Trout, Stott, Horwitz, Hicks, Bazzana, Álvarez...).

3. Cronenworth, all pitchers, first line, 113 words (screenshot skeptic_boilerplate/cronenworth_1440.png): "At 0-1 or 1-1, mostly against right-handers, let changeups and splitters below the zone go. You swung at 68% of them; hitters on average swing at 39%. The ones you swung at were typically 5 inches off the zone. You miss about as often as other hitters do, but what you hit on a chase goes nowhere (over a season your chases cost you 8 runs more than an average hitter's would): contact is your bigger cost, so this one is a take even when you could reach it. At 0-1 or 1-1, your choices are a plus overall (+0.1 runs in the count table); this pitch is where they give some back."

3. Jared Young, vs RHP, 124 words. It also says "about as often as other hitters do" twice: "You swung at these about as often as other hitters do, but more of yours came at 1-2 and 3-2 ... You miss about as often as other hitters do, but what you hit on a chase goes nowhere..." Joe Mack vs RHP does the same.

3. The 31 all-pitchers first lines over 75 words, by which clauses they carry: 12 have both the contact and plus-count clauses, 11 the contact clause only (all 50-word 'goes nowhere' sentences), 8 the plus-count clause only (6 of them video items). 67 all-pitchers plans run over 140 words.
4. Stott (1): "At 0-1 or 1-1, let breaking balls below the zone go... At 0-1 or 1-1, your choices are a plus overall". 73 all-pitchers items repeat the exact phrase; 147 across all three views.

4. Swanson (1): "When you're ahead, mostly against right-handers, let breaking balls below the zone go. ... When you're ahead in the count, your choices are a plus overall (+2.0 runs in the count table)". The same count is worded two ways inside one line, on 8 cards (Wood, Tucker, Keith, Álvarez, Carroll, Greene, Swanson, Baty).

5. Roster Start with: Moniak "When you're ahead against right-handers, let changeups and splitters below the zone go (61% vs 30%, 5 in off)" vs Goodman "When you're ahead in the count, let breaking balls below the zone go (62% vs 28%, 8 in off)". That is 34 short and 33 long in the column.

6. Caminero, plan: "let breaking balls off the plate away go"; leak list: "Two strikes, mostly vs RHP, breaking balls away". Plans say "changeups and splitters" and lists say "changeups / splitters" (79 all-pitchers items, 73 cards).

7. Ward (1st of 261, +27.1 choices, Two strikes +14.8): "Nothing stands out. Your chase choices are about league average or better in every count." Aranda, by contrast, has a plan and +4.1 runs, and his framing line reads "Overall your chase choices are better than average (+4.1 runs a season)".

Plus-count clauses on near-zero counts: Cronenworth "a plus overall (+0.1 runs in the count table)". There are 7 all-pitchers clauses under +0.5 (Bazzana, Álvarez, Rocchio, Baty, Steer, Cronenworth, Buxton) and 23 across all views.
Script: skeptic_boilerplate/measure.py → measure_out.json; per-card check of each reported card: skeptic_boilerplate/check_reported.py
issues.why_it_matters:
Coaches read the card with the player in the room. Captions about numbering and left-out leaks under an empty list, first lines of four or five sentences, a count named twice in one line, and two names for the same pitch all cost his attention and make a plan line harder to match to its leak. The fallback also tells the league's best choosers they are about average. None of this changes what he should do: the action is still the first sentence and the numbers are right, so severity is low.

Most of these are not deliberate:
- The caption under an empty list is a static string, not intended.
- The long lines come from two deliberate rules (contact reason folded into the first take, why-in-a-plus-count) stacking.
- plan_checks.py requires the repeated count phrase.
- The short opener and the two vocabularies are deliberate dictionaries, but the code comment says "One vocabulary for a leak".
issues.root_cause:
Where each item comes from:
- **Empty-list caption:** scripts/templates/player_cards.html:942-943 appends the caption whether or not leaks.length is 0. The print card has the same caption above "None worth": scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:1631-1636 and 1887-1891.
- **Long first lines:** 17_build_player_cards.py:812-819 (plan_items) appends contact_clause (lines 726-729, with contact_why's 50-word 'goes nowhere' form at 708-711) and then strength_clause (lines 738-751) to the same first item.
- **Count phrase repeat:** strength_clause restates COUNT_PHRASES of the line's own count. plan_checks.py:159-166 requires that exact phrase.
- **Two "ahead" openers:** GROUP_WORDS_SHORT at 17:523-524 is chosen whenever a hand phrase follows (17:621).
- **Two vocabularies:** PITCH_WORDS/REGION_WORDS (plan) vs LEAK_PITCH/LEAK_REGION (list and roster) at 17:398-413, under the comment "One vocabulary for a leak" (17:394).
- **"Nothing stands out" wording:** fallback_line at 17:694-699 says "about league average" plus " or better" whatever the size of the plus.
issues.suggested_fix:
Fixes, in order of value:
1. **Caption.** In aside(), append the caption only when leaks.length > 0. Give step 17 a per-view `skipped` field (leak numbers smaller than the plan's largest that the plan does not use). Print "leave a bigger one out" only when that field is non-empty, and name the leak: "The plan starts with leaks 3 and 1 (a take before two strikes costs no strikeouts); leak 2 is next." Make the same changes in the print card at 17:1631 and 17:1887.
2. **Plus-count clause.** Change strength_clause to "In this count your choices are a plus overall (+X runs in the count table); this pitch is where they give some back." Say "about even (+0.1...)" when the count is under +0.5. Update plan_checks.py:159-166 to match.
3. **Long first lines.** When both clauses would attach, move the plus-count why into the framing line. Shorten contact_why's form to "what you hit on a chase goes nowhere (8 runs a season below an average hitter's chases)". Add a plan_checks guard that fails a pitch line over about 70 words.
4. **"Ahead" opener.** Drop GROUP_WORDS_SHORT and always say "When you're ahead in the count".
5. **One vocabulary.** Use one set of words for the list and the plan, e.g. LEAK_REGION "in"/"away" = "off the plate inside"/"off the plate away", and one spelling of changeups and splitters.
6. **Good choosers.** In fallback_line, when choices >= +1 say "Nothing stands out. Your chase choices are better than average (+27.1 runs a season), and no count costs you a run.", matching framing_line's level words.
refuted_items: "75 to 107 words" understates it: all-pitchers first lines reach 113 words (Cronenworth), and hand-tab first lines reach 124 (Jared Young vs RHP).

"When both the contact clause and the plus-count clause attach" is too narrow: only 12 of the 31 all-pitchers lines over 75 words carry both. 11 have the contact clause alone and 8 the plus-count clause alone.

"Two reasons that pull opposite ways" does not hold. "contact is your bigger cost, so this one is a take" and "your choices are a plus overall... this pitch is where they give some back" agree (choices are fine, contact is the cost) and both support the take. The problem is length, not contradiction.
"Burying the instruction" is only partly true. On every pitch line the action ("let X go") is the first sentence, so the earlier first-line fix holds. What follows it is too long.
"13 cards have a 50-word 'goes nowhere' sentence": it is 12 cards.
Alec Burleson, listed under the empty-list caption (finding 425): none of his views has an empty leak list. He holds only for the left-out-leak-not-named claim (all pitchers and vs RHP).
Owen Caissie, listed under the plan-vs-leak naming finding (426): his plan lines use the same words as his leaks. He holds only under the long-first-line finding (90 words).

Trea Turner vs LHP, "about league average in every count" without "or better" next to Two strikes +1.1: technically holds but marginal. It is the only one of 190 'Nothing stands out' views with a count at +1.0 or more and no "or better" (total −0.3, inside the ±1-run band the rule uses).

issues.statement: This holds on all 261 cards, and it is by design. 115 cards give pitch lines to a hitter whose overall Choices are above 0 (96 of them +1 or better), and every one carries the framing line. On 68 of the 115, the plan's one or two instructions sit next to three or four reassuring sentences: the plus-count clause, the framing line, the fastball-strength clause and the no-target sentence. The instructions themselves are sound takes. The median first line is 5.3 inches off the zone, so following one cannot hurt a player. Two narrower cases go further. On 9 hand tabs the framing line says "better than average" while that tab's own table is negative. On 6 cards the only instruction is a pitch that both the line and the target say he does not over-chase.
evidence: Counts from all 261 cards. Pitch plans for hitters with Choices > 0: 115. At +1 or better: 96. Of the 115, 101 have at least one take line and 14 are video-only. 146 hitters have Choices > 0; 31 of them get no pitch line (Taylor Ward +27.1 'Nothing stands out').
All four count rows positive: 50 raw, 49 as printed. Matt McLain's 0-1/1-1 row is +0.041 and prints 0.0. 30 of the all-plus cards also print a no-target sentence.

The plus-count clause opens 81 first lines; 7 of these belong to hitters at 0 or below (Yordan Álvarez −5.6, Byron Buxton −4.8). 69 of the 81 pair it with a 'better than average' framing line, 74 with any good-chooser framing line. 71 of the 81 repeat the line's own opener word for word; the other 10 open 'When you're ahead, mostly against right-handers' and then say 'When you're ahead in the count'.

Reassuring sentences per good-chooser card (plus-count clause, framing line, no-target sentence, fastball-strength clause): 1 on 13 cards, 2 on 34, 3 on 41, 4 on 27. 39 cards carry plus-count clause + framing line + no-target together.

Bregman (+10.9, 18th), whole plan: "With two strikes, mostly against right-handers, let fastballs above the zone go. You swung at 57% of them; hitters on average swing at 51%. ... With two strikes, your choices are a plus overall (+3.0 runs in the count table); this pitch is where they give some back." / "Overall your chase choices are better than average (+10.9 runs a season), and on far-off pitches they cost you nothing net (the 0.0 at the top): the pitch above is one spot to tighten, not a new approach." / Target: "No target: leak 1 was 2 points above the league's chase rate in 2026, and with no change should be about at it in 2027." His By count Two strikes row: chases 40% vs 42%, Choices +3.0.

Trout (+16.1): "When you're ahead in the count, let breaking balls below the zone go. ... When you're ahead in the count, your choices are a plus overall (+0.5 runs in the count table)". The line rests on leak 3, '9 of 16'.

Hand-tab case, Rengifo vs LHP tab: "Overall your chase choices are better than average (+2.6 runs a season): the pitch above is one spot to tighten, not a new approach." The table on the same tab reads "All counts 274 38%29% ... −4.7", and all four count rows are negative there. 9 hand tabs show this; others are Swanson L (−1.2 vs +4.6), Abreu R (−1.1 vs +1.1), Guerrero R (−1.0 vs +1.5), Muncy L, Paredes L, Herrera R, Rumfield L.

Weakest case, Perdomo (+15.7, 2nd): the one line says "You swung at these about as often as other hitters do, but more of yours came at 2-2 and 3-2, and over a season they cost you 1.7 runs", and the Target says "leak 1 was 4 points below the league's chase rate in 2026". The same happens on Mead ("52% vs 51% avg"; target "about at the league's chase rate"), Matt Chapman ("leaks 1 and 2 together were 6 points below"), Okamoto ("7 points below"), McMahon ("3 points below") and Maikel García ("1 points below").

Advice quality: the median first good-chooser line is 5.3 inches off the zone; 61 of 115 are 5 inches or more. Every take line is followed by 'Keep swinging at strikes'. 51 of the 115 plans use at least one leak of 25 pitches or fewer (Kurtz '9 of 23', Trout '9 of 16').
The page text matches the data: all plan item texts for the 115 cards appear verbatim in the rendered right column (0 mismatches).
issues.method: Read BRIEF.md and the plan code in scripts/17_build_player_cards.py (plan_items, strength_clause, framing_line, keep_line, target_text and the per-hand call around line 1067), plus scripts/plan_checks.py (lines 137-161) and leak_rules.py (lines 137-138). Wrote skeptic_goodchooser.py, skeptic_goodchooser2.py and skeptic_goodchooser3.py in the audit folder and ran them on dump_2026.json over all 261 cards and their hand tabs. They count plans by overall Choices, the sign of each count row, the plus-count and framing clauses, word-for-word opener repeats, no-target sentences, rate gaps, leak sizes, hand-tab table totals against the framing line, and whether the rendered text matches. Re-read Bregman, Trout, Kurtz, Perdomo, Mead, Nootbaar, Chapman and Okamoto in full, and the rendered vs LHP tabs of Rengifo and Swanson. All 89 reported cards match the rule; 26 more cards match that no reviewer named (e.g. Seiya Suzuki +13.2, Wyatt Langford +10.1, Bryan Reynolds +9.0, Matt Chapman +8.0).
issues.why_it_matters: For a top-20 chooser, the card's single change is a 1 to 2 run spot wrapped in praise. A coach or player can read it either as noise or as a real problem, and the roster's "Start with" column shows the instruction with none of that context. Three cases go further. On a hand tab the framing line tells a hitter his choices are better than average right above a table showing they cost him runs against that hand (Rengifo −4.7 vs LHP), which undersells the one place he does have a problem. On the 6 "about as often / below the league" cards, the card's only instruction is a pitch the card elsewhere says he does not over-chase.
issues.root_cause: All in scripts/17_build_player_cards.py unless named. The leak rule never looks at overall choices: leak_rules.py:137-138 keeps any cell costing 0.75+ runs with extra chases, and plan_pitch_items (631-641) takes up to 2 of those leaks. plan_items (826-829) always appends strength_clause, and strength_clause (741-751) reopens the line with the count phrase ("With two strikes, your choices are a plus overall"). plan_items (837) adds framing_line (763-782) whenever stored choices > 0. keep_line (797-799) adds the fastball-strength clause, and target_text (988-1002) adds the no-target sentence. On hand tabs, plan_items is called with the overall summary (1067), so framing_line quotes summary["choices"], not that tab's rows["total"]. plan_checks.py:137-141 makes the framing line mandatory with the overall number on every view, and :157-161 makes the count-named plus clause mandatory, so the redundancy is enforced by the checks.
issues.suggested_fix: (1) Say it once. When framing_line fires with c >= 1, drop strength_clause from the first line and fold the count into the frame: "Overall your chase choices are better than average (+10.9 runs a season, +3.0 with two strikes): the pitch above is one spot to tighten, not a new approach." Relax plan_checks.py:157-161 to accept the framing line as the why. If strength_clause stays, stop it reopening the count: "Your choices in this count are a plus overall (+3.0 runs in the count table); this pitch is where they give some back." (2) Hand tabs: pass rows to framing_line and use rows["total"]["choices"] when view != "all" (e.g. "Against left-handers your chase choices cost you 5 runs a season..."), and give plan_checks' good-chooser check the same number. (3) Structural option: when c >= +5 and every count row is a plus (49 cards), or the first leak's rate gap is under 5 points and the target puts the leaks at or below the league (6 cards), open with a fallback-style line ("Nothing to change in your approach: +N runs a season, a plus in every count. One spot to watch: ...") and make the leak a video item, not a numbered take rule.
refuted_items: 'Get take plans' (title): 14 of the 115 are video-only plans that say 'not a take rule'; take plans are 101 (83 at +1 or better).

'a single instruction sits inside three don't-worry sentences': partly. The no-target sentence is in the Target section under the leak list, not in the plan. Inside the plan there are at most three: the plus-count clause, the framing line and the fastball-strength clause. All three sit after the instruction, which still prints first on every card (plan_checks 'frame first' = 0).
'50 cards all four count rows are a plus': true raw; 49 as printed (Matt McLain's 0-1/1-1 row is +0.041 and prints 0.0).

'81 first lines carry the plus-count clause': true, but 7 of them are not good choosers (Yordan Álvarez −5.6, Brayan Rocchio −4.8, Willson Contreras −5.4, Byron Buxton −4.8, Bryce Harper −0.9, Owen Caissie −0.8, Willy Adames −0.4). Among the 115 it is 74.

'73 say the count phrase twice in one line' (finding 444): 71 repeat the opener word for word and all 81 restate the count; the 10 others differ only as 'When you're ahead' vs 'When you're ahead in the count'.

Severity medium (finding 170): not upheld for the pattern. Every reassurance agrees with the table and the instruction survives, so this is wordiness. Only the 9 hand tabs reach medium, because there the framing line disagrees with the tab's own table.
Carlos Cortes (+0.9) 'about average': correct wording for 0 < c < 1 (19 such cards), not an error.

The idea that a good chooser should get no plan at all: not supported as a defect. A +16 hitter can still lose 1-2 runs on one cell, the framing line says exactly that, and the takes are typically 5+ inches off the zone.

issues.statement: Parts 1 and 2 hold, but the reviewers' count is too high, and part 3 is true arithmetic that the page never explains. (1) 65 second plan lines (41 All-pitchers plans, 24 hand tabs, 51 hitters) sit in a different count from line 1, in a count the table prints as a plus, and give no why. 44 of those counts are +1.0 or more (Trout +11.4, Murakami +8.4). On 19 plans (15 hitters), line 1 gets the why for a smaller plus while line 2's bigger plus gets none. The reviewers counted 100, but 35 of those second lines share line 1's count, and line 1's why already covers them. (2) The why calls 23 counts that print +0.1 to +0.4 "a plus overall". 56 of the 155 whys fall under +1.0, where the card's own framing line would say "about average". (3) Leaks costing more than their count's net total is correct net arithmetic, but the page never says the totals are net. 61 hitters on All pitchers have leaks in a count that is not a plus costing more than 1 run beyond that count's net. On 30 All-pitchers plans the plan's lines cost more than the card's whole choices loss.

When you're ahead in the count, your choices are a plus overall (+0.5 runs in the count table); this pitch is where they give some back." then "(2) With two strikes, let changeups and splitters below the zone go. You swung at 53% of them; hitters on average swing at 44%. The ones you swung at were typically 7 inches off the zone." (no why) beside "| Two strikes | 561 | 27% / 42% | ... | +11.4 | −1.1 | productive |"

Murakami, All pitchers: line 1 "When you're ahead in the count, your choices are a plus overall (+0.6 runs in the count table)"; line 2 "(2) With two strikes, let breaking balls below the zone go." (no why) beside "| Two strikes | 467 | 29% / 38% | ... | +8.4 |"

Leak 3 share_rhp 0.9545; on the vs RHP tab the Ahead row's choices are −0.66 and line 1 has no clause.

Walker, All pitchers line 2 (count 'two' +1.01): "With two strikes, mostly against left-handers, breaking balls off the plate inside are one to go over on video with your coaches, not a take rule. ... within a ball of the zone." (no why). On vs LHP, the same pitch is line 1 and ends "With two strikes, your choices are a plus overall (+0.8 runs in the count table); this pitch is where they give some back."

Cronenworth, All pitchers: "At 0-1 or 1-1, your choices are a plus overall (+0.1 runs in the count table); this pitch is where they give some back." beside "| 0-1 or 1-1 | 184 | 32% / 32% | ... | +0.1 |"
