Code vocabulary clash: framing_line uses `level = "better than average" if c >= 1 else "about average"`, but strength_clause fires on `if round(v, 1) <= 0: return None`, so anything printing +0.1 or more is 'a plus overall'.

Lowe, All pitchers: leaks "(1) Two strikes, mostly vs RHP, breaking balls below the zone ... −7.0", "(2) ... −2.0", "(3) ... −1.9" vs "| Two strikes | 337 | ... | −4.7 |"; plan lines (1)+(2) = 9.0 runs vs tile "Choices | −8.8"
McKinstry, All pitchers: two-strike leaks (1) −2.3, (2) −2.0, (3) −1.5 (5.8 runs) vs a Two strikes row of −0.4; Cowser: "(1) Two strikes ... −4.0" vs Two strikes −1.3
Page glossary (countNote): "Choices: what the swing decisions cost." It never says a count's total is net of the spots where he takes more than average.

Sweep (skeptic_pluscount/measure.py over dump_2026.json, all 261 cards × All/vs RHP/vs LHP): later line in a different plus count with no why = 65 (all 41, R 23, L 1; 51 hitters; 44 at ≥ +1.0); same count as line 1 = 35 (all 35 have line 1's why); why on +0.1..+0.4 = 23 (all 7, R 11, L 5); why under +1.0 = 56 of 155; why on the smaller plus while line 2's bigger plus goes unexplained = 19 plans, 15 hitters; leaks in a count that is not a plus costing more than 1 run beyond its net = 120 view-counts (61 hitters on All pitchers); plan lines costing more than the card's total loss (total < 0) = 82 views (30 All-pitchers plans)
issues.method: Read strength_clause (scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:741-751) and plan_items (:812-850); the plus-count check in scripts/plan_checks.py:156-167; the GLOSSARY/countNote text (:1448, :2158); and the 2026-10-17 evaluation README, whose item lists only 'First line in a count ...'. Wrote /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-samsullivan-Desktop-Personal-Projects-Baseball-Chase-Leaderboard/d455bc39-e405-4b67-b2e8-fa1ecc7f61ad/scratchpad/audit/skeptic_pluscount/measure.py (output in skeptic_pluscount/out.json). It goes over all 261 players' plan_items, plan_items_by_hand, tables and leaks for every view. For each check it rounds values the way the page stores and prints them. It splits line-2 cases into 'same count as line 1' and 'different count'. It finds whys on +0.1 to +0.4 and under +1.0. It compares the sum of each count's leaks against the count's net choices, and the plan's leak runs against the total choices loss. I checked each reviewer example against the dossier text (Trout, Murakami, Lowe, Cronenworth, Caissie) and against the dump (Walker, Baty, Lindor, Buxton, Harper).
refuted_items: 35 of the reviewers' 100 'line 2 with no why' cases do not hold. On those, line 2 is in the same count as line 1, and line 1's clause names that count and its runs one line above. Examples: J. P. Crawford (two +8.4), Jonathan Aranda, Dane Myers, Drew Gilbert, Dylan Beavers (All and vs RHP), Freddie Freeman (All and vs RHP), Byron Buxton All, Mike Trout vs RHP, Francisco Lindor vs RHP, J. T. Realmuto vs RHP, Jorge Soler (All and vs RHP), Wade Meckler (All and vs RHP), Yordan Álvarez All. The true count is 41 All-pitchers plans and 24 tabs, not 63 and 37.

Reviewer 462's list includes Crawford, Aranda, Myers, Gilbert, Beavers, Freeman and Buxton for part 1. All seven are same-count cases and are refuted. Lindor holds only on All pitchers (two strikes +0.7, line 1 ahead), not on vs RHP.

Part 3 inside plus counts (237 of the 357 view-counts, e.g. Canzone's −1.7 and −1.4 leaks in a +0.6 two-strike count) is automatic: any negative leak is more negative than a positive net. It is part 1 again, not a separate problem.

The reading 'suggests fixing them would recover more than he loses' is not a misstatement. In the model, fixing both of Lowe's plan leaks would move his choices from −8.8 to about +0.2. No sentence on the card claims a share or a sum, and the spread line, which does talk about shares, fires only when the plan covers under 25% of the loss. Both table and leaks sum the same per-pitch 'choices' (count_table :446, leak_cells in leak_rules.py:134), so there is no baseline mismatch.
Monasterio's +0.5 sits at the boundary. It counts as an overstatement only under a +1.0 threshold, not under +0.5.

Baty's '−0.7 against the hand that throws the pitch' holds in the data. But the clause says 'overall' and quotes the All-pitchers table beside it, so it is literally true. It is the same pattern on 7 All-pitchers whys (Aranda +2.1 vs −0.5 RHP, Muncy +2.5 vs −0.5 LHP, Straw +1.0 vs −1.1 LHP, Bazzana, Adames, Cronenworth, Baty). It is minor and does not need its own finding.
issues.why_it_matters: The clause exists so the table beside a plan line does not argue with it. The project fixed this for 82 first lines on 2026-10-17, and the same contradiction remains on 65 second lines, including the biggest plus counts on the page. A coach reading Trout's or Murakami's card sees the why next to +0.5 or +0.6 and nothing next to +11.4 or +8.4. Meanwhile counts that are essentially even (+0.1, 32% / 32%) get called 'a plus overall', which clashes with the card's own 'about average' wording under 1 run. Part 3 is never wrong, but an analyst who sees one leak cost more than its whole count (Lowe −7.0 vs −4.7), or a plan cost more than the card's whole loss, will suspect a bug, because the glossary never says the totals are net. None of this changes what the player is told to do, so the severity stays low.
issues.root_cause: scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:826-829 (`if items: why = strength_clause(rows, chosen[0][1])`) adds the clause to items[0] only, although strength_clause's own docstring speaks of 'a pitch line'. :747 (`if round(v, 1) <= 0: return None`) fires on anything that prints +0.1 or more, while framing_line (:776) and fallback_line use 1 run as the line between 'about average' and 'better than average'. scripts/plan_checks.py:156-161 checks pitches[0] only, at `shown(v) > 0`, so it enforces exactly this behavior. :1448 GLOSSARY "Choices: what the swing decisions cost." (the page's countNote, :2158) has no word that a count's Choices total is net.
issues.suggested_fix: (1) In plan_items, replace the items[0]-only block with a loop over the pitch items that adds the why to each line whose count is a plus and was not already explained by an earlier line: `explained = set(); for it, (_, lk) in zip(items, chosen): g = lk['count_group']; why = None if g in explained else strength_clause(rows, lk); if why: it['text'] += ' ' + why; explained.add(g)`. In plan_checks.py:156-161, apply the same rule to every pitch line, skipping a line whose count an earlier line's clause already named. The existing 'plus count misquoted' loop already checks every line. (2) Add PLUS_COUNT_MIN_RUNS = 1.0, matching COSTLY_COUNT_RUNS and framing_line's 'better than average' cut, and use it in strength_clause and plan_checks.py:160. Below it, either drop the clause, or word it 'about even overall (+0.2 runs in the count table), and this pitch is where you lose runs'. Combined with (1), the why moves from Trout's +0.5 to his +11.4 and from Murakami's +0.6 to his +8.4. (3) Extend GLOSSARY: 'Choices: what the swing decisions cost, net in each count: spots where you take more than average add runs back, so one leak can cost more than its count's total.'

issues.statement: Two wording problems hold, and both are low severity. (1) Every video line ends "Most of the ones you swung at were within a ball of the zone." That phrase is not the card's own unit. The rule is a median under 4 inches on the same scale the take lines print. 65 of the 93 video lines (47 cards) have a median over 2.94 in. In 5 plans a take printed "typically 4 inches off the zone" sits next to a video item at almost the same distance (Mack vs RHP: 4.02 in vs 3.99 in, both below the zone). The same phrase is in the target sentence (16 cards), the roster's Start with (16 rows) and Peña's coach note. The roster prints "4" inches for 7 top leaks that are video items. (2) All 49 plan views that mix one take and one video item (39 cards) close with "The only changes on this card are the pitches above." Not one says that the staff takes the video item to video first. 19 of them also call both lines "spots to tighten". Parts that do not hold: the claim that "most" from a median means only half; some of the listed cards; and the claim that the sentence is false on all 65 lines. That depends on how "within a ball" is read (see refuted items). The video item quoting a bigger rate gap than the take is by design.
evidence: Joe Mack, vs RHP tab, line 1 (take, median 4.02 in, below the zone): "With two strikes, let changeups and splitters below the zone go. ... The ones you swung at were typically 4 inches off the zone." Line 2 (video, median 3.99 in, below the zone): "With two strikes, breaking balls below the zone are one to go over on video with your coaches, not a take rule. ... Most of the ones you swung at were within a ball of the zone." Then: "the pitches above are spots to tighten, not a new approach." and "Keep swinging at strikes; your fastball decisions are a strength. The only changes on this card are the pitches above."

Other plans with a take and a video item within 0.75 in of each other, same region: Bichette vs RHP 4.24 vs 3.97 (above); Gonzales all 4.11 vs 3.87 (above); McMahon vs RHP 4.19 vs 3.75 (below); C. Walker all 4.19 vs 3.83 (above).

Sweep (skeptic_video/measure.py over dump_2026.json, 783 plan views): 93 video lines on 60 cards; all 93 carry 'within a ball'; median depth 0-2.94 in: 28 lines; 2.94-3.5: 24; 3.5-3.9: 33; 3.9-4.0: 8. Total over 2.94: 65 lines, 47 cards. By region: up 28, down 25, in 10, away 2.

False under any reading (inside/away, where the zone edge already includes the ball's radius): Kirk all 3.30 and vs RHP 3.72, Soderstrom all 3.83, J. Walker all and vs LHP 3.73, Ramos vs RHP 3.69, Chourio vs RHP 3.53, O. Lopez vs RHP 3.49 (away), Vivas all 3.23 (away), Steer all 3.03, Cam Smith all 3.00 and vs RHP 3.01. That is 12 lines on 9 cards.

Mixed plans: 49 views (all 21, vs RHP 26, vs LHP 2) on 39 cards. Every one has the closing "The only changes on this card are the pitches above." None has "video with you first". 19 views (16 cards) add "the pitches above are spots to tighten, not a new approach." Compare a video-only plan: "Nothing on this card is a take rule for you yet: the staff takes the pitches above to video with you first."

Oneil Cruz, all: (1) "let breaking balls below the zone go. You swung at 44% of them; hitters on average swing at 34%." (2) "fastballs above the zone are one to go over on video ... You swung at 67% of them; hitters on average swing at 23%." In 31 of the 49 mixed views (23 cards), the video item's printed gap is bigger than the take's, by 15+ points in 12. In 6 of them the take line quotes no rates at all, e.g. Ohtani all: take "about as often as other hitters" vs video "61% ... 26%".
Grammar: all 93 video lines use '<plural pitches> are one to go over on video', e.g. "fastballs above the zone are one to go over on video with your coaches, not a take rule."

Target, 16 cards: "No number to beat: every leak on this card was mostly within a ball of the zone, one for video, not a take rule." Leaks over 2.94 in on 12 of them, e.g. Jordan Walker (3.73, 2.75, 3.39, all inside), Kirk (3.30 inside), Gilbert (3.92, 3.12), Machado (3.67, 2.14).

Roster: a video top leak prints "Inches off" "4" on 7 rows (Gilbert 3.92, Machado 3.67, Austin Wells 3.83, Langeliers 3.59, Gonzales 3.87, J. Walker 3.73, Lewis 3.81). Gilbert's Start with in the same row: "...not a take rule (about as often as other hitters, but costing 1.4 runs; within a ball of the zone)". Machado's: "(50% vs 32%, within a ball of the zone)".

Peña coach note: "The two-strike slider away and the breaking ball below the zone at 0-1 or 1-1 ... were mostly within a ball of the zone". The leaks are breaking/away 3.57 in and breaking/down 3.90 in.
issues.method: Read pitch_line, framing_line, keep_line, start_with and the target text in scripts/17_build_player_cards.py, the roster depth cell in player_cards.html, and the zone geometry in 02_build_chase_dataset.py. depth_in is the median of distance_outside_zone over the chased pitches (17:484). Wrote skeptic_video/measure.py, measure2.py and verify.py. They cover every plan view (all, R, L) of all 261 hitters in dump_2026.json and map each pitch item to its leak; the printed rates match the leak on all 84 video lines that quote rates. They count the video lines by depth and region, the mixed take+video plans with their closing and frame text, the rate gaps, the target sentences, the roster rows and the coach note. Every reported card was checked one by one, and quotes were confirmed against the rendered card text in the dump's aside.
issues.why_it_matters: The card states take lines in inches ("typically 4 inches off") but video lines in ball widths ("within a ball"). A player or coach then reads near-identical pitches (4.02 vs 3.99 in for Mack) as categorically different, and cannot tell the split is simply under or over 4 inches. In a mixed plan, the closing calls the "not a take rule" line one of his "changes", and nothing says who handles it. That blurs the one distinction the plan works to draw. The main instruction survives in every case, because each video line says "not a take rule" itself. So the severity is low: wording, not a wrong action.
issues.root_cause: The video sentence comes from scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:622-626 (pitch_line's video branch: "are one to go over on video ... Most of the ones you swung at were within a ball of the zone."). The 4-inch cutoff is CLEARLY_OFF_IN at :527-530, whose comment calls it "a ball off the edge". The same phrase recurs in start_with :863-864, the target sentence :982 and coach_notes.py:68 (Peña). The roster cell rounds the median at scripts/templates/player_cards.html:1026 (Math.round(top.depth_in)). The frame verb at :780 uses "look at" only when every chosen item is video, else "tighten". keep_line at :785-797 has a branch only for all-video plans (its docstring says "Every other line is a take"). Any plan with at least one take therefore gets "The only change(s) on this card ... pitch(es) above". The vertical vs horizontal difference comes from 02_build_chase_dataset.py:375-393: the horizontal edge includes the ball's radius (0.83 ft), the vertical edge does not.
issues.suggested_fix: 1) In pitch_line, replace "Most of the ones you swung at were within a ball of the zone." with the card's own unit, e.g. "The ones you swung at were typically under 4 inches off the zone, too close for a take rule." Avoid :.0f here, which prints 3.97 as 4. Use the same wording in start_with ("under 4 in off"), the all-video target sentence ("every leak on this card was typically under 4 inches off the zone") and Peña's coach note. In the roster cell, print "<4" (or one decimal) when depth_in < CLEARLY_OFF_IN. 2) In keep_line, add a mixed branch. Video items always come last, so with one take and one video item it reads: "Keep swinging at strikes. The only take on this card is the first pitch above; the staff takes the second to video with you first." In framing_line, use a neutral verb for mixed plans ("spots to work on"). Add a plan_checks guard: a plan with a video item whose keep line does not mention video. 3) Optional: say "go over <pitches> on video with your coaches; they are not a take rule" instead of "<pitches> are one to go over". Also optional: when the video gap exceeds the take's, add a short reason, e.g. "pitches this close are called strikes too often for a take rule".
refuted_items: 'A median describes half, not most': refuted on its own. If the median is under a cutoff, more than half the pitches are under it. 'Most' only fails because 'a ball' (about 2.9 in) is not the 4-inch cutoff. With 'typically under 4 inches' it would be right.

'False on 65 of 93 lines': it depends on the reading. For above/below leaks (53 of the 65), the stored inches run to the ball's center with no radius (02_build_chase_dataset.py:376-378). Edge to edge, a ball 3.9 in above the zone was about 2.5 in off, which is within a ball. Only 12 lines on 9 cards (inside/away) are false under every reading. The unit mismatch with the take lines holds on all of them either way.

Jared Triolo (2.68 in), Dane Myers (2.72), Paul Goldschmidt (1.47/1.81) and JJ Bleday (1.55) were listed under the 'within a ball' pattern, but their video medians are under 2.94 in, so the sentence holds for them. Myers, Goldschmidt and Bleday belong only under the mixed-closing part; Triolo not at all.
Shea Langeliers and Royce Lewis have no video line on their cards: the plan's two lines are takes, and their video top leak is not on the plan. Only the roster's '4' applies to them.
Jarren Duran (4.06 in, a take) and Braden Montgomery all (4.32, a take) were contrasts, not video lines. As contrasts they are correct.

'Video item quotes the biggest rate gap' (Cruz, Jung): true as printed but by design. Video items are always ordered after takes, and a close pitch can carry a large gap. Jung's vs RHP plan has no take at all. Kept as an optional clause, not a defect.
Medium severity (reviewers 77 and 353): not supported. Every video line says 'not a take rule' itself, so no player is told to take a pitch he shouldn't.
The only-changes closing is not wrong in meaning: 'nothing else changes' still holds. The defect is only that the mixed case never says the staff takes the video item, unlike video-only plans.

issues.statement: Confirmed: the plan sentences and the roster are formatted in Python, and the leak list and By count table are formatted by the page's JavaScript. So a rate or run figure can print one step apart in two places on the same card. This hits 16 of 811 plan rate lines on 15 cards, 6 of 215 roster Start-with lines, 1 productive-line rate (Moreno), and 6 of 94 whole-number run phrases on 4 cards (Gonzales, Acuña, Turner, Arráez). Several of the reported run examples (Arenado's 2 > 2, Mullins, Freeman, and Jung taken alone) are ordinary rounding and do not hold. The cause is also wider than half-to-even: most of the league-rate and run cases come from rounding twice (Python formats the unrounded value, the page formats the stored 4-decimal value).

issues.method: Read BRIEF.md and the formatting code: step 17 rate_gap, rate_clause, runs_phrase, productive_line, fallback_line, contact_why, start_with and the PNG/print leak rows; the template's pct()/runs(); and plan_checks.printed(). issues.why_it_matters: The two numbers for one leak sit a few lines apart, and on 6 cards the roster repeats the plan's number against the card's list. On Caissie, Witt, Conine, Álvarez, Bailey and Goodman this is the default view's first line, and Goodman's printed card disagrees with his web card. No instruction changes and no sentence becomes false, so this is a trust and polish problem: an analyst sees 62 vs 63 or '1 run' under a −1.5 tile and wonders which number is right. plan_checks tolerates it by design, so nothing flags it.
issues.root_cause: Two formatting paths for one value. Python, on the unrounded float with round-half-to-even: scripts/17_build_player_cards.py:593 rate_gap, :603 rate_clause, :654 and :657 productive_line (rates and {contact:.0f}), :580-582 runs_phrase (round()), :706 fallback_line ({choices:+.1f}, ASCII hyphen), :716-717 contact_why, :866 start_with, and the PNG/print leak rows at :1649 and :1897. The page, with Math.round half up on the 4-decimal stored value: scripts/templates/player_cards.html:479 pct() and :481 runs(). Exact fractions (10/16, 15/24, 30/48, 21/40) split on half-to-even vs half-up. Stored values like 0.445, 0.515 and −1.461 split because they are rounded twice. scripts/plan_checks.py:82-87 printed() accepts both neighbors, so the check cannot see it.
issues.suggested_fix: In step 17, add formatters that copy the page and use them for every printed number. pct_txt(v) = math.floor(stored(v)*100 + 0.5), and use it in rate_gap, rate_clause, start_with, productive_line, contact_why and the PNG/print leak rows. runs1(v) = math.floor(stored(v)*10 + 0.5)/10. Have runs_phrase quote the printed one-decimal value ('1.5 runs'), or round that printed value half up, and use it in productive_line in place of {contact:.0f}. Use fmt_runs in fallback_line in place of {choices:+.1f}. Then make plan_checks.printed() return the single page-rounded value (drop the ±5e-5 neighbors) and add a check that whole-run phrases match the table's printed figure.
